report.summary: The release changes how drawings are rendered, positioned, exported, copied, and saved.
keyChanges: The editor now caches rendered drawing elements for on-screen display, while exports keep the unoptimized rendering path; verify drawing appearance at different zoom levels and in exported files.
Scrolling, panning, centering, and export positioning now floor scroll coordinates to whole numbers, so fractional movement can land differently than before.
Copying and saving now omit rendered canvas caches, and saving no longer filters out selection elements.
qaChecks: Verify a line or arrow drawn from bottom-right toward top-left remains fully visible and correctly positioned while panning and changing zoom.
Check a wheel or pan movement that would change the scroll position by 0.25 scene units; confirm the viewport settles at the floored whole-number position and the drawing remains aligned.
Confirm copying and pasting the rendered drawing preserves its visible elements and that the pasted elements remain selectable.
Test saving while a selection is active, then restore the drawing; verify no unintended selection overlay appears.
Verify an export of the drawing includes every element without clipping and preserves their relative positions when the drawing bounds produce a fractional export offset.
uncertainty: Saving now includes selection elements that were previously excluded; confirm whether an active selection is intended to persist after restoring a drawing.

keyChanges: Basic reporter defaults are now merged with supplied options, and its default format inserts the message in place of the previous literal “4$s”.

Fancy entries of type “log” now receive the default icon instead of no icon, and clearing calls a writer that expects a second argument.
Writing now accepts “async” and “sync” modes, with other values using the default stream-writing behavior.

report.summary: The release updates console logging and reporting, so verify that messages are formatted and delivered as expected.
keyChanges: Error logs now pass their error status under a label the writer does not read, so they may be sent to the regular output instead of the error output.

The old logging entry point accepted a boolean asynchronous option, while the new writer selects asynchronous or synchronous handling using the values async or sync; a boolean true now takes the default write path.
A request to clear the console now calls the writer without its required options, so clearing can fail before the log entry is printed.
Reporter options now override defaults directly; previously, supplied options were nested and did not replace settings such as the output stream or time format.

Log output and error output now use shared stream-writing and formatting utilities, so verify messages still reach the intended stream; the exact effect on tag formatting is unclear from the supplied evidence.
A repeated background-color lookup returns the color cache instead of the selected style, putting output that reuses a background color at risk.
Stream writing now supports default writes, synchronous writes, and asynchronous writes that wait for a drain event when the stream signals backpressure.
Formatting utilities now convert named format placeholders to positional arguments and format dates.
Entries of type log now use the configured default icon when no icon is explicitly supplied; previously, this entry type omitted the icon.
Custom icon options are now used for entry types, replacing the built-in icon when an override is provided.
The reporter’s previously exported icon collection is no longer exported; supplied evidence identifies no consumers of it.
qaChecks: Verify an error log is written to the error output destination and not the regular output destination.
Check that a log using the exact mode value true waits for the stream to release backpressure before completing, as the former boolean asynchronous option did.
Confirm that a fancy log requesting a console clear clears the console and prints its log entry without throwing an error.
Verify that configuring a custom output stream and logging a message sends it to that stream instead of the default output stream.
Check that an error message is sent to the configured error stream, while a regular message is sent to the configured output stream.
Verify that selecting the same background color twice still applies the intended background styling to the second output.
Check asynchronous writing when a stream write returns false and later emits drain; confirm completion waits until drain.
Verify an entry of type log with no explicit icon shows the configured default icon; previously, this entry type omitted the icon.
Check a success entry with its icon overridden to X shows X instead of the built-in success icon.
uncertainty: The earlier asynchronous selector is not included, so the evidence cannot establish whether passing true previously guaranteed asynchronous completion, although the new writer recognizes async and sync as its special mode values.

The previous reporter converted colons in tags into namespace separators, but the supplied evidence does not show whether the new formatting preserves that behavior; verify a tag such as service:worker.
No prior implementation or application navigation was supplied, so the old-versus-new input that exposes a regression and the user-facing route for these utilities cannot be established.

No application surfaces or navigation are supplied, and no downstream consumer is identified for the removed exported icon collection, so its compatibility impact and intended test entry point remain unknown.

report.summary: The release makes rotated drawings behave consistently throughout editing, restoration, and export.
keyChanges: Element outlines and their selection handles now follow the element’s angle, and selected elements have a rotation handle; text remains non-resizable but is now checked for rotation-handle interaction.
Scene bounds now include rotated corners, affecting where pasted content is positioned and how rotated content is centered and cropped for export.
Canvas rendering now rotates elements around their center in both optimized and unoptimized drawing paths, so the editor and exported images should show rotated content consistently.
Diagram elements can now be rotated by dragging the rotation handle, with Shift constraining rotation to 22.5-degree increments; resizing a rotated element now follows its rotated orientation.
Text editing now follows the text element’s rotation, and finishing a rotation gesture clears its temporary rotation state.
Restored elements with a missing or null angle now default to 0 radians, and the temporary rotation flag is excluded from saved editor state.
Element hit-testing now accounts for rotation, so clicking rotated shapes and text should target their visible positions rather than their unrotated bounds.
Selected elements have rotation handles, and text editing uses the element’s angle so the editing area follows rotated text; new elements default to an angle of 0.
Resize hints are now shown only for mouse input, and a rotation hint is added while rotating with a mouse.

SVG output now rotates shapes, lines, arrows, and text by each element’s angle around its center; previously, these exported elements were not rotated, so rotated drawings should now retain their intended orientation.

Check that saving and reopening a drawing with a nonzero element angle preserves that angle.

Check that double-clicking text rotated to 90° opens editing aligned to the rotated text, and that submitting the edit preserves the text’s rotation.

report.summary: The release updates how drawings are displayed, navigated, saved, and exported while preserving their content.
keyChanges: On-screen drawing now renders objects from zoom-specific cached canvases; fractional object origins are rounded down to whole canvas units, so their placement can shift by less than one unit.

Scene rendering now reports whether any drawing objects are visible, which the editor uses to track whether the drawing is outside the viewport; rendering also uses scene scroll values instead of separate per-render offsets.
Canvas scrolling and restored centering now use floored positions, so fractional movement or placement is rounded down.
Canvas redraws now enable rendering optimizations, and resizing clears cached shape data before redrawing.
Local saving now includes entries of type “selection”; restored scenes also clear cached rendering data and default missing canvas offsets to 0.
Raster exports now use floored offsets, which can change the padding for drawings whose bounds are fractional.
Copy, undo/redo history, and local saves no longer retain cached canvas data with drawing elements; verify these workflows still preserve the visible drawing.
Canvas-based exports now use floored scroll offsets, so fractional drawing bounds may shift export placement by less than one unit and should not cause artwork to be clipped.

Wheel scrolling, canvas panning, and scrollbar dragging now round each resulting scene offset down to a whole unit, so fractional movement may produce a different viewport position than before. Newly created elements also receive canvas-cache defaults, with no user-visible behavior established by the supplied evidence.
qaChecks: Verify the object at x=10.5 renders from the rounded-down origin x=10 and remains visible at the current zoom.
Check that a drawing with an object in the viewport is treated as having visible content, then pan until all objects are outside the viewport and confirm it is treated as outside.
Confirm the exported drawing includes all objects and text, with the fractional-position object rendered from a rounded-down origin rather than its old fractional origin.
Verify a horizontal wheel delta of 0.25 from scroll position 0 moves the canvas using a floored position of -1, rather than retaining -0.25, and that the drawing remains navigable.
Check that visible drawing elements redraw correctly after resizing the browser window and then scrolling the canvas.
Verify the saved drawing retains its “selection”-type entry after reload and that its ordinary drawing elements remain present.
Confirm the legacy drawing loads with its elements in the expected positions despite missing canvas offsets.
Verify the raster export contains the full drawing and places its left and top bounds 9.5 units from the export origin, reflecting the floored 9-unit offset.
Verify copying a selected, already-rendered shape and pasting it preserves its appearance and editability.
Check cutting a selected, already-rendered shape and then undoing and redoing restores and removes the shape as expected.
Confirm a drawing containing rendered shapes remains intact after allowing it to save and reloading the editor.
Verify a canvas-based export of the drawing with a 10.7 offset keeps all artwork visible and does not clip edge content.
Verify that a vertical wheel input with delta 1 at 150% zoom moves the viewport and leaves its position at a whole scene unit; before this change, that input produced a fractional offset.
Check that a one-screen-pixel canvas pan at 150% zoom still moves the viewport and that the scroll indicators track its position.
Confirm that dragging a scrollbar thumb at 150% zoom continues to move the viewport and that its position is reflected by the scroll indicators.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not say whether rounding fractional object origins is intended, and it provides no navigation or caller details for manually exercising the removed separate-offset input.
The supplied evidence does not identify which drawings may look different with optimized redraw enabled, so its precise visual trigger is unknown.
Fractional scroll and pan movements now round down, but the supplied context does not establish whether this loss of fractional positioning is intended for trackpad input.

report.summary: The release adds direct editing of line and arrow points, with related updates to deletion, finalizing edits, history, and editing hints.
keyChanges: Selecting a single line or arrow for editing now exposes its points for selection, dragging, and Alt-click point insertion; dragging an endpoint can close a loop.
Deleting a selected point updates the line, while finalizing an edit removes lines with fewer than two points or that are invisibly small; point edits are included in undo and redo.
Contextual hints now cover line and arrow editing and display platform-adjusted shortcut text.
qaChecks: Verify that double-clicking a selected line or arrow shows its point handles and that clicking a handle selects it.
Check that dragging an endpoint moves it, and that dragging an endpoint of a looped path to the other endpoint closes the loop.

Test deleting a selected point on a three-point line, then undo and redo; the point should be restored by undo and removed again by redo.
Verify that selecting a line or arrow shows an editing hint, and that selecting a point or clearing the point selection changes the hint to the corresponding point-selection guidance.
uncertainty: When a point list keeps the same length and only its first coordinate changes, the new update check may treat it as unchanged; the supplied evidence does not establish whether a normal editing workflow produces that input or what the visible effect would be.

report.summary: The release expands drawing-editor support for creating and managing groups across selection, editing, copying, and restored drawings.
keyChanges: Selecting elements within a group now selects their group, while selection-box drags also include group members; nested groups are resolved relative to the group being edited.
Grouping within an edited group inserts the new group at that nesting level, and duplication now receives the editing-group context to handle group IDs together.
Clicking empty canvas clears group selection and exits group editing; clicking an element while a group is selected no longer clears that selection when no drag occurred.
Double-clicking an element in a selected group now enters group editing instead of starting text entry; clicking outside that group exits editing without selecting the outside element.

Pasted elements made while editing a group now join that group, and changing to a drawing tool, finishing text editing, or releasing Space with a drawing tool active clears group editing and selection.
Restored elements without group metadata now receive an empty group list, so older drawings can be handled by the group-aware editor.
New canvas elements start with no group membership, while copies of grouped elements receive remapped group IDs so duplicated members can remain grouped without reusing the source group.
Select All now exits group editing and selects groups along with all non-deleted elements; duplication and paste use the active group context when remapping memberships.
Selecting two or more elements and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G groups them; pressing Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+G removes the selected group membership.

A selected group is outlined as a whole rather than giving its grouped elements separate local-selection outlines, and the same group-selection rendering change is used wherever scene rendering is enabled.

The shortcut reference adds Group (Ctrl+G on non-Mac platforms or Cmd+G on Mac) and Ungroup (Ctrl+Shift+G or Cmd+Shift+G); this adds guidance but does not establish that the shortcuts perform those actions.

report.summary: The release improves whiteboard drawing edits and makes them more reliable.
keyChanges: In the drawing editor, line and arrow points can be dragged, points can be added with Alt-click, and dragging an endpoint near the other endpoint closes a path when it has at least three points.

Point updates with the same number of points are now skipped when their coordinates are unchanged; however, a change to only the first point is also skipped, so that point update may not appear or be recorded.

Replacing drawing elements now refreshes the element lookup map and non-deleted list, supporting actions on newly pasted or otherwise replaced elements. The loop-check change only alters a type annotation and has no runtime behavior change.

Pressing Enter or double-clicking with exactly one line, arrow, or freehand drawing selected now enters point-editing mode; its points are shown as handles, and canvas pointer input is routed to point editing instead of ordinary selection or resizing.

Point editing is finalized when its drawing is no longer selected, and its temporary state is omitted from saved editor state; rendering also suppresses ordinary selection outlines while a linear drawing is being edited.
Editing a line or arrow normalizes its first point to the origin while adjusting its position, and point selection and movement account for the drawing’s rotation.

Alt-dragging in point-edit mode previews a new point, releasing Alt removes an uncommitted preview, and Alt-clicking adds or commits a point; releasing a dragged endpoint can close a loop when the path qualifies as closed.
Resize-handle hit testing now takes the pointer’s scene coordinates as separate values; the supplied evidence does not establish a different user-visible resize result.

Selecting one line, arrow, or free-draw element can now show context-sensitive editing guidance; shortcut names in that guidance and other displays no longer translate CtrlOrCmd, Alt, Del, Enter, or Return when the token is embedded within a larger word.

Editing a line or arrow is now included in history: entering or leaving edit mode can create an undo step, while changes that keep the same element being edited do not create a step just because the editor state changed.
Moving or removing a point on a line or arrow now uses the rough-rendered curve bounds to calculate its position, so point edits can affect the element’s placement as well as its points.

The drawing now keeps an ID-based lookup of all elements and provides a separate lookup that returns only elements that are not deleted; line and arrow editing uses the latter. The change making point lists read-only is type-level and has no direct user-visible effect.

Deleting while a line or arrow point is active now removes that point instead of deleting selected drawing objects; the edited element stays in point-editing mode unless it had fewer than two points, in which case it is removed.

Finalizing point editing now exits that mode and removes the element if it has fewer than two points or is invisibly small; Escape can also trigger finalization while point editing is active, including during a drag.
qaChecks: Verify Alt-clicking a segment of a rotated line adds a point at the pointer location, then drag that point and confirm the path updates in the intended location.
Check a line with at least three points by dragging its first or last endpoint close to the opposite endpoint and releasing; confirm the path closes.
Confirm deleting an active point from a line with multiple points removes that point, and deleting the only remaining point removes the line.
Test pasting an element and immediately moving it with an arrow key; confirm the pasted element is visible and moves.
Verify that pressing Enter with exactly one line selected, and separately double-clicking the selected line, displays point handles and enters point-editing mode rather than starting text editing.
Check that moving the pointer over the selected drawing and clicking a point or the line edits its points, while ordinary selection outlines are suppressed during point editing.
Confirm that clicking elsewhere to deselect the edited drawing finalizes editing and returns the canvas to its normal selection state.
Ensure that after entering point-editing mode, saving or leaving the editor and then reopening the drawing restores the drawing without restoring a stale active point-editing state.
Check that the exported drawing retains the line or arrow and does not show point-editing handles or other editing-only selection marks.
Verify that entering point-edit mode for the rotated line or arrow preserves its visible position and that clicking and dragging a point moves the intended point with the drawing.

Test Alt-dragging to create a provisional point, then release Alt; the provisional point should be removed. Alt-click with no provisional point should add a point, and Alt-click with a provisional point should commit it.
Check dragging either endpoint of the prepared loop close to the opposite endpoint and releasing; the endpoints should coincide and the loop should remain closed.
Confirm that dragging a selected shape from a resize handle changes its size in the direction of the pointer movement.
Verify that selecting exactly one line or arrow shows relevant editing guidance, and that selecting multiple elements does not trigger this single-element guidance.
Check the guidance while editing a line or arrow with its first point selected (index 0): confirm whether the displayed tip identifies a point as selected rather than saying no point is selected.
Verify that entering edit mode from the non-editing state creates a history step: undo should restore the non-editing state and redo should restore edit mode.
Check changes made while continuing to edit the same line or arrow; confirm that the change in editing details alone does not add a history step.
Verify moving the first point on the three-point line or arrow updates its position and visible curve without losing the other points.
Check removing a point from the three-point line or arrow updates the visible drawing and leaves the remaining points editable.
Confirm a deleted line or arrow is no longer available for point editing.
Verify that deleting an active point from a line with exactly two points removes that point and leaves the element in point-editing mode.
Check that finalizing a line with exactly one point removes the element and exits point-editing mode.
Confirm that pressing Escape while a line point is being edited and a drag is still active triggers finalization and exits point-editing mode.
uncertainty: A same-length point update that changes only the first point coordinate is ignored by the new comparison, although it was applied before; the supplied context does not identify a manual editor action or named API that produces exactly this input, so its user-visible effect cannot be directly verified from the provided navigation.

The export renderer receives the current editing state, and the new rendering adds point handles for an actively edited line or arrow; whether those handles are intended in exported images is unclear.

The supplied changes add the point-editing implementation and change resize-coordinate arguments, but include no prior implementation to compare; therefore no concrete input proven to take a different old path from the new one, or a changed visible resize outcome, can be established.

The new guidance treats point index 0 as no point selected, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether index 0 represents a selected first point; verify the expected tip. The supplied context also does not identify a visible shortcut string containing one of the changed tokens inside a larger word, so that formatting difference has no confirmed UI test input.

The supplied diff adds the geometry and element lookups but does not include their prior implementations, so it is not possible to identify an exact input that the old behavior handled differently; the checks cover the affected editing and deletion capabilities, but a specific regression-triggering input is unknown.

report.summary: The release reorganizes the whiteboard’s collaboration and scene-loading flows, with the greatest QA focus on live sharing and participant updates.
keyChanges: Live collaboration now handles room creation, joining, scene synchronization, participant presence, and room saving separately from the drawing editor; verify these still work together across two participants.
Starting a collaboration session clears undo history and shares the current non-deleted drawing, so content deleted before the session should not reappear for participants.
Pointer updates now reach the collaboration handler even when a coordinate is invalid; this differs from the previous behavior, which discarded invalid coordinates.
The editor can now initialize from missing scene data without requiring a scene object, while retaining the existing scene-restoration flow.

uncertainty: The previous code discarded invalid pointer coordinates, while the new flow forwards them; verify whether ordinary off-canvas pointer movement can produce such a coordinate and affect the cursor shown to collaborators.

report.summary: The release adds an optional drawing grid that helps align and adjust elements and is remembered in saved scenes.
keyChanges: When grid mode is enabled, the canvas draws a faint grid with 20-unit spacing; grid mode is off by default, and the shortcuts dialog lists Ctrl/Cmd+'.
Saved scene data now includes the grid setting, allowing a drawing saved with the grid enabled to retain that setting when reopened.
New-shape drawing supports equal-side sizing and center-based sizing, while moving a selection positions its shared top-left at the pointer and preserves the elements’ relative offsets.

Text resizing adds a third font-size measurement, scaled down by 1% from the second attempt, so some sizes that previously could not be applied may now fit within the existing less-than-1-pixel tolerance.
Rotation and two-point line or arrow resizing now receive a dedicated discrete-angle setting; verify that modifier-based angle locking remains consistent across these operations.
Grid mode can be toggled from the empty-canvas context menu or with a Ctrl/Cmd keyboard shortcut, and it snaps most new elements to grid points while leaving freehand drawing unsnapped.
With grid mode on, moving or resizing elements follows grid points, and arrow-key nudges move by one grid spacing normally or by the regular translation step with Shift held.
qaChecks: Verify the shortcuts dialog lists Ctrl/Cmd+' for grid mode.
Check that a drawing with grid mode enabled remains gridded at 20-unit spacing after saving and reopening it.

Check drawing a shape with equal-side sizing enabled and confirm its sides remain equal; repeat with center-based sizing enabled and confirm it grows around its starting point.

Test resizing text with a narrow target size where the first two font-size attempts do not fit but a further 1%-smaller size would fit within less than 1 pixel; confirm the resize succeeds and the text remains within the target bounds.
Confirm that rotating an element and resizing a line or arrow with discrete-angle locking enabled produces locked angles, and that disabling the setting allows unrestricted angles.
Verify that toggling grid mode from the empty-canvas context menu turns snapping on, and toggling it again turns snapping off.

Check grid placement by creating a shape one quarter of a grid spacing beyond an intersection; confirm it lands on the intersection, then draw a freehand stroke and confirm its path remains unsnapped.
Confirm that, with grid mode on, dragging a selected element from an off-grid grab point and resizing it toward a position between grid points results in grid-aligned movement and resizing.

Verify that pressing Ctrl/Cmd with the keyboard key mapped to 222 toggles grid mode; then select an element and press an arrow key once to confirm it moves one grid spacing, while Shift+arrow uses the regular translation step.
uncertainty: The evidence confirms the shortcut is listed but does not establish that pressing it toggles grid mode.

The supplied evidence does not include the previous implementations of the moved drawing helpers or the mapping from keyboard input to the new discrete-angle setting, so it does not establish a concrete before-versus-after input for those changes; it also does not identify an exact text string and target size that reaches the new third-measurement case.
The supplied evidence does not identify the visible key label for the Ctrl/Cmd grid shortcut.

report.summary: The release overhauls live collaboration and editor integration to make shared drawings easier to set up, synchronize, and restore.
keyChanges: A new participant previously triggered a full initial scene broadcast; that explicit send is removed, so verify joining participants still receive the existing drawing.
Collaboration updates now use AES-GCM encryption with a newly generated 12-byte initialization value, and shared-scene loading handles encrypted data as well as legacy JSON.
Collaboration links are now recognized only when their URL hash exactly matches the room-and-key format, with letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens in each value.
Scene restoration now accepts null data and restores an empty scene with default settings instead of trying to read fields from missing data.
Drawing and collaboration setup now runs through the collaboration-aware editor wrapper, which handles saved drawings and incoming share links before supplying the scene to the editor.
Scene changes now reach live collaboration through the editor’s change callback, and pointer updates are passed to collaboration even during gestures with multiple active pointers.
The embeddable editor now defaults omitted dimensions to the browser window and exposes readiness, history, scrolling, and scene-reading controls through its editor reference.
Scene updates can omit drawing elements, include collaborator state, and request history recording; an initial-data promise that rejects is caught and the editor continues with an empty scene.
External drawings and collaboration links are initialized through the app’s scene-loading flow; an empty local drawing forces the link to load without an override prompt.
A collaboration link for the same room as one unloaded less than 15 seconds earlier also bypasses the override prompt; other non-empty local drawings still require confirmation.
Drawing changes are saved locally and broadcast during live collaboration, while joining a collaboration room loads its saved drawing or falls back to the live session.

The editor replaces its directly rendered room dialog with an optional collaboration button that invokes an action supplied by the host; when shown, it displays a collaborator count only when the count is greater than 0.

Collaboration cursor updates no longer include selected-element IDs, while the prior automatic scene-load shortcuts for an empty scene and reopening the same room within 15 seconds are removed; verify the resulting collaboration experience and load flow.

The main editor no longer contains its previous collaboration startup, remote-scene update, sharing, and unsaved-exit handling; verify that collaboration links, synchronized drawings, and unsaved changes still work.
The embeddable editor contract now allows optional dimensions and null or promise-based initial data, and exposes a readiness promise and status for its public API.
Flushing a debounced action before it has ever been called now does nothing instead of invoking it without saved arguments.

When two versions of the same drawing object have the same edit version but different tie-break values, collaboration now keeps one version instead of potentially dropping the object; verify that the drawing retains the selected version on both participants.
Scene updates now pass the syncable drawing snapshot from the collaboration caller, with full resyncs updating the tracked scene version; verify participants stay in sync during a live session.

Live pointer updates now take selected-element state from the editor, falling back to an empty selection when that state is unavailable, so collaboration should transmit the editor’s current selection.
The embeddable editor now forwards an editor ref and collaboration and pointer callbacks; an omitted collaboration-button callback defaults to a no-op.
Creating a room clears drawing history before sharing the current scene, while incoming collaborator changes update the drawing and clear undo history.
Drawing changes are broadcast when the scene version advances, and pointer updates are sent only when fewer than two pointers are active.
The collaboration dialog supports creating and ending a session, copying its link, and saving a changed username; ending a session saves the room and removes its room link from the address.
qaChecks: Verify that when the second participant joins, the existing drawing appears for them and subsequent scene changes synchronize between both participants.

Check that a collaboration link whose hash is exactly #room=abc_123,xyz-789 opens the session, while a hash with an added suffix such as #room=abc_123,xyz-789&extra=1 is not treated as a matching collaboration link.
Verify that starting with no saved scene data opens a usable blank drawing with default settings instead of failing during restoration.
Verify that reopening the app restores the saved drawing and that opening a share or collaboration link loads the linked drawing or session.
Check that one participant creates a drawing change and the other participant sees the synchronized scene change.
Test a two-pointer gesture while collaborating and confirm the other participant continues to see the participant’s pointer without invalid jumps.
Confirm that after one participant closes or reloads the tab, the other participant sees the session presence update and can continue collaborating.
Verify that an embed with width and height omitted uses the browser window dimensions and becomes ready through its editor reference.
Check that an update containing only a new background color and no elements changes the background while leaving the drawing intact.
Test a rejected initial-data promise and confirm the editor finishes loading with an empty scene rather than remaining stuck.
Verify that opening an external drawing or collaboration link with no elements in local storage loads the linked scene without showing the override prompt.
Check that reopening the same collaboration room 14,999 milliseconds after unloading it loads without the override prompt.
Confirm that opening a collaboration link with a non-empty local drawing and no recent same-room unload asks for confirmation before loading the linked scene.
Verify that a drawing change made by one participant appears for the other participant.
Check that joining a room displays its saved drawing when available, and that participants’ live scene synchronizes when no saved drawing is returned.
Verify the collaboration button is shown when the host supplies the collaboration action, is absent when it does not, and invokes the supplied action when clicked.
Check the collaborator count with 0 and 2 collaborators: no numeric count should appear at 0, and 2 should appear at 2; check desktop and mobile layouts.
Test selecting an element and moving the pointer in one session; confirm the other session still receives the collaborator's cursor update.

Confirm the intended load behavior for the exact prior edge cases: reopening the same room within 15 seconds and loading a collaboration link into an empty drawing. Previously, both cases could load without prompting; the new expected behavior is not established by the supplied evidence.

Verify that creating a shared session after drawing and deleting an element does not expose that deleted element to the other participant; the previous sharing flow removed deleted elements before sharing.
Check that a participant joining through a collaboration link receives the drawing and that a drawing change made by one participant appears for the other.
Confirm that attempting to leave while a collaboration change is unsaved shows the browser's leave warning, and that choosing to stay preserves the drawing.

Verify a conflict where both copies of the same object have the same edit version but different tie-break values leaves one version visible in the drawing rather than removing the object, and that both participants converge on that version.
Verify that with one element selected, moving a participant’s pointer sends the current selection state and the other participant sees the corresponding collaboration update.
Check that starting a session produces a collaboration link and that another participant can use it to join the shared session.
Verify that after deleting an element and starting a room, a second participant joining from the copied room link sees the current drawing but not the deleted element.
Check that a drawing change from either participant appears in the other participant's scene, and that receiving a remote change clears the receiver's undo history.
Confirm that pointer presence updates during a one-pointer interaction and is not broadcast during an interaction with two active pointers.

Test copying the room link, changing the username, and ending the session; verify the link can be used to join, the username remains available after reopening, and ending clears the room link from the address.
Verify that a promise resolving to drawing data loads that drawing, and that the API readiness promise resolves with the ready status before API methods are used.
Check that the editor can be initialized without explicit width or height, and with null initial data.
Confirm that the supplied editor ref reaches the editor and provides the integration’s expected editor access.
Verify that supplied collaboration-button and pointer callbacks are forwarded and respond to their corresponding editor events.
Verify that flushing before any save has been scheduled does not invoke the save action or produce an error; the previous behavior attempted to invoke it with no saved arguments.
uncertainty: The prior new-participant event explicitly sent the full scene, but the replacement behavior is not shown here; confirm that participants still receive the existing drawing on join, since missing initialization could leave them without it.

The supplied evidence shows that unloading no longer explicitly destroys the collaboration connection, but does not establish how the new wrapper handles connection cleanup; verify that other participants see a user leave after the tab is closed or reloaded.

The supplied changes do not include the prior implementation of the newly added scene-loading flow, so they do not establish whether the automatic no-prompt cases are new or confirm how those cases behaved before.

The supplied changes remove the previous in-editor room creation, room destruction, and username-change handlers, as well as the old unload-save helper and automatic load shortcuts, but do not show whether replacement flows preserve them; confirm the intended behavior for room management, leaving a session, and the two load edge cases.

The previous collaboration lifecycle and safety steps were removed from the main editor, but this evidence does not establish their replacement or new location; whether deleted-element cleanup and unsaved-change protection remain is unresolved.
The supplied context does not describe how to start or join a session, and it may be difficult to manually create the precise same-version conflict needed to reproduce the main regression.

The supplied evidence has no before-code for the collaboration-link generator or the embeddable editor’s prior public contract, so it does not establish whether their generated link format or removed username-change callback behavior is intentionally changing.
The supplied changes contain no removed code, so the previous behavior and an exact input that followed a different old path cannot be established; navigation details were also not supplied.

report.summary: The release makes drawing and scene restoration better match the editor’s visible view.
keyChanges: Canvas coordinate mapping now accounts for horizontal and vertical viewport offsets as well as scroll and zoom, which can change where pointer-driven actions land when the view is offset.
Text editing now positions its on-screen editor using the viewport offsets, affecting text placement and alignment while editing.

The editor now measures its position in its parent before loading a scene and refreshes that position when its supplied width or height changes, so canvas placement and coordinate handling should stay aligned in embedded or repositioned layouts.

Loading a scene now recalculates its scroll position, and dropping an Excalidraw drawing uses the current editor state when restoring it; drawings that were previously outside the visible area should be brought into the current view. Restoration no longer accepts the earlier optional request to center content.

Importing a drawing file through the editor now uses the current view to position the restored scene; when the scene lies outside that view, positioning is based on its closest element rather than requesting scroll-to-content.
Shared-scene imports no longer request automatic scrolling to the imported content, so the restored view state can determine what is initially in view.
Saved and exported drawing data now excludes top and left viewport offsets, while Node canvas exports explicitly use zero for both offsets.
qaChecks: Verify that, with those offsets and zoom, clicking directly on the visible center of the shape selects it and starting text there places the new text at the shape center rather than a displaced point.
Check that editing the existing text in the same state keeps the on-screen editor aligned with the text, and that typing and submitting leaves the text at its original drawing position.
Verify a drawing with elements outside the current viewport is dropped onto the canvas; confirm the drawing is restored and its content is brought into the current view.

Check an embedded editor whose parent begins at nonzero top and left offsets, then change the supplied editor width or height; confirm the canvas remains aligned with the editor’s parent after the size change.
Confirm a saved drawing with content outside its saved view loads into the editor with the content brought into view.
Verify importing the drawing file while its entire scene is outside the current view brings the closest element toward the center of the editor view.
Confirm importing the shared scene uses its restored view state rather than forcing the viewport to scroll to the content.
Verify saved drawing data with top and left viewport offsets of 12 and 8 omits both values while retaining the drawing content.
Confirm a Node canvas export completes when both viewport offsets are set to 0.
uncertainty: The intended relationship between viewport offsets and zoom is not documented, and the forward and reverse canvas mappings apply offsets differently; confirm that clicks and text placement remain aligned when offsets are nonzero.

The earlier restoration option could explicitly request content centering, but the supplied evidence does not establish which user flows relied on it; confirm that saved-drawing and other restoration flows still bring off-screen content into view.
The supplied context gives no navigation steps or affected surface IDs, and does not establish the exact visible viewport result when a shared scene’s saved view differs from its content.

report.summary: The release improves how drawing elements connect and behave during canvas editing.
keyChanges: Canvas hit detection now uses element geometry and rotation to identify objects for selection, text editing, and context menus.

Arrow connections now support rectangle, diamond, ellipse, and text elements; connection updates cover moving or resizing connected elements and removing a connection without dropping a remaining link to the same shape.
Canvas hit testing now uses shape-relative distance checks with a 10-pixel-at-100%-zoom tolerance; this changes how clicks near shapes, text, and lines are recognized.

Arrow binding and its suggested highlight use a shape-size-based boundary: at least 15 pixels, at most 80 pixels, with diamond dimensions adjusted to align with rectangles; binding focus and gap are calculated for rectangles, text, diamonds, and ellipses.
Suggested arrow bindings now show a faint shape-boundary or endpoint highlight, and linear-point and rotation handles are drawn as filled circles.

New geometry operations underpin pointer hit-testing, shape transforms, line intersections, and arrow-to-shape connections, so verify that selecting and manipulating drawings and maintaining connections still work.
Arrows can suggest and form connections to shapes while being drawn or edited; holding Ctrl or Cmd disables binding, and changing tools can complete a connection at the arrow’s last point.
Pasting or inserting a copy now repairs connections between copied elements so an arrow can connect to its copied shape rather than the original.
Submitting an empty text edit removes the text and repairs connections that referred to it; canvas picking for selection, text editing, and context menus also uses a shared hit-testing path.
Arrows can connect to shapes, and their endpoints are recalculated when connected shapes move or resize; simple two-point arrows cannot connect both ends to the same shape.
The diamond-coordinate edit has no visible effect because the old and new left-edge coordinates are both zero.
Drawing or editing a line or arrow can suggest and commit connections to shapes at its endpoints, including when an endpoint is moved over a shape.
Moving, resizing, or rotating connected elements now updates their connections; deleting a connected shape or line endpoint clears the affected connection.

report.summary: The release improves how text attached to shapes is displayed and handled throughout the drawing editor.
keyChanges: Text attached to a shape now wraps to the shape’s available width, and the shape can grow or shrink as the text changes; font and size changes also recalculate the text layout.
When finding a shape for text editing, existing text is ignored as a hit target so text inside a shape can be edited without treating that text as its own container.
Text editing can now reuse or create text attached to a shape, including when editing at the shape center; verify the text remains positioned within its shape.
Duplicating a shape with attached text now preserves the attachment on the copy, while attached text is excluded from ordinary hit-testing and marquee selection.
Text editor positioning now uses viewport coordinates directly, so editing with the canvas offset from the page should still place the editor over the text.
Resizing a shape with attached text now recalculates the text’s wrapping, position, and height, including when multiple elements are resized together.
A shape with attached text cannot be resized to negative dimensions, and its width must remain above the estimated minimum needed for a line of text.
Rotating a shape also rotates and repositions its attached text; adding text to a shape that is too small increases the shape to estimated minimum text dimensions.
Text wrapping now accounts for the available shape width and breaks overlong words across lines when needed.
Editing text attached to a shape now measures it within its current width and can expand the shape when the text exceeds its available space.
Copying a selected shape now includes its attached text, so both should be present when the copied drawing content is pasted.
Interior dragging now treats transparent fills differently: transparent shapes with attached text can be dragged from inside, while transparent shapes without attached text cannot.
Text already attached to a container is no longer eligible as a binding element, while standalone text remains eligible; this can affect arrow connections to text.
Selecting one rectangle, diamond, ellipse, or image now shows contextual guidance about binding text to it.
Text width measurement now uses canvas measurements and cached character widths, which may affect wrapping and the sizing of text attached to containers.
Clicking a shape to add text now targets its center, while starting text entry with one shape selected requests text binding; verify both ways of adding text to a shape.
Pasting, inserting from the Library, or drag-duplicating content now reconnects copied text to its copied shape; dragging an ungrouped shape also moves its attached text.

When adding selected content to the Library or exporting a selection, attached text is now included with its selected shape; pasted content selection also changes to include only standalone text elements.
Imported text missing attachment or original-text data now receives defaults of no attached shape and an empty original-text value.

Attached text now uses approximate font line height instead of dividing its total height evenly across its lines; unbound text keeps the previous spacing calculation, and attached-text spacing may look different on the canvas and in image exports.
When a shape is selected, its attached text is now included for grouping, Library additions, and PNG or SVG clipboard copies; verify those operations include both the shape and its text.
Deleting a selected shape now also deletes text attached to it, while duplicating the shape creates a copy with its text still attached.
Select All no longer selects text attached to a shape as a separate element; it selects the shape without independently selecting its attached text.

report.summary: The release makes attached text placement and overflow behavior more consistent across editing and export.
keyChanges: When a container is resized, bound text now aligns to its chosen vertical position: top or bottom with 5 px of padding, or centered for middle alignment; the editing overlay also follows that alignment instead of always centering. This changes the position of existing top-aligned text and adds bottom-aligned placement.

Editing existing text no longer resets its vertical alignment when it is not center-snapped or its text alignment is not centered; bottom-aligned text is now drawn using the container’s bottom padding in the editor and exports.

report.summary: The release lets users add and use links on drawing elements through new editor controls and canvas interactions.

The hyperlink popup starts hidden and is dismissed when the context menu opens or the active tool changes from selection.

Submitting a link trims surrounding spaces and adds https:// when a non-empty value has no protocol and does not begin with a slash or the pattern’s other excluded prefix; submitting an empty value leaves the element without a link.
The link popup supports editing and removal, appears above the element, and can close after the pointer moves outside the element and popup areas.
Links beginning with a slash or containing the current site address open in the current tab; other links open in a new tab, with link-icon hit detection adjusted for canvas zoom.

Selecting exactly one linked element now shows its hyperlink information popup, including after a selection drag that selects exactly one linked element; clicking the link icon is handled separately from normal element selection.

report.summary: The release makes drawing-editor interactions with lines and arrows clearer and more consistent.
keyChanges: When one unlocked line or arrow is selected for point editing, its point handles are shown instead of standard resize and rotation handles; hovering a point also highlights it.
Point handles now use purple styling, and handles are larger while editing points; a fresh or restored editor state starts with no linear element selected.

Point editing now follows a selected line or arrow even when it is not already in edit mode; selecting exactly one linear element can enable point handles, and releasing a dragged endpoint can update its shape connection.
Selecting a line or arrow through the context menu now also prepares it for point editing, while selecting multiple elements clears the single-element handles.

When a selected line or arrow is in point-editing mode, clicks in empty space inside its bounding rectangle no longer count as hits on the line; stale point-editing state is cleared when its element is no longer selected.
Finishing a multi-point line or arrow now leaves that element selected for point editing, and selecting only one line or arrow with Select All also opens point editing.
Point handles are reduced from 20 to 10 units, while the point-hit threshold remains 11 screen pixels; point selection and dragging now use the selected line or arrow editor state.
Locking selected elements now clears line or arrow point-editing state.

report.summary: The release improves file importing and loading across the editor and its embedded example.
keyChanges: File reading now has a fallback for browsers that lack the standard Blob reading capability, supporting image hashing, encryption, and PNG metadata operations.
Files with no declared type are now recognized by the exact lowercase .excalidraw and .excalidrawlib suffixes, while supported images can be identified or corrected using their contents.
When a dropped file supplies a native file handle, loading now passes it into scene restoration, with an explicitly supplied handle taking precedence.

Opening a file now normalizes its type before import, allowing image bytes to be recognized when the file has no MIME type or an incorrect supported-image type; this can let a PNG containing drawing data load where it was previously treated as text.

The embeddable editor example adds file loading for drawings and libraries, and the package now exposes the shared scene-or-library file loader. The example forwards parsed file data to the editor’s scene update.

Dropped files are now classified by their contents rather than the .excalidrawlib filename suffix or MIME type, so valid drawings and reusable-item collections can be handled according to their actual data.
Dropped, file-launched, and shared files now pass through the same normalized import handling, which can load either a drawing or a reusable-item collection.

report.summary: The release centralizes how selected drawing objects are retrieved across editing actions and canvas interactions.
keyChanges: Selection-dependent editing—such as aligning, distributing, grouping, copying, and editing frames or attached text—now obtains selections through the drawing scene, which also caches repeated selection lookups; verify that selected objects and their associated contents remain consistent across these actions.

Some canvas interactions previously looked up selections using a collection that included deleted objects, while the new lookup uses the current non-deleted scene; the practical effect for a user-created selection is not established.
qaChecks: Verify selecting multiple shapes and aligning or distributing them updates the intended shapes, and that grouping and ungrouping still act on the selection.
Check that copying selected shapes with attached text or frame contents includes the expected associated objects.
Confirm selecting one frame allows selecting its contents and removing all contents from the frame, without affecting unrelated objects.
Test selecting, dragging, resizing, and editing text or line points; confirm the visible selection and resulting edits apply to the intended non-deleted objects.

Check the changed edge case where a selected-object ID refers to a deleted object, if that state can be reached through normal editor use; confirm deleted objects are not acted on as current selections.
uncertainty: The changes consistently move selection lookups to the current non-deleted scene, but the supplied evidence does not establish a normal user action that produces a selected deleted object; whether that old-versus-new difference is user-reachable remains unclear.

report.summary: The release makes line and arrow editing more accurate and responsive, including for curves and shared changes.
keyChanges: Editing a multi-point line or arrow now exposes midpoint controls for its individual segments, and clicking a control inserts a point into that segment instead of at one overall midpoint.

For round lines and arrows with more than two points, midpoint placement and the short-segment threshold are based on the curved path; outside point-editing mode, midpoint controls are limited to elements with exactly two points.
The edited line or arrow’s point handles are now rendered from the visible drawing element during scene rendering, supporting alignment during live collaboration.

Rounded lines with more than two points now use their rendered curve to locate segment midpoints halfway by curve length and to measure segment length, affecting where editing handles appear and how short segments are treated.
Other lines continue to use straight-line midpoints and endpoint distances; point equality now requires both coordinates to match exactly.

Midpoint hover and insertion now target individual line segments, including curve-aware positions; previously the control used the line’s endpoint midpoint and was unavailable for lines with three or more points.
Pointer movement now reads the active editing state and returns without an edit result when no line is being edited. Navigation was not found in code.
qaChecks: Verify that a three-point line or arrow outside point-editing mode shows no midpoint controls, then enter point-editing mode and confirm each eligible segment has its own control.

Check a three-point line or arrow by clicking the midpoint of its second segment, away from the overall drawing midpoint; confirm a new point is inserted on that second segment and the other points remain in order.

Confirm that a round multi-point line or arrow’s midpoint control follows the curved segment, and that a segment whose curve length multiplied by zoom is below four point-handle sizes has no control while one at or above that threshold does.
Test editing a line or arrow during live collaboration while scene changes are synchronized; confirm its visible point handles stay aligned with the drawing.
Verify the curved two-point line’s midpoint control appears on the curve rather than at the midpoint between its endpoints, and that clicking the control inserts a point on that segment.
Check the three-point line and confirm each segment has its own midpoint control and that using one inserts a point on the chosen segment.
Confirm that moving the pointer over the canvas when no line is being edited leaves the drawing unchanged and the canvas usable.
Verify the segment midpoint handle for the curved line is positioned halfway along the visible curve, rather than at the straight midpoint between its endpoints.
Check that hovering over and selecting the curved segment's midpoint handle works at its displayed position.
uncertainty: The supplied changes add the curve calculations without showing the previous implementations, so the exact input that behaved differently before this change cannot be confirmed.

report.summary: The editor gains a hand tool for panning, with related updates to tool switching and shortcut guidance.
keyChanges: A hand tool is added to the desktop and mobile toolbars and the shortcut help; pressing H or choosing the tool activates panning, clears the current selection, and toggling it off returns to the previous tool or selection.
While the hand tool is active, canvas pointer gestures pan instead of creating or selecting drawing elements, and the cursor changes to a grab cursor.
Leaving the eraser now restores the tool recorded as the last active tool, rather than using the eraser-specific previous-tool value. Single-letter shortcuts in help are shown in uppercase.
qaChecks: Verify that pressing H or choosing the hand tool clears the selection, shows the grab cursor, and allows a canvas drag to pan without creating or selecting an element; toggle the tool off and confirm the previous tool returns.
Check the changed cursor path with Space held while activating the hand tool: confirm the cursor is grab and a canvas drag pans rather than drawing.
Confirm that the shortcut help includes the hand tool’s H shortcut and displays single-letter shortcuts in uppercase.
Test entering the eraser from a non-selection tool and then leaving it; confirm the previously active tool is restored.
uncertainty: The supplied evidence does not establish how older saved scenes populate the previous-tool value, so it is unclear whether eraser exit behaves differently for scenes saved before this change.

report.summary: Editing actions now consistently use the current drawing’s selection, with changes focused on selection-based operations.
keyChanges: Canvas interactions and selection-based editing now retrieve selected objects through the drawing scene, with explicit inclusion of frame contents and attached text retained where those options are requested.

Frame membership updates after selection operations, including alignment, distribution, and flipping, now resolve the selection against the supplied drawing elements. The diff does not establish a broader change to how these actions should behave.
Horizontal and vertical flips now pass the editor instance into frame-membership updates, allowing the update to use the current drawing selection.
Adding items to the Library now reads selected items from the current drawing scene, while continuing to include bound text and frame contents and to reject selections containing images.

The two selection-based zoom actions and contextual editing hints now get selected objects from the current scene instead of the element list passed to them, so verify zoom framing and selection hints remain appropriate.
Connector editing actions, context-menu labels, and keyboard selection handling now retrieve selected elements through the drawing scene while retaining the same stated selection options.
Pasted or inserted drawing items now pass editor context to selection handling; this supports selection processing after clipboard, library, and drop insertion.
The six alignment controls now check the editor scene’s selection; alignment remains available only for more than one selected non-frame object, so verify their availability and alignment results.

Lock availability, its context-menu label and shortcut, and the objects changed by locking now read the selection from the editor scene, retaining the existing handling of attached text and objects inside frames.

The six alignment operations now select objects from the editor’s current scene and pass the editor through frame-membership updates, so verify edge and center alignment also leaves selected objects correctly associated with their frames.
Copy, cut, text copying, and PNG/SVG clipboard exports now obtain selection from the current scene; attached text remains included, and object copying and image exports also include frame contents.

Grouping, ungrouping, and horizontal or vertical spacing now use the scene’s selected-object lookup; the visible selection criteria and spacing directions are otherwise unchanged in the supplied evidence.
Binding, unbinding, and wrapping text in a container now use the current scene’s selected elements; their existing selection requirements and resulting drawing changes are otherwise unchanged.
Selecting all elements in a frame and removing elements from a frame now use the current scene’s selection to determine whether one frame is selected and which frame to act on.
qaChecks: Verify selecting multiple objects and dragging them moves the selected objects together, and that double-clicking a selected line or arrow still enters its editing interaction.
Check a selection containing frame contents and attached text, then duplicate it; confirm the selected frame contents and attached text are handled with the selection rather than omitted.
Confirm that aligning, distributing, or flipping selected objects updates their frame contents appropriately and does not unexpectedly remove objects from their frames.
Test a specially prepared drawing with a deleted object whose ID remains selected, then drag-duplicate the selection; confirm deleted content stays absent while live selected objects are duplicated.
Verify that flipping a selected element inside a frame horizontally and vertically completes and updates its frame membership appropriately.
Verify the selected text object is framed when using each selection-based zoom action, and that the contextual hint reflects a selected text object.
Verify that with exactly one selected line or arrow, its context menu offers connector-point editing, entering that mode allows point editing, and invoking it again exits the mode.
Check keyboard movement and arrow-key binding behavior with a selected connector and confirm the selected drawing elements continue to respond.
Confirm that pasted or inserted multi-element content appears in the drawing and remains selected for continued editing.
Verify that selecting two non-frame objects makes the alignment controls available and that each alignment option lines the objects up by its corresponding edge or center.
Check that selecting a frame along with another object does not make alignment controls available.
Verify that locking a selection that includes attached text or frame contents locks the selected objects and that toggling again unlocks them.
Confirm that Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+L toggles locking for a non-empty selection and that the context-menu label reflects whether the selection will be locked or unlocked.
Verify each edge and center alignment operation lines up the selected objects at the requested edge or center.
Check that aligning selected objects associated with a frame leaves their frame association consistent.
Verify copying or cutting the selection includes attached text and objects inside the frame.
Check PNG and SVG clipboard exports of a non-empty selection include its attached text and frame contents.
Confirm copying selected text places the text contents on the system clipboard, with two selected text objects separated by a blank line.
Verify that selecting two non-frame objects and distributing them horizontally spaces them along the horizontal axis, and distributing them vertically spaces them along the vertical axis.
Check that grouping two selected objects treats them as a group, and ungrouping that selection removes the group while leaving the objects in the drawing.
Confirm that grouping a selected shape with its attached text keeps the text associated with the shape.
Verify selecting one text item and one unbound container allows binding and leaves the text attached to the container.
Check that selecting a container with bound text and unbinding it leaves the text separate from the container.
Confirm wrapping a selected text item creates a rectangle around it with the text attached.
Verify selecting all elements in the frame selects its contents, excluding text that is attached to another element.
Check that removing all elements from the selected frame removes its contents and leaves the frame selected.
uncertainty: The clearest old-versus-new input difference is that one drag-duplication path previously resolved selection from a list that could include deleted objects and now resolves it from non-deleted scene objects; whether a stale selection of a deleted object can occur in normal use is not established by the supplied evidence.

The Library action now reads selection from the current scene instead of its supplied element list, but the evidence does not identify a real user input where those lists differ, so a regression-specific check for that change cannot be specified.

The evidence does not establish an input that the previous element-list lookup handled differently from the current-scene lookup, so the check covers expected selection behavior rather than a confirmed regression-triggering case.

The supplied changes show selection retrieval being redirected through the scene, but do not establish a concrete input that the old behavior handled differently; the checks are focused on confirming the affected editor workflows remain usable.

The evidence does not identify a concrete user input where the objects supplied to an action differ from the editor scene’s current objects, so it is unclear which input would expose a behavioral regression from changing the selection source.

The old and new selection sources differ when the action’s supplied drawing objects do not match the editor’s current scene, but the supplied context does not establish a way for manual QA to produce that condition.

The old and new selection lookups use different sources, but the supplied evidence establishes no concrete user-produced input where those sources differ; a specific regression-triggering input could not be identified.

The supplied evidence does not identify a concrete user input that produces different results before and after the change; the difference is which source supplies the selected elements, and the expected relationship between that source and the current scene is not documented.

report.summary: This release changes how drawing updates are recorded for undo and redo, including updates from scene loading and live collaboration.
keyChanges: Drawing updates now distinguish captured changes, which create history increments, from snapshot-only updates; scene synchronization, image updates, and collaboration updates are explicitly marked as snapshot-only.

Before this change, an update with elements or app state was captured even when the old commit option was false; now an update with no store action does not update the history snapshot, so scene loading and integrations that omit the new option need focused checks.
qaChecks: Verify an integration sends an update containing one changed element while omitting the store-action option; confirm the element appears and check whether Undo treats the update as a recorded change, since the previous behavior captured it but the new behavior does not update the history snapshot.
Check that a normal drawing edit can be undone and redone, and that an update explicitly marked for snapshot-only handling does not become a separate undoable change.
Confirm a drawing change made by one participant appears for the other participant and remains present after ending the session and reopening the shared drawing.
Check that an image added during collaboration finishes loading and is visible to both participants.
uncertainty: The new store-action option is optional, but an update that omits it no longer changes the history snapshot; the supplied context does not establish whether integrations that omit the option are expected to remain undoable.

report.summary: The release improves canvas navigation and tool switching with hand-tool support across the editor.
keyChanges: The hand tool is available in the desktop and mobile toolbars; on desktop, H is its shortcut, and the tool changes the cursor and lets users pan the canvas.
While hand mode is active, shape actions are hidden when no elements are selected.
Finishing an eraser action now returns to the remembered active tool using the updated tool-state field; toolbar hints use a letter when a numeric shortcut is absent.
The editor toolbar now offers a hand-tool control on desktop and mobile, and the help dialog lists H as its shortcut.
Mobile toolbar controls are reordered: Library now appears before pen and lock controls, while the hand-tool control follows them.
Help-dialog shortcuts now capitalize a standalone lowercase single-character key; the supplied shortcuts do not show whether any currently displayed key uses that format.

The hand tool now routes a single-pointer drag into canvas panning and skips normal drawing interactions, so dragging the canvas in hand mode should move the view rather than create or alter an element.
The editor now connects a hand-tool control to its toggle action and supplies a hand icon; the exact control label is not provided.

Pressing H switches to the hand tool, clears the current element and group selection, and changes the cursor to a grab cursor; pressing H again restores the previous tool, or selection if none was saved.

Eraser switching now uses the shared previous-tool history, so turning it off should return to the tool active before the eraser; the evidence does not establish whether older editor state remains compatible.
When restoring a drawing saved with the hand tool active, restoration now permits that tool to remain active instead of treating it as an unlisted tool.
qaChecks: Verify that selecting the hand tool and dragging the canvas pans the drawing without moving its shapes; on desktop, also verify that pressing H activates the hand tool and shows the grab cursor.
Check that switching from the hand tool to the eraser, completing an erase action, and finishing it returns to the hand tool.
Confirm that shape actions are hidden when hand mode is active and no elements are selected.
Verify that a toolbar tool with a letter shortcut but no numeric shortcut displays the letter as its key hint.
Verify the desktop toolbar shows a hand-tool control and that selecting it makes its active state visible.
Verify the mobile toolbar shows the hand-tool control after the pen and lock controls, and that selecting it makes its active state visible.
Check the mobile toolbar order: Library appears before pen and lock, and the hand-tool control follows them.
Check the lock control while zen mode is enabled and confirm its intended visibility and toggling behavior.
Verify the tools section lists the hand tool with the H shortcut.
Confirm the existing shortcut entries remain legible and their key labels display as expected.
Verify that with the hand tool active, a left-button drag on the blank canvas pans the view and does not create an element.
Check that with the hand tool active, a left-button drag starting over an existing element pans the view instead of selecting or moving that element.
Verify pressing H while an element is selected clears the selection and changes the cursor to a grab cursor; press H again and confirm the prior drawing tool is restored.
Check the eraser toggle by pressing E while a drawing tool is active, then pressing E again; confirm the tool active before the eraser is restored.
Verify restoring drawing data with active tool set to hand retains hand as the active tool.
uncertainty: The supplied evidence does not identify whether any actual toolbar tool has a letter shortcut but no numeric shortcut, so that hint fallback may not have a concrete item to test.
The supplied shortcuts do not show a currently displayed standalone lowercase key, so the capitalization change has no confirmed real dialog input to distinguish the old and new display.
The hand control’s exact label and location are not supplied, so its navigation path cannot be specified.

It is unclear whether editor state created before this change can still restore the prior tool when leaving the eraser, because the restoration now uses shared tool history instead of the previous eraser-specific history.
The evidence does not establish what restoration did with hand before this change, only that it was not listed as an allowed tool.

report.summary: The release adds a searchable command palette and updates how editor actions and dialogs are presented.
keyChanges: Users can open a searchable command palette with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P or Ctrl/Cmd+/; it exposes editor, drawing, sharing, collaboration, and Excalidraw+ commands, with availability based on the current selection and view mode.
The main menu gains a command-palette entry, and many editor actions now have labels, icons, and search terms so they can be found and run from the palette.
Unlock-all is now available only when nothing is selected and at least one element is locked; previously, locked elements anywhere in the drawing were enough to make it available.
Regular dialogs no longer show the close button; the button remains on fullscreen dialogs.
qaChecks: Verify Ctrl/Cmd+/ opens the palette and pressing it again closes it; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P should also open it.
Check that searching for “align” with multiple elements selected offers alignment commands, and choosing one lines up the selected elements.
Confirm that with one or more locked elements and one element selected, unlock-all is unavailable; clear the selection and confirm it becomes available.
Verify the Excalidraw+ entries match account state: signed-out users see “Excalidraw+” and “Sign up,” while signed-in users see “Sign in / Go to Excalidraw+.”
Check that a regular dialog has no close button, while a fullscreen dialog shows a close button.
uncertainty: The removal of the close button from regular dialogs may be intentional; the supplied context does not clarify the intended dismissal experience.
