report.summary: The release refreshes sidebar behavior and related editor controls across the main and embedded editing experiences.
keyChanges: When restoring saved drawings, any string-valued sidebar setting now opens the default sidebar, even if the saved docking preference is false; previously only the Library setting could reopen, and only when docked.

Library updates that request the sidebar now open it on the Library tab, while updates without a confirmation prompt no longer automatically return keyboard focus to the editor; accepting a prompt still does.
The editor now takes keyboard focus on startup only when auto-focus is enabled, and the embeddable editor API can toggle a sidebar or force it open or closed.
The Library’s browsing and management controls are now grouped together, including in the empty-library state; removing items still clears the selection, and resetting still clears the Library.
The welcome screen’s center content and menu, toolbar, and help hints use updated wiring; their visible content is intended to remain available.
Buttons now support an active selected state, which applies selected styling when enabled.
The Library panel is now content within the default sidebar, and its control area groups browsing with library management options.
The default sidebar uses a saved docking preference, while custom integrations can supply their own docking behavior.
When host-provided UI is removed, the internal fallback can become available again instead of remaining suppressed.

Pasting, dropping, or inserting library items now keeps an open sidebar according to the default dock preference rather than its current docked state; the new element-insertion capability places supplied elements at the canvas center.
Sidebar control now uses a sidebar name and optional tab instead of the previous library/custom-sidebar toggle, and no longer explicitly rejects a custom sidebar when no renderer is configured.
Confirming or cancelling through a confirmation dialog now returns focus to the editor container, including clear-canvas and library removal or reset confirmations.
Shared buttons now run a supplied click handler before their selection action, skip that action when the handler prevents the default, and apply selected styling when selected.
Sidebar content now renders only for the active sidebar, and selecting a tab updates the active tab; sidebar triggers control whether their sidebar is open.
Outside clicks and Escape close an undocked sidebar, or one that does not fit the device, unless a dialog is open; a docked sidebar that fits stays open.
The dock control appears only when the device can fit the sidebar and docking is configured, while closing a sidebar no longer invokes its supplied close notification.
The editor now shows its default sidebar instead of choosing between the previous library menu and a host-provided custom sidebar, changing which sidebar content appears when a sidebar is open.
On mobile, the scroll-back control is now hidden whenever any sidebar is open; on desktop, a docked sidebar reserves space beside the drawing.
Choosing a chart preview now inserts its elements through the editor’s shared insertion path and closes the paste dialog.

Custom sidebars now use editor-provided sidebar content, triggers, and named tabs instead of the former sidebar-render callback; the package also exposes its default sidebar, so integrations relying only on the old callback need to migrate.
On devices too narrow for a sidebar, editing tips are now hidden whenever any sidebar is open, rather than only when the Library sidebar is open.
The previous Library toolbar control implementation is removed; its replacement and continued availability are not established, so verify how editors reach their reusable drawing Library.
The sidebar header no longer includes its previous dock toggle, while its close action now uses a close-request callback; verify docking and closing remain available as intended.
qaChecks: Verify that loading data with the sidebar stored as “library” and its docking preference set to false opens the default sidebar; previously, this combination restored it closed.
Check that loading data with only the older Library-open preference set to true does not reopen the sidebar.
Verify that a library update requesting the sidebar opens it on the Library tab, without moving keyboard focus to the editor when no confirmation prompt is shown.
Confirm that accepting a library confirmation prompt returns keyboard focus to the editor.
Test the sidebar control by requesting the Library sidebar twice, then forcing it open and forcing it closed; it should open, toggle closed, open, and close in that order.
Verify the empty Library shows its browsing and management controls when there are no saved items and no pending elements.
Check that selecting and removing a saved item removes it from the Library and clears the selection.
Confirm that resetting a populated Library clears its saved items.
Confirm pressing Escape while the sidebar is undocked still closes the Library, as it did before this change.
Verify the welcome-screen center content and its menu, toolbar, and help guidance appear in their expected positions.
Check that a button presented as selected shows its active styling, and that the unselected state does not show that styling.
Verify the Library tab shows its browsing and management controls, and that inserting a Library item adds it to the drawing.
Check the undocked sidebar by clicking outside it; confirm it closes as it did before the Library panel moved into the default sidebar.
Confirm changing the default sidebar’s docked state is reflected in its saved docking preference when the sidebar is shown again.
Verify that after host-provided UI has been mounted and then removed, rendering the editor without that host UI displays the internal fallback.
Verify that pasting, dropping, or inserting elements while the sidebar is open, the device can fit it, and the current state is docked but the default preference is false closes the sidebar.
Check that submitting elements through the embedded-editor insertion capability places them at the canvas center.
Verify that requesting the custom sidebar to open is accepted and reports success when no renderer is configured.
Check that choosing either confirm or cancel closes the confirmation and returns focus to the editor container.
Verify that opening a sidebar trigger shows its sidebar, selecting a tab changes the displayed tab, and selecting the same trigger again closes the sidebar.

Check that an outside click or Escape closes an undocked sidebar when no dialog is open, but leaves it open when a dialog is open; on a device that can fit it, confirm a docked sidebar stays open for both actions.
Confirm the dock control appears only when docking is configured on a device that can fit the sidebar, and that selecting it toggles the docked state.

Test a button with a click handler that prevents the default: the handler should run, the button’s selection action should not, and a button marked selected should show selected styling; confirm closing an embedded sidebar does not invoke its supplied close notification.
Verify that the default reusable-drawing sidebar opens from its toolbar trigger and can be docked and undocked on desktop and mobile.
Check that the drawing area leaves room for a docked sidebar on desktop.
Confirm that on mobile the scroll-back control is hidden when the drawing is scrolled away and a non-library sidebar is open; this case previously showed the control.
Verify that choosing either offered chart preview inserts the selected chart into the drawing and closes the paste dialog.

Verify the integration using only the former sidebar-render callback does not show that supplied panel, while the child-provided sidebar opens from its configured trigger and switches between both tabs.
Confirm the integration using the package-provided default sidebar displays it and its tab controls respond.
Verify that opening a non-Library sidebar suppresses the line-editing tip, and that closing the sidebar makes the tip visible again.

Verify Library access when the Library sidebar is already open and docked; this was the exact state in which the previous toolbar control was hidden, and confirm the current editor still provides the intended way to use the Library.
Check Library access with the sidebar closed and confirm the intended current entry point opens the reusable drawing Library.
Verify whether the sidebar can still be docked in that setup; the previous header offered a dock control under these conditions, but its replacement is not established here.
Confirm activating the sidebar close control closes the sidebar.
uncertainty: The intended compatibility behavior for drawings saved with the older Library-open preference is unclear; restoration no longer uses that preference, so confirm whether those drawings are expected to reopen the Library.

The Library’s former Escape-to-close handler was removed, and the supplied evidence does not show whether another handler replaces it; the intended keyboard-focus destination after resetting the Library is also unclear.
The Library panel’s former outside-click close behavior was removed during the move into the default sidebar; verify that an undocked panel still closes when the user clicks outside it.

The old behavior explicitly rejected opening a custom sidebar without a renderer; the replacement removes that rejection, but the supplied context does not establish whether accepting that request is intended.
The previous host-provided custom sidebar path is no longer selected, but the supplied context does not establish whether embedders are expected to retain that sidebar capability.

The supplied evidence removes the Library toolbar component and its previous sidebar-header docking control but does not establish their replacement or whether those capabilities are intentionally removed.

report.summary: The release standardizes how drawing and image changes are tracked, saved, undone, and synchronized across editing and collaboration.
keyChanges: Already-observed editor state is now recognized and reused rather than projected again, which should preserve observed selection details when state updates are recorded.
Unchanged observed elements or editor state reuse the existing snapshot, avoiding a new recorded increment when there is no detected change.

Canvas interactions now distinguish updates to the current history snapshot from changes captured for undo and redo, so short touch-drawing cleanup and other transient edits should not become separate undo steps.
Choosing a color with the eyedropper now records the selection as a captured drawing change, while completed editor updates are committed after rendering.
Importing an Excalidraw drawing updates the existing drawing’s history snapshot before adding imported content, helping preserve element ordering when undoing.

Image save and failure status changes, and scene refreshes synchronized from another browser tab, are now applied as scene updates; loading a scene after a URL change is explicitly captured, while ordinary scene loading no longer explicitly disables store commits.
Line and arrow point editing has no identified runtime behavior change.

Incoming and initial collaboration scenes, session-stop updates, and completed shared-image uploads now explicitly use the UPDATE store action; verify drawings and shared images remain intact and synchronized in these flows.
The exported store-action values are now lowercase (“capture”, “update”, and “none”) instead of uppercase, so integrations using literal values must update them.
Store updates are now committed according to scheduled actions, with capture taking precedence over a snapshot-only update; resetting the store also clears queued actions.
qaChecks: Verify the selected line or arrow remains selected after an editor-state update and that undoing and redoing the drawing edit restores the expected drawing state.
Verify a very short touch-drawn freehand mark that records fewer than 10 points, followed by placing a second finger, is discarded and does not return as a separate change when undoing.
Check that resizing an element and then undoing and redoing leaves the drawing in the corresponding before-and-after states.
Confirm that choosing a color with the eyedropper updates the selected element, or the current drawing color when no element is selected, and that undo and redo reverse and reapply the color change.
Verify that importing the drawing and then undoing and redoing preserves the distinct ordering of existing and imported elements.
Verify that an element update without a specified history action appears on the canvas, and check whether it creates a new undo step.
Verify that loading the scene URL replaces the current drawing and that the loaded drawing is available to undo, as expected for a captured scene change.
Check that when the image file is unavailable, the image remains in the drawing with its error state and the status refresh does not create a separate undoable drawing edit.
Confirm that after saving an image, its saved status appears without creating a separate undoable drawing edit.
Verify that when the second tab receives the newer saved scene, the drawing refreshes without treating the synchronization itself as a new user edit.
Verify that when one participant changes the scene, the other participant receives the drawing changes and any shared image loads.
Check starting a new collaboration room from a drawing with a saved image; confirm the drawing remains present and the image can be shared with the joining participant.

report.summary: The release improves how people discover and use editor actions while refining related editing and dialog interactions.
keyChanges: Shortcut lookup can now return a requested alternate shortcut, falling back to the first when that index is unavailable; the Ctrl/Cmd+P hint can therefore show the second shortcut instead of repeating the first.

The command palette’s supplied implementation supports keyboard navigation, marks unavailable commands, and closes before running a selected command; its displayed labels and icons can reflect the current drawing.
Dialogs now focus their initial control after a delay, and the header close button appears only on mobile, where it uses a close icon.
Double-clicking a selected line or arrow that is already being edited now continues through regular canvas double-click handling instead of returning early.

Ctrl+P or Cmd+P without Shift or Alt now shows a temporary command-palette shortcut hint, the help dialog lists the command-palette shortcuts, and a command-palette menu item is configured to open the palette.
Context-action captions now use the action’s general label instead of its context-specific caption, so actions that supply only the older context-specific caption may have no displayed caption.
Dialogs now receive disabled-animation styling when animation disabling is active when the dialog first opens, and external links are opened with opener access disabled.
The command palette groups commands in a defined order and supports fuzzy, accent-insensitive search; searches discard spaces and the characters <, >, -, _, and | before matching.

The palette exposes stroke- and background-color commands when the current selection supports them, using the same eligibility rules as the selection controls; running a command opens its corresponding color popup.

The command palette is added to the main menu and gains actions for sharing, live collaboration, Excalidraw+ promotion and export, community links, and theme switching; signed-in users see a combined Excalidraw+ sign-in or destination option instead of the separate promotion and sign-up options.
Element-lock actions now require a selection to toggle locking, show wording and an icon based on the selection, and offer unlock-all only when nothing is selected and at least one element is locked.
Opening another editor dialog now closes the share or collaboration dialog.

Editor actions now include display labels and icons, with palette names for canvas background, clearing, and hand-tool actions; theme switching gains dark/light search keywords, a theme-dependent action label and icon, and a command that runs the registered theme action.
Choosing the image tool from the command palette by keyboard sets direct insertion on, while choosing it by mouse does not.
When no element is selected, hyperlink label generation now safely resolves to the create-link label; the hyperlink action itself is available only when exactly one element is selected.

Frame actions now use action labels rather than context-menu-specific labels, and the frame tool gains an icon and is explicitly unavailable in view mode; selecting or removing frame contents is otherwise unchanged.
Grouping and ungrouping gain action labels and icons, with no change to their grouping behavior shown.
Undo and redo gain explicit labels and icons and are marked unavailable in view mode; their history operations and keyboard shortcuts are unchanged.
Line editing is categorized under Elements and its label switches between entering and exiting editing; the label check now safely handles a missing selection.

Several editor actions now have labels and icons for command selection, and the command palette has shortcuts Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P and Ctrl/Cmd+/; additional mappings cover zoom, fit-to-view, tool, and shortcut-help commands.
Object snapping is no longer marked as available in view mode; its existing Alt+S action still toggles snapping and clears the grid when used.
Dropdown menus now remove their Escape-key listener using the same capture setting used when adding it, preventing the listener from remaining after a menu closes.

Editor actions across selection, drawing properties, text binding, library, clipboard, menus, and export now have general labels, and several now specify icons; QA-visible impact is limited to how these actions are identified wherever the editor presents them.

Clipboard actions now include discovery terms: SVG and PNG copy actions use “svg”, “png”, “clipboard”, and “copy”, while text copy uses “text”, “clipboard”, and “copy”. No old-versus-new input producing a different drawing result is evident in these changes.

report.summary: The release changes how drawing edits and editor actions are recorded and restored, with undo and redo behavior the main area to verify.
keyChanges: Deleting the last remaining point of an edited line now captures the deletion in history; before, this case did not capture it, so undo should restore the line.
Text attached to a rotated container now takes on the container’s angle when its bounding box is redrawn, so verify its orientation after editing or changing its layout.

Connection handling now revisits bound text and arrows when elements change or are removed, including resolving competing bound text; verify connections and attached text after edits, deletion, undo, and redo.

Grouping and ungrouping now capture successful changes in the drawing store, and grouping uses the reordered elements returned by the ordering step; verify group order and that undo restores the prior drawing.

Undo and redo now track drawing and app-state changes separately; unlike before, an app-state-only change no longer clears redo, so edits such as changing the canvas background should not discard a pending redo.
Loading a scene after a URL hash change now commits it to the drawing store rather than recording it as a history change.
When the drawing has no undo or redo entries, the corresponding control is now disabled; previously it remained enabled and clicking it made no change.

Undo and redo now apply recorded drawing and app-state changes against the current scene snapshot, including resolving affected element bindings; verify edits can still be reversed and reapplied without losing visible drawing relationships.
Undo and redo now apply drawing and editor-state changes together, including element order, bindings, and text attached to shapes; verify that restored edits remain visually consistent.

History application now reconciles selected shapes, groups, and line-editing state against elements that still exist, removing references to deleted items and restoring state when the related item exists.

Scene snapshots now detect changes to elements and observed editor state, preserve missing elements as deletions, and capture increments when changes are detected; this also reaches scene loading and has potential relevance to collaboration.

Pasting drawing content or text, erasing, editing line points, changing selected colors, importing drawings, and removing frame contents now request history capture; frame selection changes are captured too.
After undo, a selection-only change no longer clears redo, and a pointer-up that changes the selection can now be recorded even when nothing remains selected.

A local scene update that changes elements but does not explicitly request a store commit was previously undoable as a side effect; it is now not undoable, while imported drawings also have invalid or conflicting stacking-order positions synchronized.

Receiving a collaborator’s scene update no longer explicitly clears the undo history, and starting or stopping a session no longer explicitly clears or suppresses history; check that local undo behavior remains safe when scene changes arrive.
The zoom-in control is disabled at the maximum zoom and zoom-out is disabled at the minimum; fitting content now clamps to the configured zoom limits instead of hard-coded limits.
Canvas, drawing-property, scene-load, and save actions now use the updated history/store handling, with capture or no-capture choices corresponding to their previous history settings.

Finalizing a drawing now captures a store update regardless of the active tool; previously only freehand finalization was committed to history, so finishing a rectangle or line is an important undo and redo check.
Entering or leaving line-point editing, selecting all, and opening the link editor now capture updates; finalizing line editing also clears its selected-line editing state.
Library, clipboard, collaborator-follow, style-copy, and grid, snapping, stats, view, and zen-mode actions are now marked as store no-ops, preserving their intent not to add drawing-history entries.
Aligning, distributing, flipping, locking or unlocking, and changing layer order now request snapshot capture; verify these edits still work and can be undone and redone.

Duplicating now reconciles element ordering using the duplicated elements and the returned ordering result, rather than the previous-elements-plus-duplicates map; verify duplication preserves the original drawing and places copies correctly.
Opening or closing the canvas menu, editing menu, and help dialog now explicitly requests no snapshot capture; new snapshot helpers also expose snapshot state and filter pending element updates.

report.summary: This release adds freeform lasso selection and updates how the editor determines which elements are selected or belong to frames.
keyChanges: The lasso tool is available from the toolbar and command palette; drawing around or across elements selects them, and Alt-drag from selection mode starts a lasso instead of a selection-area drag.
Lasso and frame hit-testing now follows curved and rotated element outlines more closely, and lasso intersections allow a tolerance of 1 scene unit.
For eligible selected elements, the image tool no longer by itself prevents stroke-color controls from being available.

Check that, with an existing element selected, holding Alt and Shift while lassoing another element keeps the existing selection and adds the newly selected element.
Test a lasso path that passes 0.5 scene units from an element outline without crossing it; verify that the element is still selected under the 1-unit intersection tolerance.
Confirm that a narrow frame crossing only the rounded rectangle’s visible curved corner recognizes the element as intersecting the frame.
Verify that stroke-color controls remain available for the selected element while the image tool is active, and that changing its stroke color takes effect.
uncertainty: Generic drag-created areas no longer honor center resizing, but the supplied evidence does not identify the user input that previously enabled it, so a reliable reproduction input cannot be specified.

report.summary: Selection and lasso interactions now adapt to touch devices, with related changes to pasting and snapping.
keyChanges: Touch devices now start with lasso as the selection tool, while desktop retains the standard selection tool; after actions such as clearing, deleting, or pasting, the editor returns to the device’s default.

Pasted drawing content is placed at the canvas center on mobile or tablet instead of at the pointer; desktop placement remains at the pointer.

Dragging selected elements with the lasso tool can now use snapping, while lasso selection itself remains unsnapped; on touch devices, the lasso tool also takes the primary selection toolbar position and the “1” shortcut.

report.summary: The release adds elbow arrows and improves how they connect, route, and respond to editing and undo.
keyChanges: Elbow arrows now have logic to choose a route around shapes and to update that route as endpoints or intermediate points are edited, or as connected shapes move, resize, or rotate.
Connection logic accounts for rotated shapes, distinguishes diamond sides, and snaps dragged endpoints toward shape edges or midpoints; navigation was not found in the supplied context.
Elbow-arrow connections can now treat a point inside a shape’s bounds as a binding target while the arrow is being dragged, not only points on or near its outline.

Elbow arrows now render with rounded bends, up to 16 units of corner radius and limited to half the length of either adjoining segment; corner routing and connected-arrow transforms also receive updated handling.
New elbow-arrow routing chooses a path around drawing elements; newly created arrows default to the round arrow type.
Undo and redo now recalculate arrows connected to changed elements using the current drawing, which can affect the restored connector route.

Arrow tools and selected arrows now offer arrow-style controls; pressing A while the arrow tool is active cycles sharp, round, and elbow styles, while arrows no longer offer roundness changes and elbow arrows are excluded from the line-point editor.
Elbow arrows now route around drawing elements and can bind to shapes; unlike before, moving a single bound elbow arrow by dragging, resizing it, or pressing an arrow key does not move it.
Elbow-arrow point editing no longer snaps to the grid, and box selection of their points is limited to the two endpoints.
The arrow-tool hint now gives arrow-specific guidance including the A shortcut; line-tool and multi-segment guidance remain distinct.

Elbow-arrow connections now use fixed attachment points, and resizing a connected shape or duplicating its arrow preserves the full connection details; verify attachments remain at the same relative point.
Elbow arrows no longer show rotation handles or a bounding box, and their editing handles and point highlights omit interior route points while retaining the endpoints.
Elbow-arrow routing now adjusts snap points to avoid rectangular corners, and binding previews use a fixed 10-pixel outline thickness instead of a shape-dependent thickness.
Negative angles now convert to a 0–360° range: for example, -90° previously produced -90° and now produces 270°.
Elbow arrows no longer expose the rotation control in the Stats panel, and rotation edits there skip elbow arrows.
Changing element position or size through the Stats panel now supplies the drawing context when updating connector bindings, including when resizing groups.
When restoring a drawing, elbow-arrow status is retained and a missing binding fixed point defaults to [0,0]; non-elbow bindings have their fixed point cleared.
Arrow skeletons are now created as arrows, and arrow containers are recognized for binding during conversion.

Arrow properties now offer sharp, round, and elbow styles; converting an arrow to elbow style keeps its endpoints and recalculates its route, while switching away from elbow style also starts from those endpoints.
Elbow arrows are excluded from the straight-line editor and no longer accept segment midpoints; the general roundness setting also no longer changes elbow arrows.
Arrow connections are recalculated during drawing, editing, flipping, and property-panel moves, resizes, and rotations so connectors can stay attached to shapes.

Elbow arrows are created with two endpoints, route as users draw, and finalize instead of accepting another bend point; with grid snapping enabled, their drawing points are no longer snapped to the grid.
Deleting a shape connected to an elbow arrow now clears that connection and recalculates the arrow route; cutting a selected shape follows the same deletion behavior.
Undo and redo now recalculate connected-arrow routes when restoring drawing changes.
Ctrl+double-clicking a selected elbow arrow no longer follows the special path that opens point editing.

Check a connection to a rotated diamond from each side; confirm the arrow attaches to the corresponding side rather than an unrelated edge.

Verify the new arrow uses the round arrow type by default.

uncertainty: The supplied changes contain no removed code for these additions, so the previous behavior and a concrete input that takes a different old path cannot be established; the boundary case is based on the new logic, not a proven regression.

The routing and heap functions are supplied as additions without their before versions, so the evidence does not establish a specific old-versus-new routing input that exposes a regression; test obstructed paths and aligned endpoints, but the precise previous behavior is unknown.
The evidence does not explain why a single bound elbow arrow cannot be dragged or resized; confirm that this restriction is intended.

The added scene-wide input to endpoint binding may affect which candidate is considered when shapes overlap, but the supplied evidence does not establish which overlapping shape should take precedence.

report.summary: The release expands drawing-editor selection with lasso tools and refines related drawing interactions and controls.
keyChanges: Ellipse outlines used four unique straight chords, duplicated, for geometry checks; they are now represented by a closed 90-segment approximation, which can change whether lasso strokes and frame edges intersect an ellipse.

Lasso selection now checks element outlines for enclosure or intersection, applies a tolerance of 1 to intersection checks, and normalizes selection so bound text selects its container and selecting a frame omits its children. The prior behavior of these newly supplied lasso routines cannot be established from the available evidence.
Lasso feedback now uses an animated, dashed indigo trail that is cleared when the gesture ends; updating a trail also discards previously completed trails, including laser-pointer trails.
Dragging a new shape while holding the center-resize modifier no longer draws it outward from its center; it uses the initial pointer position as its origin instead.

Lasso gestures now update selection as the path is drawn, clear the existing selection when started without Shift, and preserve it when started with Shift; the trail and selection state are cleared when the gesture ends.
Holding Alt while dragging an existing selection box now switches to lasso selection; releasing Alt during that drag returns to box selection instead of continuing the lasso.
Restoration now recognizes lasso in its tool map, so imported drawing state with lasso selected should retain that tool instead of treating it as unrecognized.

Line-segment intersection checks now accept an optional tolerance; a crossing 0.5 units beyond a segment endpoint can count as an intersection when the supplied tolerance is 1, while existing callers shown do not supply a tolerance.

The lasso tool can be selected from the extra-tools menu or command palette, and the selection tool button switches to lasso when selection is already active; verify the tool shown as active matches the choice.
With lasso active, shape actions are hidden when nothing is selected but remain available when elements are selected; releasing Space no longer clears an existing selection.
Two canvas hints are now displayed as a one-item hint list, which removes a final period if the translated hint includes one; the embed tool symbol also has a slightly heavier outline.
A new lasso tool lets editors select drawing elements by enclosing or intersecting them; activating it clears the current selection, and activating it again returns to the selection tool.

Explicit custom names are removed from the canvas background, clear canvas, hand tool, unlock-all, statistics, view mode, and zen mode actions; the effect on how those actions are found is not established.
qaChecks: Verify a narrow lasso stroke crossing the ellipse’s upper-left curved edge near the point 15 units right and 9 units down from its top-left corner, without touching the old straight chord from the top to the leftmost point, selects the ellipse.
Check that a frame edge crossing that same curved part of the ellipse recognizes the ellipse as intersecting the frame.
Confirm that lasso-selecting bound text selects its container, and lasso-selecting a frame does not separately select its contained children.
Verify that a lasso gesture shows an animated, dashed indigo trail while dragging and that the trail clears when the gesture ends while the lasso-selected elements remain selected.
Check two successive laser-pointer strokes, including a collaborator's stroke if available: after the second stroke updates, confirm the earlier completed trail is no longer displayed.

Test drawing a new shape by dragging while holding Alt (or Option on Mac), the modifier that previously requested center-based drawing; confirm the shape starts at the initial pointer position rather than expanding from its center.

Verify that holding Alt while dragging out a selection box follows the lasso path and selects elements along or inside it, rather than continuing the old box-selection behavior; release Alt during the drag and confirm box selection resumes.
Check that starting a lasso gesture without Shift clears the previous selection, while starting it with Shift preserves the previously selected elements as the lasso updates selection.
Confirm that after completing a lasso gesture, the trail is cleared and a subsequent lasso gesture starts cleanly without stale selection or trail state.
Verify that restoring the drawing with lasso saved as its active tool recognizes and retains lasso rather than falling back to another tool.
Test the intersection with tolerance 1 and confirm the crossing at (10.5, 0) is included; without the tolerance, confirm this 0.5-unit endpoint overrun remains outside the segment.
Verify that, with selection active, choosing the selection tool button switches the active tool to lasso, and that choosing it while another tool is active switches to selection.
Check that with lasso active and no elements selected, shape actions are hidden, and that selecting an element makes those actions available.
Confirm that with lasso active and an element selected, pressing and releasing Space leaves the element selected.

Verify that when the displayed canvas-panning or deep-selection hint ends in a period, the displayed hint has no final period; also confirm the embed tool symbol remains clear with its slightly heavier outline.
Check that the lasso tool command is available and choosing it makes lasso the active tool.
Verify that activating the lasso tool while an element is selected clears the current selection.
Check that drawing a closed lasso around a shape selects it, and that a lasso path crossing another element also selects that element.
Confirm that activating the lasso tool again returns to the selection tool.
uncertainty: The lasso selection and update routines are supplied only as additions, without their prior implementations, so their old-versus-new behavior cannot be confirmed; the ellipse outline difference does have a direct before-and-after comparison.

The lasso tool can now be switched on with an option to preserve the current selection, but the supplied context does not establish whether a user workflow uses that option or what selection behavior it should show.
No supplied application surface or current caller demonstrates use of the new tolerance, so it is unclear whether it has a user-visible effect in this release.
The supplied evidence does not show whether either affected hint actually ends with a period in the tested language, so the visible hint change may depend on its translation.
The supplied evidence does not describe prior lasso behavior or identify where actions with removed custom names are presented, so their before-and-after discovery behavior cannot be confirmed.

report.summary: The release moves text-to-diagram creation into a streamed chat workflow with persistent chat history and updated Mermaid previews.
keyChanges: Text-to-diagram generation now streams assistant responses into a conversation, supports stopping generation, and presents rate-limit and error messages in the chat.
The prompt limit increases from 1,000 to 10,000 characters, while the 3-character minimum remains; a 1,001-character prompt now passes validation instead of being rejected.

report.summary: The release improves device-aware selection behavior and tool recovery across the editor.
keyChanges: On touch-capable devices with a coarse pointer, lasso is the default selection tool; after pasting or inserting items, creating text, or finishing a drawing, the editor now returns to that default instead of always returning to selection.

Lasso interaction now distinguishes taps on elements from lasso gestures: touch users select an unselected element immediately and can drag it, while desktop users avoid moving elements accidentally during a lasso gesture.
In lasso mode, Ctrl+Alt pointer-down now starts a lasso trail and switches to lasso selection; touch context menus and canvas double-click handling are also allowed when lasso is the default tool.

When lasso is the default selection tool, it takes the primary selection-tool position and the 1 shortcut; the separate lasso menu item is hidden, and returning from the laser tool or unlocking a tool returns to lasso.
With lasso active and no elements selected, hovering over a movable element no longer shows the move cursor; the move cursor remains available when elements are selected.
Pasting copied drawing elements on mobile or tablet now places them at the canvas center instead of at the cursor; desktop placement remains at the cursor.
The welcome screen on an empty drawing now appears when the default selection tool is active, including when that tool is lasso.
On mobile or tablet, a restored selection, lasso, or image tool now becomes lasso; on desktop, a restored lasso now becomes selection, while selection and image resolve to selection.
After image selection is canceled or fails, the editor now returns to its device’s default tool instead of always returning to selection.

After clearing the canvas from the image tool, deleting selected elements, or finishing an interaction, the editor now returns to its configured default selection tool instead of always returning to standard selection; leaving the eraser with no saved prior tool follows that same default.

The lasso-tool action is suppressed when lasso is already the default, and snapping can now operate during a drag of selected elements with lasso active, while remaining disabled during lasso selection itself.
iOS platform detection now ignores letter case, and a mobile-device classification has been added; this may affect which resize and rotation handles are available on mobile devices.
qaChecks: Verify that tapping an unselected element while lasso is active selects it immediately, and that dragging it in the same gesture moves it rather than drawing a lasso trail.
Check that tapping a frame whose child is selected selects the frame and deselects its child, so the frame and its contents are not selected together.
Confirm that after pasting an item, creating text, or finishing a shape, the next selection interaction uses lasso behavior rather than the previous selection-tool behavior.
Test a long-press on the canvas and a double-tap in the default touch mode; verify that the context menu opens and the canvas double-click behavior is handled.
Verify that holding Ctrl+Alt and dragging across elements starts lasso selection and selects elements along the gesture.
Check that lassoing across an element does not move it during that same gesture, then confirm a later pointer-down can drag the selected element.
Confirm that when lasso mode is active, dragging an already selected element moves it; previously, dragging was blocked whenever lasso was active.
Verify that an empty drawing with lasso as the default selection tool shows the welcome screen.
Check that lasso occupies the primary selection-tool position, the separate lasso menu item is absent, and pressing 1 activates lasso.
Confirm that pressing K to leave the laser tool and unlocking a locked tool both return to lasso.

Verify that hovering over an unselected element with lasso active does not show the move cursor, while hovering over a selected element does; then paste copied drawing elements on mobile or tablet with the cursor away from center and confirm they appear centered rather than at the cursor.
Verify on a mobile or tablet that loading a saved drawing whose active tool is selection starts in lasso mode; this input previously remained in selection mode.
Verify on desktop that loading a saved drawing whose active tool is lasso starts in selection mode; this input previously remained in lasso mode.
Check on a mobile or tablet that starting image insertion and canceling file selection returns the editor to lasso mode; it previously returned to selection mode.

Verify that, while selected elements are being dragged with lasso active and no Ctrl/Cmd modifier held, an element brought within 8 canvas units of an alignment target snaps into alignment; this drag case did not snap before the change.
Check that finishing a drawing leaves lasso active rather than standard selection.
Confirm that deleting selected elements and clearing the canvas while the image tool is active each leave the configured lasso default active.
Verify that leaving the eraser with no saved prior tool returns to lasso, and that the lasso-tool action is suppressed when lasso is already the default.
Verify that the expected resize and rotation handles are available and that resizing the selected element still works; uppercase IPHONE was not recognized by the previous case-sensitive iOS check.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not specify which device sizes the editor classifies as mobile or tablet.
The supplied context does not explain how to configure lasso as the default or reach an eraser state with no saved prior tool, so those selection-tool checks may require a specially prepared editor.

report.summary: Flowchart creation and keyboard handling have been reorganized, with the main visible change being obstacle-aware placement of newly created nodes.
keyChanges: New flowchart nodes are placed beside the selected node while avoiding other nodes connected into that flowchart; when extending a preview in the same direction, existing preview nodes should stay in place when the expanded group still fits.
Keyboard-driven flowchart creation and navigation now share a dedicated handler, which reveals pending or selected nodes when needed and records completed creation or navigation changes for history.
qaChecks: Verify that pressing Ctrl or Cmd with an arrow key previews a new connected node beside the selected node, and releasing the modifier commits it.

Check the changed-placement case: with a connected node obstructing the new branch’s placement band, press Ctrl or Cmd plus the arrow key toward that band; confirm the preview uses the nearest available clear space and leaves at least a 100-pixel cross-axis gap from the obstacle.

Confirm that while continuing to create nodes in the same direction, earlier preview nodes keep their positions when the expanded group still fits; press Escape during preview and confirm it is canceled without committing.
Test Alt plus an arrow key on a flowchart node with a linked node in that direction; confirm the linked node becomes selected and visible, and releasing Alt ends navigation.

report.summary: This release changes how framed drawings are targeted, ordered, and displayed during editing.
keyChanges: Frame targeting now accounts for the topmost object and existing frame membership, while dragged selections are previewed in frame order before the drop is committed.
New objects and pasted framed drawings are inserted with frame-child ordering in mind; text bound to a container no longer joins a frame unless that container belongs to it.
Interior hit testing now treats a non-transparent color as a filled background only for element types that support backgrounds.
qaChecks: Verify selecting the existing frame child and the unframed element together, then dragging them into the same frame, makes both frame contents and reorders them together relative to the frame.
Check dragging an eligible new element over a frame where a higher-stacking non-frame object covers the pointer: the frame is not highlighted as the drop target.
Confirm that when a text container outside a frame is under the pointer inside that frame, new text remains attached to the container and does not join the unrelated frame.
Verify pasting the copied frame preserves the relative stacking order of its children and does not change their association with the copied frame.

Check that the underlying filled shape remains reachable for selection or arrow connection through the overlaid element, rather than being blocked by a color that is not a supported fill for that element type.
uncertainty: The hit-testing difference requires an element type that does not support a background but carries a non-transparent background color; supplied context does not establish whether users can create this input through normal editing, so suitable manual test data may need to be prepared.

report.summary: The release refines keyboard-driven flowchart creation and navigation in the drawing editor.
keyChanges: Ctrl/Command+Arrow creation and Alt+Arrow navigation are handled together; when creation commits, the new elements are inserted and the first is selected and brought into view if needed.
When navigation and creation end on the same key release, both workflows are cleared and an immediate history capture is requested once, rather than separately for each workflow.

Newly created flowchart nodes are positioned to avoid space occupied by connected nodes, rather than always using the previous evenly spaced layout; repeated additions in a blocked direction may appear in a different open position.
Keyboard navigation between linked nodes now uses the direction of their elbow-arrow connections, and canceling creation clears its saved placement position.

New flowchart nodes are placed one 100-pixel gap along the chosen direction and shifted to the nearest clear cross-axis slot, accounting for obstacles throughout the connected flowchart rather than only nearby linked nodes.
When a pending group of nodes grows, its existing nodes are intended to keep their positions if the larger group still fits.
The creator’s initial direction changes from right to unset, and the former fallback that mapped unrecognized keys to right is removed; the expected keyboard behavior needs confirmation.

Undo and redo still defer history updates while a flowchart is being created, and the editor still receives pending flowchart nodes; these values are now accessed through the flowchart state holder. The diff does not establish a change to what users see or how they create diagrams.
qaChecks: Verify the combined-release case: hold Alt and press an Arrow key to navigate, then while still holding Alt press Ctrl/Command+Arrow to start creating from the selected node; release Alt and Ctrl/Command together. Confirm navigation ends, the new flowchart elements are committed, and the first new element is selected and brought into view if hidden.

Verify that, with the usual placement position blocked by an existing connected node, adding another node in the same direction with Ctrl/Cmd+Arrow places it in open space and leaves it connected by an elbow arrow.
Check that Alt+Arrow navigates to a connected node in the indicated direction when the connection is an elbow arrow.
Confirm that after starting and canceling flowchart creation with Escape, creating a new flowchart starts with a fresh placement position rather than retaining the canceled attempt's position.

Verify that adding a node when an existing connected node occupies the next-node creation band places the new node in the nearest available cross-axis slot without overlapping the existing node, while keeping at least 100 pixels of clearance.
Check that extending a pending group from one node to two in clear space leaves the first node in its original position.
Confirm the direction used when creating a node before selecting a direction, and the result of pressing a key unrelated to direction selection.
Verify that requesting undo or redo while flowchart creation is in progress does not apply the history update mid-creation, and that undo or redo works on the completed drawing afterward.
uncertainty: The combined modifier release now requests one history capture instead of two; the expected undo-step behavior for this simultaneous navigation-and-creation case is not established.
The previous navigation logic is not included, so the exact elbow-arrow arrangement that changes which node Alt+Arrow selects is unknown.

The supplied change sets the initial direction to unset and removes the old rule that mapped any unrecognized key to right, but does not show the replacement keyboard rule; the expected result before direction selection or after an unrelated key is unresolved.

The diff changes how the editor accesses flowchart-creation state, but shows no input that follows a different path before versus after the change; confirm whether this is intended as a behavior-preserving reorganization.

report.summary: The release expands text-to-diagram creation into a chat-based workflow with improved diagram previews and related interface behavior.
keyChanges: Text-to-diagram chat now supports prompt entry, saved-chat management, message actions, generated-diagram preview and insertion, and Mermaid viewing; the chat area also shows remaining message limits and generated responses can be opened as Mermaid.

The send button is enabled only when the trimmed prompt has more than 3 characters, but pressing Enter submits any nonblank prompt; Shift+Enter adds a line break, and submitting trims and clears the prompt.
Actions explicitly marked disabled are now unavailable; during generation, the new-chat and chat-history controls are disabled, and network-error retry becomes available after the 5-second wait.

Saved chats are stored locally, sorted by update time, limited to the 10 most recently updated chats, and titled from the first user message; titles are trimmed and messages longer than 50 characters become the first 47 characters followed by an ellipsis.
Preview errors now have a localized title and can show a generic Mermaid syntax message instead of parser details; the preview canvas is hidden when an error is present.
Workflow panels can show multiple button, link, or rate-limit actions, affecting chat actions and the diagram preview’s insert action.

Chat management now supports starting a fresh chat, restoring saved chats, and deleting chats; deleting the active chat switches to the first remaining saved chat or starts a blank chat if none remain.

Saved chats are applied with message timestamps normalized, and the active error state is restored from the last assistant message; chats are saved when message history changes and generation is not active.

Mermaid previews now validate and throttle streaming content, flush pending content when generation finishes, and render the latest assistant message when switching chats; a chat with no assistant messages clears the preview.

Text-to-diagram generation now sends chat messages to a streaming service, combines streamed content into the generated diagram, and handles rate-limit and stream errors; an HTTP 429 now returns “Rate limit exceeded” instead of the previous daily-limit message.
Mermaid preview rendering now rejects empty text, mismatched brackets, braces, or parentheses, and text ending with an incomplete diagram operator or separator.

Mermaid conversion now returns a success or failure result, uses the supplied editor theme for its preview, and no longer checks the rendered canvas by converting it to a blob; test oversized diagrams and conversion failures.
Dialogs no longer carry the outside-click prevention marker, so check that backdrop dismissal and clicks inside dialog content behave as intended.
The command palette’s clock symbol is replaced by a history-style symbol, and the code-family symbol in font selection is updated.
Text-to-diagram prompts must contain 3–10,000 characters, and generation is blocked when no requests remain.

Generation adds the prompt and a pending assistant reply to chat, sends the three most recent non-empty chat messages plus the current prompt, streams the reply, and attempts to convert it into a diagram.
Request failures distinguish rate-limit warnings from exhausted-message-limit warnings; Mermaid parsing errors are reported in chat, with nested error messages displayed on separate lines.
An aborted generation is not reported as a request or parsing failure.

The current chat handling adds and updates messages, selects the latest assistant reply, and excludes empty content from generation context; prior implementations are not supplied, so these cannot be confirmed as behavior changes.
Text-to-diagram is now presented as a chat workflow with chat history and actions to retry or repair a response, view it as Mermaid, and insert a diagram into the drawing.
The Mermaid preview now renders and saves edits only while its tab is active, clears when its active input is empty, and uses the editor’s current theme.
Deleting an assistant reply truncates the chat before the prompt immediately preceding that reply, so later messages may also be removed.
qaChecks: Verify the prompt "abc" cannot be submitted with the send button, but pressing Enter submits it and clears the input; confirm a 4-character prompt enables the send button.
Check that Shift+Enter inserts a line break without submitting, while Enter submits a nonblank prompt after trimming surrounding spaces.
Confirm that while a response is generating, the new-chat and chat-history controls are disabled and the stop action remains available.

Verify that a saved chat can be restored and deleted, and that a generated diagram can be inserted from its preview; for a network error with a recorded attempt, confirm retry becomes available after 5 seconds.
Verify that saving a chat whose first user message is exactly 51 characters gives it a title made of the first 47 characters followed by three periods.
Check that saving 11 distinct chats leaves the 10 most recently updated chats in saved history.
Confirm that starting a new chat or restoring a saved chat preserves the current non-empty chat, and that deleting a saved chat removes it from history.
Test Mermaid text with a syntax error and confirm an error is shown and the preview canvas is hidden.
Verify that a generated diagram can still be inserted from its preview.
Check that the chat’s view-as-Mermaid action is available when a generated response is present.
Verify starting a new chat from a chat with messages leaves an empty conversation and clears its error state.
Check restoring a saved chat shows its messages and, when its last assistant message contains an error, restores the associated error state.
Confirm deleting the active chat while another saved chat remains switches to the first remaining chat, and deleting the final active chat leaves a blank conversation.

Test a streaming Mermaid response whose intermediate text ends with an incomplete connector such as "A -->" and whose final text completes the connector; confirm the completed diagram is previewed when generation finishes.
Verify switching to a completed chat with valid Mermaid content renders its preview, and switching to a chat with no assistant messages clears the preview.
Verify a prompt that produces Mermaid content split across multiple stream chunks results in a complete diagram preview.
Check an HTTP 429 response with a remaining-request count and confirm the dialog reports a rate-limit error and does not treat generation as successful; the error text is now “Rate limit exceeded.”
Verify submitting an empty prompt remains blocked with validation feedback and does not start generation.
Confirm Mermaid text ending in “A -->” or containing an unmatched “[” is not previewed, then complete the syntax and confirm preview rendering resumes.
Verify that an invalid Mermaid definition does not add elements to the drawing and that the conversion failure is communicated to the user.
Check a Mermaid definition large enough to trigger the former canvas-to-blob size error; confirm the preview is usable before treating it as insertable, or that a clear failure is shown.
Verify that clicking the backdrop closes the dialog and clicking within its content does not close it unexpectedly.
Confirm the command palette shows the updated history-style symbol and font selection shows the updated code-family symbol.
Verify a 2-character prompt is rejected, a 3-character prompt can generate, a 10,000-character prompt can generate, and a 10,001-character prompt is rejected.

Check that when the remaining limit is 0, submitting a valid 3-character prompt does not start generation; when generation succeeds, confirm the prompt and streamed reply appear in chat and valid Mermaid output converts into a diagram.
Confirm a 429 response with remaining limit 0 produces the exhausted-message-limit warning, while a 429 response with remaining limit greater than 0 produces the rate-limit warning.

Test an in-progress generation that is aborted and confirm it is not shown as a network or Mermaid-parsing failure; for a nested JSON parsing error containing two messages, confirm the chat error displays both on separate lines.
Check a conversation containing an empty assistant message and nonempty user messages; confirm generation proceeds using only nonempty user or assistant content.
Verify entering the prompt “Create a two-step flow from start to finish” and sending it produces a response in the chat that can be viewed as Mermaid.
Check selecting an assistant response with a valid Mermaid diagram for insertion adds its diagram elements to the drawing.
Confirm that, in a two-exchange chat, deleting the first assistant reply removes the messages from that point onward; confirm whether losing the later exchange is intended.

Test an empty Mermaid input while the Mermaid tab is active and confirm the preview is cleared; then preview a non-empty diagram with the editor in dark theme and confirm the preview reflects that theme.
uncertainty: Navigation to the text-to-diagram capability was not supplied, so the exact steps to open it are unknown.

The supplied context does not show which workflow hides parser details, and it provides no previous chat-saving behavior to compare against; confirm the expected error message in that workflow and whether the new save limits and title rules change prior behavior.

The supplied changes contain added code but no removed code, so there is no evidence to identify an exact input handled differently before and after; the checks verify the new behavior but cannot target a confirmed regression-specific input.

The previous submit handler enforced minimum and maximum prompt lengths, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether the replacement chat workflow preserves those limits; verify the empty-prompt case and confirm how overlong prompts are handled.
The removed canvas-to-blob check previously detected oversized previews, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether those previews remain usable or are still prevented from being inserted.

The supplied changes add these functions without showing prior implementations, so no input can be established as working before the change but behaving differently now; application navigation and visible labels were also not supplied.
The prior implementations are missing, so it is not possible to identify an input handled differently before and after this change or confirm that the empty-message check covers a regression.

The intended scope of deleting an assistant reply is unclear: the current behavior also removes the preceding prompt and later chat messages. The supplied changes do not include before-versions for the new chat actions, so an old-handled input that now behaves differently cannot be established for those actions.

report.summary: This release changes database startup validation, resource filtering and value handling, and command-line database initialization and file watching.
keyChanges: Server startup now rejects database data that is not a plain object or has a property name containing a slash.
Resource filters now compare values as strings and skip records when the filtered value is falsy, so a zero-valued field no longer matches a filter for zero.
Submitted form values and resource IDs are no longer converted from strings to native values before processing.
Starting with a missing JSON database now creates it with default data, and watched source or route files use directory change notifications to trigger reloads.
qaChecks: Verify that filtering the numeric field with a query value of 0 does not return the record whose field is 0.
Check a form-urlencoded create request with a field value of 0 and confirm the created value remains the string 0 rather than becoming the number 0.
Confirm startup creates the missing JSON database with default data and continues loading it.
Check startup with a database property name containing a slash and confirm startup rejects the data with an error instead of serving it.
uncertainty: The evidence does not establish a specific file-change input that behaves differently with the new directory watcher, so a targeted reload-regression check cannot be specified.

report.summary: The release improves frame-aware drawing and editing, including element placement, visual feedback, and browser support.
keyChanges: Canvas hit-testing now treats a nontransparent background as fill only for element types that support backgrounds; previously any element with a nontransparent background could be treated as filled, affecting clicks inside elements and which overlapping elements can receive arrow connections.

Frame highlighting now uses an explicit eligible-type list, and deselecting or finishing an element clears the highlight; verify permitted drawing tools can still highlight frames and stale highlights disappear.
Browsers missing several standard array methods now receive fallbacks, supporting the editor in those environments.
Adding a mixed selection to a frame now reorders already-contained elements together with newly added elements, while keeping attached text with its shape.
A single frame-associated element is now inserted at the end of the drawing order instead of at the frame’s position; batch insertion’s replacement behavior is not shown in the supplied changes.
Library-item copies and drops now use a frame-duplication path that preserves the original ordering of frame contents, so overlapping objects may stack differently from before.

Frame membership now considers the topmost object under the pointer, and dragging an existing frame child can retain its current frame; placement over an unrelated object above a frame can therefore differ from the previous topmost-frame-only behavior.

Text creation now checks the text’s final placement and gives a bindable container priority over a frame; frame highlights are also refreshed when new elements are inserted and cleared when the active tool changes.
Pasting or dropping drawing items now preserves the order of items inside copied frames; verify copied frame contents remain in their original order.
New elements, including pasted text, images, and embeddable items, are inserted in frame-aware positions rather than always being added at the end of the drawing.
Moving the pointer can update which frame is highlighted, except while creating or dragging elements or when the pointer is over a scrollbar.
The drawing renderer now selects which in-progress element to show on the preview canvas, so verify new elements display correctly as they are created.

report.summary: The release updates how the service starts, reloads data, and validates and handles requests.
keyChanges: Starting with a missing .json database source now creates that file with bundled example data before loading it; router setup errors are now printed and cause the process to exit with status 1.
Editing the watched routes file now restarts the server, while database and routes watching now use native directory file events instead of the previous watcher library.
Collection filters now skip records when the matched field is falsy, including numeric 0; zero-value searches may no longer return records they matched before.

Create and update requests no longer convert numeric-looking body strings to numbers, and individual-record lookups and deletions no longer convert URL IDs before matching. GET collection responses also build pagination links using a URL formatter; no changed link behavior is established by the evidence.

Request parsing and method override are now attached to the database router rather than the shared default middleware; method override runs before body parsing, which may affect requests that supply the override in a form body.

When a collection already contains a nonnumeric identifier, the next generated identifier changes from a UUID to a shortid-generated string; empty collections still start at 1 and numeric identifiers still increment.
Database contents are now validated during router setup, but the validation rules and resulting error behavior are not specified in the supplied evidence.

Nested GET and POST requests now pass the parent ID through unchanged instead of converting values such as "true" to booleans or numeric strings such as "1" to numbers; verify downstream filtering and association use the literal string.
New validation code accepts only plain objects and rejects top-level property names containing "/"; its connection to a runnable request path is not established.
Launching the new command-line entry point invokes the existing CLI argument handling; the remaining edits preserve the prior behavior.
qaChecks: Verify starting with a missing .json database path creates the file with bundled example data and starts the server.
Check that editing the watched routes file restarts the server and loads the updated routes; before this change, the edit was only logged.
Test replacing the watched JSON database file atomically with different contents and confirm the server reloads.
Verify a collection filter with the precise input score=0 still returns the record whose score is 0; this input matched before but is skipped by the new falsy-value check.
Check a request that creates or updates a record with the precise body value {"count":"7"} preserves count as the string "7", rather than converting it to the number 7.
Confirm an existing record with numeric ID 7 remains retrievable and deletable when its URL ID is "7".
Verify a URL-encoded request containing _method=DELETE is still treated as a DELETE request, as it was when body parsing ran before method override.
Confirm a database containing arrays or objects of records starts successfully and remains available for requests after startup validation.
Check that adding a record to a collection whose existing identifier is a string produces a shortid-generated string identifier rather than a UUID-shaped identifier.
Verify a nested GET using parent ID "true" filters by the literal string "true", not the boolean true.
Verify a nested POST using parent ID "1" associates the submitted record with the literal string "1", not the number 1.
Check that a plain object containing property "a/b" is rejected with an error identifying the unsupported slash in the property name.
Check that an array input is rejected because the data must be an object.
Verify launching the entry point with a source argument reaches the existing CLI argument handling.
uncertainty: The exact database input that makes router setup fail is not specified, so the new error-and-exit behavior has no concrete rejection case to verify from the supplied evidence; native file-watch event handling may also vary by platform.

The application context provides no API routes or navigation, and does not document whether numeric-looking body values are intended to remain strings; confirm that expectation. The changed lookup and filtering behavior also creates a regression risk for numeric IDs and zero-valued fields, which the checks should resolve.

Because method override now runs before form-body parsing, a URL-encoded _method=DELETE may no longer be recognized; verify this against the prior behavior. The supplied evidence also does not define startup validation rules or show whether consumers of the default middleware separately install the newly exported parsers.

No affected application surfaces or dependency paths are supplied for the new validation code or the removed JSON-file detection helper, so whether either is reachable through a user-facing flow cannot be confirmed.
No application navigation or role information was supplied, and there is no prior entry-point behavior to compare for a changed input boundary.

report.summary: The release overhauls console logging and reporting, changing how messages are formatted, colored, and written.
keyChanges: Error-marked logs now pass an error flag under a name the writer does not read, so they may be sent to normal output instead of the error stream.
Fancy log requests that clear the console now reach a writer without the options object it requires, risking an exception before the log is displayed.
The writing interface now accepts a named mode where it previously received an async flag; the effect on callers still using a boolean needs confirmation.
Reporter options now override defaults directly, so custom output and error streams can be honored.
The default log template now places the date and type first, followed by the tag, message, and additional details. The reporter routes entries to the configured output or error stream.
Console output can now be written in default, asynchronous, or synchronous mode; asynchronous mode waits for the stream’s drain event when a write reports backpressure.
New formatting utilities translate named placeholders into positional ones and format dates; new color utilities support named colors and hexadecimal colors.
A repeated request for the same background color returns the color cache instead of that color formatter, which may affect repeated background styling.
Log-type entries no longer suppress icons: a supplied icon is shown, or the default icon is used, so check output for an unexpected marker.
Badge coloring now uses a text-color style where it previously used a background-color style, which may change the badge’s visible appearance.
qaChecks: Verify a log marked as an error is written to the error stream and not the normal stream.
Check a fancy log request with clearing enabled clears the console and displays the log without throwing.
Confirm an asynchronous request using the previous value true waits for the stream’s drain event before completing.
Verify the exact input with distinct custom output and error streams in the reporter options: a normal entry reaches the custom output stream and an error entry reaches the custom error stream.
Check the default format with the prepared entry: confirm the output presents the date and type first, then the tag, message, and additional detail.
Verify mode='async' with a stream write result of false: the write waits for drain, then completes, with the supplied output written once.
Check mode='default' with the mode omitted: the supplied output is written once.
Confirm mode='sync' writes the supplied output to the stream’s file descriptor.
Verify format '%message$s' with an argument array whose fourth entry is 'hello' produces 'hello'.
Check date '2026-11-26' with format 'YYYY-MM-DD' produces '2026-11-26'.
Verify requesting the same background color twice applies that color both times and does not change the second result into cache data.
Verify a type "log" entry with the supplied icon "!" displays "!"; previously, this entry suppressed the icon.
Check a badge entry with color "red" and confirm whether its type label has the intended colored background; the new styling applies the color as a text color.
uncertainty: The previous async-selection behavior is not shown, so the expected result for callers that still pass true instead of the new named mode cannot be confirmed from the supplied evidence.

The supplied changes contain no prior implementation for comparison, so an input handled differently before and after cannot be established; the background-color cache’s repeat-use result is directly indicated by the new code, but no application surface consuming it is supplied.
The supplied context does not establish whether badge colors are intended to color the background or the text; the change switches from background styling to text styling.

report.summary: The release changes how whiteboards are displayed, navigated, saved, restored, and exported.
keyChanges: Elements are now rendered through per-element canvases, and the editor enables this optimization while export disables it; placement and appearance can therefore differ at fractional coordinates, so check both the live drawing and exported output.
Scrolling and automatic centering now round positions down to whole scene units, which can shift fractional positions by up to one unit.
Restoring a drawing now resets cached rendering data and defaults missing or falsy canvas offsets to zero, while local saving now includes selection-type elements previously excluded.
Normal redraws now use rendering optimizations, and resizing clears cached shapes so they can be redrawn for the new viewport.

Canvas-based export previews, PNGs, and clipboard images now use a floored scene offset instead of a separate offset; with default 10-unit padding and a leftmost bound of 0.5, the computed offset is 9.
Copied elements and locally saved drawings no longer include their canvas data, while undo and redo history records it as null; verify these drawing workflows still preserve the elements and edits.
Export positioning now floors the scroll offsets instead of retaining fractional offsets, so fractional drawing bounds can shift the exported content by less than one pixel.
Wheel scrolling, canvas panning, and scrollbar dragging now floor updated scroll positions to whole scene units, so small movements can shift the viewport differently than before.
New drawing elements start with empty rendering-cache data, and text elements clear any inherited cached shape before being added to a scene.
qaChecks: Verify the element at x + horizontal scroll = 10.7 appears at whole-pixel placement and remains visible, then pan and zoom and confirm it does not disappear or become misaligned from the other elements.
Check the exported drawing includes the fractionally positioned element and that its placement remains consistent with the drawing canvas.
Verify the exported drawing is not clipped and has 9.5 pixels of space at its top and left bounds, reflecting floored offsets of 9 rather than the former fractional 9.5.
Verify that a horizontal wheel movement of 0.2 units from a position of 0 results in a whole-unit position of -1, and that centering which computes -0.2 also results in -1.
Check that loading a drawing with missing canvas-offset values displays its elements in the correct positions.
Confirm that resizing the viewport while a drawing is open redraws its shapes and preserves their appearance.
Ensure that edits and redraws continue to display the complete drawing without missing shapes.
Check that saving and reopening a drawing containing a selection-type element preserves the intended drawing contents without displaying an unintended temporary selection artifact.
Check the export preview and a PNG or clipboard export: the computed scene offset should be 9, and the complete drawing should remain visible without clipped edges.
Verify copying a selected shape and pasting it preserves the shape in the drawing.
Check undoing and redoing an edit restores the expected drawing each time.
Confirm the drawing remains intact after saving locally and reopening the editor.

Verify at zoom 1 and the starting viewport position that wheel movement of +0.5 pixels on both axes shifts the visible scene by one whole scene unit, while movement of -0.5 pixels on both axes leaves the viewport at its starting position.
Check at zoom 1.5 that dragging the canvas left by 1 pixel and dragging the horizontal scrollbar right by 1 pixel each move the viewport by a whole scene unit rather than a fractional amount.
Confirm that pasting text into a drawing with an existing element displays the text and leaves it selectable after moving it.
uncertainty: The supplied evidence establishes whole-pixel rounding for fractional placement but does not establish whether the resulting visual difference is noticeable at ordinary zoom levels.

The change now saves selection-type elements that were previously excluded, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether such elements are intended drawing content or temporary interaction artifacts.

The supplied paste flow already creates text from an element with an empty shape, so the evidence does not identify a user input that changes visibly because text now clears an inherited shape; the visible purpose of the added rendering-cache defaults is also not established.
