report.summary: The release makes rotated drawings work consistently throughout editing and export.
keyChanges: Scene bounds now use the four rotated corners of each element instead of its unrotated coordinates, affecting export framing, centering, and placement when elements are rotated.
Selected elements gain rotation-aware handles and outlines, including a rotation control for text; drawing and export rendering now apply element rotation.
Elements can now be rotated on the canvas; holding Shift snaps rotation to 22.5° increments, and text editing follows the element’s angle.
Resizing now accounts for an element’s rotation; with Shift held, corner resizing sets the height to the resulting width rather than the element’s original width.
Restored elements without a saved angle default to 0°, and the temporary rotation-in-progress state is excluded from saved editor state.
Element hit testing now compensates for an element’s angle, changing which rotated shapes, text, and lines are found by pointer actions.
Text editing now follows the text element’s angle, and new elements receive an angle of 0 by default.
Resize guidance is now shown only for mouse input, while rotation guidance is shown during mouse rotation.
SVG rendering now applies each element’s rotation around its center for shapes, lines and arrows, and text; a 90° rotation that was previously omitted should now appear in exported output.
qaChecks: Verify the 45-degree shape’s selection outline and resize handles align with its rotated orientation, and dragging its rotation control rotates the shape.
Check that selecting rotated text shows a rotation control, that dragging it rotates the text, and that text has no resize controls.
Confirm that pasting the rotated shape places its rotated bounds centered at the pointer location.
Verify an image export includes the complete rotated shape without clipping its corners and preserves its rotated appearance.
Verify dragging a selected element’s rotation control rotates it, and dragging with Shift held snaps its angle to 22.5° increments.

Check the changed Shift-resize behavior using the 100-by-60 rectangle: drag its southeast corner 20 scene units to the right with Shift held; the result should be 120-by-120, rather than the old behavior’s 120-by-100.
Confirm resizing a rotated rectangle from a corner follows the rotated element’s local direction and keeps the opposite corner anchored.
Verify editing the rotated text keeps the editing text aligned with the element’s angle.
Check that loading the drawing with no angle value restores that element at 0°, and that a drawing with a rotated element retains its angle after saving and restoring.

Verify that clicking near a rotated corner of the 100-by-40 rectangle, beyond its original unrotated top or bottom edge but on the visible rotated shape, selects it; the rotated shape should be found.
Check that editing the angled text element places the text editor at its center and rotates it to match the element’s angle.
Confirm that mouse resizing shows resize guidance and mouse rotation shows rotation guidance; touch resizing should not show the resize guidance.
Verify an SVG export shows all three elements rotated around their centers; the previous behavior exported them without rotation.
Check copying the same drawing as a PNG preserves the 90° rotations in the copied image.
uncertainty: Navigation and the specific way to create rotated elements were not supplied, so testing requires existing nonzero-angle elements or suitable prepared test data.

report.summary: The release makes grouping and ungrouping more consistent across diagram editing and keyboard help.
keyChanges: Selecting elements by clicking or marquee can now select their group as well, with nested-group selection scoped to the group currently being edited; group selection also feeds scene selection rendering and related export rendering.

Canvas clicks now preserve element selection when a group is selected, while clicking empty canvas clears element selection, group selection, and group-editing state; creating groups while editing also inserts the new group before the active group in the hierarchy.
Duplicating selected elements while editing a group now passes group context and a shared ID map into duplication, so verify copies retain appropriate group relationships.
Double-clicking an element in a selected group now enters editing for that group rather than starting text editing, while clicking outside the group or clearing selection exits group editing.

Pasting while editing a group now duplicates elements with group-aware membership, and switching to a drawing tool, releasing Space while using one, or starting text editing clears group selection and editing state.
Restored elements without group information now receive an empty group membership, so group checks can safely include older drawings.
Duplicating grouped elements now gives the copies new group identities while keeping copied group members together, so copies can remain grouped without joining the original group.
Select all now clears active group editing and applies group-aware selection to non-deleted elements.
Selecting at least two elements and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G groups them; pressing Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G ungroups selected groups, while grouping fewer than two elements does nothing.
Selected groups and groups being edited receive one selection outline around their combined bounds rather than separate local outlines for each selected member.
The shortcut reference adds Group (Cmd+G on Apple platforms, Ctrl+G elsewhere) and Ungroup (Cmd+Shift+G on Apple platforms, Ctrl+Shift+G elsewhere), making these combinations visible to editors.
qaChecks: Verify that after selecting a group, clicking one of its elements without dragging keeps the group and its elements selected.
Check that after entering a nested group and marquee-selecting an element inside it, selection applies to the appropriate group level without selecting the edited group itself.
Confirm that while editing a group, duplicating a selected element preserves the copy’s appropriate group relationship.
Ensure that clicking empty canvas while a group is selected and being edited clears the group selection and exits group editing.
Verify that after selecting a group, double-clicking one of its elements enters group editing and selects that element instead of starting text editing.
Check that clicking an element outside the group exits group editing, while selecting an element inside the group keeps editing within that group.
Confirm that pasting multiple copied elements while editing a group keeps the pasted elements associated with the intended group.
Verify that switching to a drawing tool, releasing Space while using a drawing tool, or starting text editing clears group selection and editing state.
Verify that opening the older drawing with no group information succeeds and its elements can be selected on the canvas.
Check that opening the drawing with existing groups preserves group selection and editing.
Verify duplicating two elements from the same group creates copies that remain grouped with each other but are separate from the original group.
Check duplicating grouped elements while editing a nested group keeps the copies in the active group and preserves their nesting.
Confirm Ctrl+A while editing a group exits group editing and selects all non-deleted elements.
Test pasting grouped elements into the drawing and confirm copied group members remain grouped without joining the original group.
Verify selecting two elements and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G groups them and shows one selection outline around the group's combined bounds.
Check that pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G with only one element selected does not group it.
Confirm selecting a group and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G ungroups it, leaving its elements individually selectable.
Verify the shortcut reference lists Group as Cmd+G on Apple platforms or Ctrl+G elsewhere, and Ungroup as Cmd+Shift+G on Apple platforms or Ctrl+Shift+G elsewhere.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not specify the exact expected nesting of duplicated elements; confirm that a duplicate remains grouped consistently with its original.
The supplied changes add these behaviors without showing a previous implementation, so no concrete input that worked before but behaves differently now can be identified.
This change documents the shortcuts, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether pressing them performs grouping or ungrouping.

report.summary: The release makes line and arrow editing more complete and consistent, from adjusting points to finishing changes.
keyChanges: While editing a line or arrow, dragging a point now moves it directly; Alt-clicking or Alt-dragging adds a point at the pointer, and releasing an endpoint near the opposite endpoint can close a path with at least three points.
Point-list updates with the same number of points are now ignored when the compared points match, avoiding redundant drawing updates; however, a change limited to the first point may also be missed.

Double-clicking or pressing Enter with exactly one line, arrow, or freehand line selected now enters point-editing mode instead of the previous double-click text-editing behavior; point handles appear on the selected element.
While point editing is active, pointer input is routed to line-point editing rather than the usual selection and resize handling, and deselecting the element triggers finalization.
The new editing state starts inactive and is excluded from saved local editor state, so reopening should not resume an in-progress point edit.

Entering point editing normalizes a line or arrow’s point coordinates while adjusting its position, and point handles are calculated using the element’s rotation; verify the drawing stays visually aligned.

While editing, Alt-click adds a point, Alt-pointer movement previews an uncommitted point, and releasing Alt removes that preview; dragging a loop endpoint preserves the join when the pointer is released.
Resize-handle hit detection now receives scene pointer coordinates separately; verify handle selection and resizing still follow the pointer.
When exactly one line, arrow, or free-draw element is selected, the editor can show line-editing guidance, with different guidance depending on whether a point is selected.
Undo/redo history now records entering or leaving editing on a linear element, but does not create a separate entry for changes within the same element’s editing state.
Shortcut text now replaces CtrlOrCmd, Alt, Del, Enter, and Return only when each token is a whole word, preventing replacements inside longer words.
When a line or arrow point changes, its bounds are now calculated from the generated curve and used to adjust its position; verify that editing points keeps the drawing placed as expected.
The drawing now keeps an ID-based element lookup, and deleted or missing elements are treated as unavailable to point-editing interactions.

When a line is being edited at an active point, Delete removes that point instead of deleting selected drawing objects; if the line has fewer than two points, it removes the line and exits point editing.
Escape now finishes line-point editing directly, removing the line if it has fewer than two points or is invisibly small, and otherwise keeping it in the drawing.
qaChecks: Verify dragging a middle point moves that point while the other vertices remain in place.
Check Alt-clicking a line or arrow at a new location adds a point there, and Alt-dragging moves the added point with the pointer.
Confirm dragging either endpoint of a path with at least three points to within the endpoint-closing threshold, then releasing, joins the endpoints and closes the path.
Verify a same-length point list where only the first coordinate changes retains that change in the drawing.

Verify the precise input of exactly one selected line followed by a double-click, and separately exactly one selected line followed by Enter: point-editing handles should appear instead of starting text editing.
Check that clicking a line point or the line while editing changes or adds points as appropriate, and that deselecting the line ends point editing while retaining the edit.
Confirm that after editing a line and reloading the drawing, its drawing content remains but point-editing mode and its handles do not resume.
Check an image export made while a line is in point-editing mode; the exported drawing should contain the diagram without the red and white editing handles.
Verify that entering point editing on a rotated line or arrow whose first point has nonzero local coordinates leaves the drawing in the same visual position and places point handles on its vertices.
Check that, while editing a line or arrow, Alt-pointer movement previews a point, releasing Alt removes that uncommitted preview, and Alt-click adds a point.
Confirm that dragging either endpoint of a closed line or arrow with at least three points and releasing the pointer leaves the endpoints joined.
Test pointer interaction at a selected element’s visible resize handle and verify the expected handle is selected and resizing follows the pointer.
Verify that selecting exactly one line or arrow outside point-editing mode shows line-editing guidance.
Check point-selection guidance with active point index 0 and then 1: index 0 should show the nothing-selected guidance, while index 1 should show the point-selected guidance.
Test history by entering editing on a selected line or arrow, then undoing and redoing; confirm history returns to the corresponding prior and restored editing states.
Verify that shortcut text containing the exact string CtrlOrCmdEnter is not normalized as a whole-word token; separated text such as CtrlOrCmd+Enter should still be normalized.
Verify that dragging the first point of each element updates the drawing while the remaining points stay in their expected relative positions.
Check that deleting a line or arrow removes it from the canvas and that it cannot be edited afterward.
Verify that with the first point active on a two-point line, pressing Delete removes that point rather than deleting selected drawing objects, and leaves the line in point-editing mode.
Check that with the single point active on a one-point line, pressing Delete removes the line and exits point editing.
Confirm that pressing Escape while editing a one-point line removes it and ends point editing, while pressing Escape on a valid line with at least two points ends point editing and keeps the line.
uncertainty: The update comparison skips the first point, so a same-length point update that changes only that coordinate may be ignored; the supplied application context does not establish whether normal editor actions can produce this input.
The renderer is also used for image exports and now draws point handles when a line is being edited; confirm whether those editing handles are intended to appear in exports.

The supplied evidence has no earlier implementation for the line-editing behavior, and the resize-coordinate change provides no input that is shown to behave differently before and after; a concrete regression input handled by the old version but differently by the new version cannot be identified.
The supplied context does not identify a UI path or a user-provided input for shortcut text, so it is unclear how QA can exercise the changed whole-word formatting case through the application.

The supplied diff does not show the previous point-bounds calculation, so it does not establish a concrete input that the old behavior handled differently; the precise regression case for this change remains unclear.

report.summary: The release adds an optional whiteboard grid that guides drawing and editing and is preserved in saved work.
keyChanges: When the drawing state has a non-null grid size, the canvas renderer draws grid lines; a new default state leaves the grid off, and the grid setting is included in drawing JSON when saved or exported.
The Shortcuts dialog now lists Ctrl/Cmd+' for toggling grid mode; the grid spacing constant is 20.
When text resizing does not fit after two measurements, it now tries once more at 99% of the second candidate font size before giving up, so some close-fit resizes may now succeed.
Drawing and selection movement use shared element operations; the supplied evidence does not establish a different user-visible outcome for these operations.

Grid mode can now be toggled from the blank-canvas context menu or with a Ctrl/Cmd keyboard shortcut; with the grid enabled, shape and line placement, selection dragging, and resizing snap to grid positions.
Freehand drawing continues to use the pointer’s unsnapped positions, while arrow-key movement in grid mode moves a selection by one grid interval for a regular arrow press.
qaChecks: Verify the enabled-grid drawing displays grid lines and its PNG export includes the grid.
Check that saving or exporting the enabled-grid drawing preserves its grid setting, then reload it and confirm the grid remains enabled.
Confirm that loading the older drawing without a grid-size setting leaves the grid off.
Verify the dialog lists Ctrl/Cmd+' as the shortcut for toggling grid mode.
Verify text resizing at a target size that the first two font measurements fail to fit but the additional 1%-smaller candidate fits; confirm the resize completes and the text remains visible.
Check a newly drawn shape dragged to zero width or zero height; confirm it is not updated until both dimensions are nonzero.
Confirm dragging a multi-element selection preserves the elements’ relative positions and moves the selection’s top-left corner to the pointer position.
Verify that right-clicking a blank canvas opens a context menu with a grid-mode toggle, and that using it switches grid mode on and off.
Check shape creation with grid mode on by placing the pointer one-quarter of a grid interval past an intersection; confirm the shape starts at the intersection rather than the pointer position.
Confirm that dragging and resizing a selected shape with grid mode on snaps its position or size to grid intervals, including when the pointer is one-quarter of an interval past an intersection.
Test one regular arrow-key press on a selected shape with grid mode on; confirm it moves by one grid interval.
uncertainty: The supplied changes show the shortcut being listed but do not show the action that handles it, so whether Ctrl/Cmd+' actually toggles the grid is not established here.

The evidence does not provide a concrete text-and-size fixture that fails the first two measurements but fits the third, and it contains no prior implementation for the extracted drawing operations; therefore their exact before-and-after user-visible differences cannot be established.
The grid interval and the displayed key for the Ctrl/Cmd shortcut are not supplied, so the exact keyboard input and numeric positions for these checks cannot be specified.

report.summary: The release overhauls shared drawing sessions and embedded-editor behavior, changing how scenes load, sync, and are shared with participants.
keyChanges: Scene restoration now accepts null imported data and supplies an empty drawing with restored default settings instead of failing when data is absent.

New encrypted sharing and collaboration paths load private-key-protected drawing data while retaining a legacy JSON import path; live collaboration scene and participant updates also use encrypted messages.

The previous scene-sync and conflict-reconciliation implementations were removed, but the supplied evidence does not show their replacements, so verify that joining and concurrent editing still preserve the drawing.
The editor now initializes stored or linked drawings through a collaboration-aware wrapper; verify the drawing and collaboration state load correctly on startup.
Pointer updates are now sent through the editor’s callback even during multi-pointer gestures, where live collaboration previously suppressed broadcasts.
The embedded editor now defaults omitted width or height to the browser window, and scene updates can omit elements while applying supported background or collaborator changes.

Scene setup now considers saved drawing content and a recent same-room marker when deciding whether to load an external scene without a confirmation; collaboration-room loading and live change broadcasts are also handled in the showcase app.
Editor changes are saved locally after a 300 ms debounce, and are broadcast when live collaboration is active; the supplied diff does not establish whether this differs from the prior behavior.

The desktop canvas actions and mobile canvas menu replace the room dialog with a collaboration button; it appears only when a click handler is provided, shows a participant count only above zero, and reflects whether collaboration is active.
Live pointer updates no longer include which drawing elements the sender has selected.

The editor no longer contains its former collaboration-link setup, incoming-scene handling, and leave-time save protection; confirm those collaboration outcomes remain available after the responsibility shift.
Creating a collaboration session previously removed deleted drawing elements before sharing; verify drawings that had deleted content do not expose it to people joining the session.
The embedded-editor contract now allows optional dimensions and null or promised starting data, and provides a readiness signal and additional scene controls.

A joining participant’s initial drawing and periodic full-scene updates are now supplied by the collaboration wrapper, while scene version tracking is handled there; verify that shared drawings still synchronize and remain current for all participants.

Remote drawing reconciliation now checks the wrapper’s most recently captured editor state to protect an element being edited, resized, or dragged; confirm a concurrent remote update does not overwrite that local interaction.

Live collaboration now gets participant selection data from the editor state and sends an empty selection when that state is unavailable, which may affect the selection shown alongside a participant’s pointer.

The embeddable editor now passes through collaboration-button, collaboration-status, pointer-update, and editor-reference props; the previous username-change callback is no longer passed through under that prop.
Starting a session creates a collaboration link and clears prior undo history while retaining the current drawing; ending the session saves it and returns the address to the site origin.
Collaborators’ drawing updates are reconciled and displayed without rebroadcasting the received scene, and each incoming update clears the local undo history.
The room dialog supports copying the active link, editing the participant name, and closing or ending a session; copied links are selected in the field, and clipboard failures display an error.
Pointer updates are sent only when fewer than two pointers are active and a collaboration socket is available.
qaChecks: Verify that opening a collaboration link with a room ID and key joins the same drawing in both sessions and that edits and participant presence appear in the other session.
Check that the collaboration controls still let a user start and stop a session, copy its link, and set a name; the previous implementation for these controls was removed from the supplied changes.
Verify that a fresh editor with no initial or local drawing data (null data) opens with an empty drawing and default settings instead of failing.

Verify a drawing change made by one participant appears for the other participant.
Check that a participant moving two pointers at once still sends pointer updates and that the other participant continues to see synchronized drawing changes.
Verify that when a second participant joins, the existing drawing appears for them and subsequent drawing changes from either participant appear in the other session.
Check that while one participant is editing, resizing, or dragging an element, a remote update to that same element does not replace the in-progress local interaction.
Check that a participant with no selected elements still has their pointer visible to the other participant, without showing a selection.
Verify that a participant with an element selected has that selection reflected in the collaboration update.
Verify that omitting width and height gives the editor the browser window’s width and height.
Check that applying a background-color-only scene update with no elements leaves the existing drawing intact.
Verify that opening a collaboration link with no saved drawing loads the shared scene without asking to replace local content.
Check that opening a collaboration link with a saved drawing and no recent same-room marker asks for confirmation before replacing it.
Confirm that opening the same room again with its marker less than 15 seconds old skips the confirmation and loads the shared scene.
Test a drawing edit during a live session and confirm the change is saved locally and appears for another participant.
Verify that an edit remains in the drawing after waiting at least 300 ms and reloading the editor.
Verify that when the collaboration click handler is omitted, the collaboration button is absent; when supplied, the button appears and clicking it invokes the configured collaboration entry point.

Check the collaboration button with zero participants and then one participant: show no count at zero and show 1 when there is one; confirm its active appearance reflects whether collaboration is in progress.
Test pointer movement while a drawing element is selected in one session; confirm the other participant still receives live pointer updates and synchronized scene edits.
Verify opening a collaboration link with a non-empty hash loads the shared drawing and that a change made in one window appears in the other.
Check that an element deleted before creating the collaboration link is absent when another participant joins.

Confirm that after making a collaborative edit and immediately attempting to leave, the latest drawing is recoverable when reopening the session and the browser offers a chance to stay if a save is still pending.
Verify the editor becomes ready after the starting-data promise resolves and displays the supplied drawing when it resolves with drawing data.
Check that a null starting-data result still allows the editor to become ready and be used.
Verify that when the integration supplies a collaboration-status value of true and a pointer-update handler, the handler receives pointer updates while the editor is in use.
Confirm that omitting the collaboration-button handler still allows the editor to render and be used.
Verify that after deleting an object and starting a session, the second participant sees the current drawing without the deleted object.
Check that a new drawing change in either session appears in the other session, and that receiving a remote change does not cause repeated or duplicate scene updates.
Confirm that after a remote drawing update arrives, the receiving session reflects it and its earlier undo history is cleared.
Test pointer sharing with fewer than two active pointers and then with two or more; pointer updates should be shared only in the fewer-than-two case.
Verify that starting a session produces a link that can be copied and used by the second browser session to join.
Check that clicking the link field selects its contents, and that the copy control places the full displayed link on the clipboard.
Confirm that entering a participant name and reopening the room dialog retains that name.
Verify that ending the session clears the active collaboration state and returns the address to the site origin.
uncertainty: The supplied changes remove the earlier full-scene join broadcast, conflict-resolution rules, and room-dialog implementation without showing their replacements; confirm that new participants receive the drawing and simultaneous edits do not lose changes.

The editor no longer performs its own socket cleanup during unload; the supplied evidence does not establish whether the collaboration wrapper reliably handles that transition, so verify that reloading or leaving a session does not leave stale collaboration state.

The supplied evidence shows substantial moves and newly supplied scene-handling code but does not include the prior implementations for a reliable before-and-after comparison; no concrete input that is proven to take a different old path can be identified.

Because pointer updates no longer carry selected-element information, it is unclear whether collaborators are still expected to see another participant’s selection; verify the intended selection display in a shared session.

The supplied changes remove the editor’s previous collaboration setup, remote updates, and unload-save logic, but do not show whether the replacement preserves those behaviors; link loading, deleted-content privacy, and recovery of unsaved shared changes need confirmation.

The wrapper’s editor-state snapshot is refreshed when drawing changes are broadcast; it is unclear whether it is always current at the instant a remote update arrives, so concurrent editing is the highest-risk check.

The supplied before-and-after evidence does not establish a specific input that the previous collaboration-selection update handled differently, and it does not include prior implementations for the relocated link-generation code; regression expectations for those cases remain unclear.
The supplied changes contain no removed code or prior-behavior rules, so there is no supported concrete input that demonstrates what worked before but behaves differently now.

report.summary: The release changes how drawings are positioned and edited to account for the canvas viewport.
keyChanges: Pointer and drawing-position mapping now includes the canvas’s left and top offsets, affecting placement, selection, and other canvas interactions when the editor is offset within its host.
The on-screen text editor’s zoom transform now also accounts for those offsets, so verify text remains aligned with its drawing while editing.
The editor now measures and retains the canvas’s screen offsets during startup, resizing, and scene updates, and uses them when positioning the canvas and centering loaded scenes.

Dropping a drawing file now uses the current editor state to recenter its contents in the current canvas instead of relying only on the file’s saved view; the shared restore step also no longer has its former optional scroll-to-content behavior.
Loading a drawing file now calculates its scroll position using the current editor view, so test files whose saved view differs from the active editor.
Shared-scene imports no longer force the view to scroll to the drawing; they restore the imported view state instead.
Browser storage and drawing-file exports are configured to omit the new canvas offsets, so these values are not retained with saved drawings.

Node-based canvas export now supplies top and left offsets of 0 rather than leaving them absent, establishing an explicit zero-offset starting point. The type additions alone do not establish further runtime changes.
qaChecks: Verify clicking the displayed center of the shape at this nonzero canvas offset selects the shape at that location, rather than a different drawing position.
Check that pasting an element with the pointer over the canvas places it at the pointer’s displayed location with the 40 px left and 30 px top offsets.
Confirm that editing the existing text at 150% zoom keeps the text editor aligned with the text on the canvas, including when the canvas has both nonzero offsets.
Verify dropping the prepared file recenters its elements in the current canvas, even when the file’s saved view would leave them off-screen.
Check loading a non-collaboration scene with elements outside its saved viewport; confirm the elements are brought into view using the current canvas dimensions and position.
Confirm the loaded scene remains correctly positioned after the editor’s width or height changes.
Verify importing that file positions the drawing using the active editor view, rather than the file’s saved scroll offsets.
Check that importing the shared scene uses its saved viewport state instead of automatically scrolling to center the drawing.
Check that browser-saved and drawing-file data omit the top and left offsets while the drawing remains available to reopen.
Verify a Node-based canvas export with both offsets set to 0 renders the drawing without an offset-related position shift.
uncertainty: The removed restore-time recentering applied only when an optional scroll-to-content setting was true; no supplied caller shows that setting being used, so the affected user workflow is unclear.
No user-produced input is supplied that distinguishes the old absent offsets from the new zero offsets, and no in-app navigation for these checks is provided.

report.summary: The release improves whiteboard editing by making it easier to select shapes and keep connecting lines attached as diagrams change.
keyChanges: Arrow connections now use explicit rules for which elements can be connected and which shapes can receive a connection; hovering, creating, editing, moving, resizing, and removing connections use this binding logic.
Canvas hit-testing and connection geometry now use updated calculations for element positions and rotations, which can affect selecting elements and where arrows meet shapes.

Canvas hit detection now uses shared shape-distance checks instead of the previous per-shape rules; notably, unselected text with a transparent background may no longer respond to clicks well inside its bounds as it did before.
Arrow binding and its on-canvas suggestions now use shape-aware distances and a gap of at least 15, at most 80, or 25% of the smaller shape dimension between those limits.
Linear-element editing handles are now filled circles rather than outlined squares, and suggested arrow connections are highlighted on the canvas.
The supplied geometry and transform calculations feed canvas hit-testing and arrow binding, so verify that selecting elements and connecting arrows still targets the intended shapes.
The same calculations reach updates when bound elements move or resize, so confirm that connected arrows continue to meet their shapes after those edits.
Arrow binding suggestions now respond to pointer position; holding Ctrl or Command disables binding, and releasing the modifier or leaving the editor restores it.
Duplicating connected drawing elements now repairs connections between the copies, and deleting bound text now updates its connected arrows.
Text editing, group entry, and context-menu targeting now use the editor’s element hit-testing path; the supplied evidence does not establish a specific changed pointer outcome.
The supplied connection logic avoids binding both ends of a simple two-point connector to the same shape and recalculates attached endpoints when a shape moves or resizes.
Arrows and other linear elements can suggest and establish connections to shapes while drawing or moving endpoints, and connections are updated as elements move or resize.
Deleting a connected shape or a linear element endpoint now clears the corresponding connection instead of leaving a reference to the removed target.
Copying connected elements and Alt-dragging selections now adjust connections so copied elements can stay connected to their matching copies.
New lines and arrows can connect their endpoints to nearby shapes when drawing is finished, with connection behavior enabled by default.
Duplicating a connected line and its shape together now preserves the connection in the copied pair.
Undo and redo now repair connections when a connected shape is removed, while loading saved drawings now restores saved line and arrow endpoint connections.
Restoration now preserves falsy non-null group ID values instead of replacing them with an empty list, which may affect drawings containing malformed group data.
Arrow connection points are recalculated using shape-specific geometry, so check that connections remain correctly placed on rectangles, diamonds, text, and ellipses as shapes move or resize.
Pointer hit detection and shape-boundary intersection calculations have also changed, so check that selecting elements and connecting arrows still works at shape edges.
qaChecks: Verify that drawing an arrow from a rectangle to an ellipse connects its ends to the shapes, and that the connection suggestion appears when an arrow endpoint is over a shape.
Check that dragging or resizing a shape with a connected arrow keeps the arrow attached at the appropriate shape boundary.
Confirm that moving an existing arrow endpoint onto a different shape updates the connection, and moving it away removes the old connection.
Test selecting a rotated shape by clicking inside it and clicking outside it, and confirm the selection handles match its visible bounds.
Verify that clicking well inside the transparent text element, away from its border, still selects it or opens text editing; the previous behavior hit anywhere within the text bounds.

Check arrow binding on the 40-by-40 rectangle by moving an arrow endpoint to 14 scene units from its edge and then to exactly 15; confirm the suggestion appears inside the 15-unit gap and not at the strict boundary.

Confirm that moving an arrow endpoint near a rectangle, diamond, and ellipse shows the suggested-connection highlight around the shape or relevant arrow endpoint, and that completing the connection attaches the arrow.
Verify that selecting a line or arrow shows filled circular point handles and that dragging a handle still changes the line or arrow point.
Verify clicking the visible edge of the rotated rectangle selects the rectangle rather than an unrelated element.
Check that clicking the ellipse selects it and that clicking empty canvas does not select either shape.
Confirm that connecting the arrow to an off-center point on the rotated shape places its endpoint at the shape boundary.
Verify that moving and resizing the connected shape keeps the arrow attached at the boundary.
Verify that moving an arrow endpoint over the rectangle suggests a connection and completing the arrow connects it to the rectangle.

Check the changed modifier behavior: hold Ctrl or Command while drawing an arrow endpoint over the rectangle and confirm it does not connect; release the modifier and draw another arrow to the rectangle, confirming it connects.
Test changing away from the arrow tool while an unfinished arrow endpoint is over the rectangle and confirm the endpoint connects when the tool changes.
Ensure that after the editor loses focus and regains it, drawing an arrow toward the rectangle can connect again.
Verify that copying and pasting the connected rectangle-and-arrow pair creates a copied pair whose arrow connects to the copied rectangle, while the original pair remains connected.
Check the deletion case: edit the connected text element, remove all its text, and submit; confirm its connected arrow is no longer left bound to the deleted text.
Verify that when one end of a two-point connector is attached to a rectangle, moving its free end over that same rectangle does not attach the second end there.
Check that dragging and resizing a shape with an attached connector keeps the attached endpoint connected to the shape.
Verify that drawing an arrow with its endpoint over a shape shows a connection suggestion and releasing there connects the arrow to the shape.
Check that dragging an arrow endpoint onto a different shape and releasing updates the connection to that shape.
Confirm that after holding Alt to preview a new point, releasing Alt to discard it, then holding Alt and clicking elsewhere adds a fresh point at the new location.
Verify that dragging the connected shape moves its arrow endpoint with it.
Check that resizing or rotating the connected shape keeps the arrow attached to the shape.
Confirm that dragging or resizing a selection containing connected shapes and arrows keeps their connections aligned.
Verify that deleting the connected shape leaves the arrow without a connection to the deleted shape.
Check that deleting an arrow’s first or last point clears that endpoint’s connection.
Confirm that copying a connected shape and arrow, then Alt-dragging a connected selection, keeps copied connections with the corresponding copied elements and leaves the originals connected.
Verify that finishing an arrow with its endpoints on a nearby rectangle connects the arrow to that rectangle.
Check that selecting a connected rectangle and arrow together and pressing Ctrl+D creates a copied pair that remains connected.
Verify that deleting the rectangle and then using undo restores the rectangle and its connection to the arrow.
Check that redoing the deletion removes the rectangle without leaving the arrow connected to the removed shape.
Confirm that loading the drawing with a saved arrow connection retains the connection.
Check that the legacy drawing with an empty-string group ID opens and its elements can still be selected and edited.
Verify that an arrow connected to an ellipse with its adjacent point exactly level with the ellipse center attaches to the ellipse boundary and stays attached when the ellipse is moved or resized.
Check that arrows connected to rectangles, diamonds, and text remain on the appropriate shape boundary after moving and resizing those shapes.
Confirm that clicking a visible shape near its boundary selects the intended element, and that an arrow can be connected to each supported shape type.

report.summary: The release makes text attached to shapes more consistent throughout editing and export.
keyChanges: Text attached to shapes now wraps within its container while editing and after saving, keeps the entered text for later editing, and can grow or shrink its container as the text changes.
Text sizing now accounts for line height and empty lines, so verify text spacing and fit after editing or changing its font.
When text overlaps a shape, text is ignored while locating the underlying container, helping editing continue to target the attached text and its shape.

Ordinary canvas hit-testing and marquee selection now exclude text attached to a shape, while text editing can still find it; double-clicking a selected shape that has attached text targets that text instead of creating separate text.
Starting text at a container’s center can attach it to the container, and committing edits recalculates text dimensions; keyboard submission selects the container when editing its attached text.
Duplicating a shape with attached text now preserves the attachment on the copy, and transparent shapes with attached text can be dragged from their interior.

Resizing a shape with attached text now reflows the text to the available width, adjusts its position and height, and uses the container width when measuring text; verify long content remains visible.
Attached text now follows its shape when the shape is rotated, including when multiple elements are rotated together.

Resizing a shape with attached text now rejects negative dimensions and prevents its width from shrinking below the estimated minimum needed for a line of text; adding text to a shape also enforces minimum width and height.
Copying a selected shape now includes its attached text, so copying or cutting a shape should preserve the complete shape-and-text unit.

Interior dragging now treats alpha-transparent fills such as #00000000 as transparent; shapes with attached text remain draggable from inside, while shapes without attached text are not draggable by their transparent interior.

Editing attached text now measures it within the text element’s width and can expand its container when the text exceeds the available space, adding 30 pixels of padding on each side; text updates can also leave dimensions unchanged when recalculation is not requested.
Arrows can no longer treat text already attached to a shape or image as a binding target; standalone text remains eligible.
Selecting one rectangle, diamond, ellipse, or image now shows a hint about binding text to that element. Line and arrow selection guidance remains available.
Text created by clicking a shape is positioned at its center, while the existing keyboard action for adding text to a selected shape now explicitly enables attachment.
Dragging an ungrouped shape also moves its attached text; pasted or inserted copies now restore the shape-to-text attachment and select only standalone text.
Selecting a shape for image export or adding it to the Library now includes its attached text.
Restored text without attachment metadata now receives explicit standalone-text and empty-original-text defaults.

Text attached to a shape or connector now uses approximate font line height when drawn, instead of dividing the text element’s height evenly among its lines; this changes the spacing of bound text in the canvas and rendered exports.
Selecting a shape now also includes its bound text for grouping, deletion, duplication, PNG/SVG clipboard copying, and adding the selection to the Library.
Duplicating a shape with bound text now duplicates and rebinds the text to the new shape, while the duplicate selection does not select bound text independently.
Select All no longer selects bound text as a separate element, and grouping eligibility now counts bound text included with a selected shape.
qaChecks: Verify that, in the narrow shape, entering one unbroken word longer than the available text width wraps it within the shape and the shape grows as needed; after saving and reopening, the entered text is still available and displays wrapped.
Check that removing enough text from an expanded shape lets the shape shrink, and that changing the attached text’s font size or family keeps the text within the shape.

Confirm that text entered as “\nA\n” retains its leading and trailing blank-line spacing, and that starting to edit text overlapping its shape edits the existing bound text rather than treating the text as the container.
Verify that with a shape containing attached text selected, double-clicking its edge away from the text opens the existing attached text for editing rather than creating separate text.
Check that starting text at the center of an empty shape smaller than the current font’s minimum text size attaches the text and enlarges the shape enough for the minimum text size.
Confirm that appending text beyond an attached text box’s available width and committing the edit retains the text and expands the container to fit it.
Verify that editing standalone text on a canvas offset from the viewport keeps the text editor aligned with the text.
Test duplicating the shape with attached text and confirm the duplicate’s text remains attached to the duplicate, not the original.
Check that a marquee fully enclosing a shape and its attached text does not select the attached text as a separate element.
Verify that dragging a transparent shape with attached text from its empty interior moves the shape and its attached text together.
Verify that resizing the text container until the long word must wrap keeps the text visible within the shape and expands the shape vertically when the wrapped text needs more height.

Check that dragging a text-containing shape’s resize handle past the opposite edge, which would make its width or height negative, does not leave the shape or its attached text with negative dimensions.

Confirm that narrowing a text-containing shape below the estimated minimum line width does not shrink it further, and that typing text into a shape narrower or shorter than the minimum creates enough room for the text.
Test rotating a shape with attached text by itself and together with another selected element; confirm the text remains attached and rotates with its shape.
Verify that dragging from inside the #00000000 shape with attached text moves the shape and its text together.
Check that dragging from the transparent interior of the #00000000 shape without attached text does not move it, while its outline remains targetable.

report.summary: The release adds end-to-end hyperlink support for drawing elements, from editing and viewing links to preserving them when drawings are restored.
keyChanges: A link action is now included when exactly one element is selected, and the Help dialog lists Ctrl/Cmd+K for the link tool.
Linked elements now show a delayed URL tooltip positioned by the link icon, with the icon and its clickable area calculated consistently for rotated elements and different zoom levels.
Control tooltips are now kept 5 pixels from the left or right viewport edge when they would otherwise overflow.
The context menu gains a link action when its eligibility condition is met, and opening the menu dismisses a visible hyperlink popup.
Linked elements show an external-link icon while unselected, but the icon is not drawn in exports.
Hyperlink popups start hidden and close when switching from selection to another tool; context-menu action handling also resets menu-open tracking.
Ctrl/Cmd+K is newly mapped to the link action; previously, this shortcut had no mapping.
Restored drawing elements now retain a stored link, while elements with no link receive a null value; this applies through restoration paths such as imports and pasted or library content.

A single selected element can open hyperlink editing through the context action or Ctrl/Cmd+K; the action indicates whether the selected element already has a link, and new elements start with no link.
The link popup lets users enter, edit, save, or remove an element’s link; saving trims whitespace and adds https:// to nonempty links without a protocol or leading slash.

Links containing the current site origin or beginning with / open in the current tab, while other links open in a new tab; the popup stays open around the linked element and popup, and the link icon’s hit area scales with zoom.
Hovering over an unselected link icon now indicates it is clickable, and clicking the icon opens its destination; external links open in a new tab, while local links open in the same window.
Selecting one linked element, including by dragging a selection around just that element, now displays its hyperlink popup; clicking its link icon is handled separately from selecting the element.
Drawing elements now include a link value that can be a string or null; the supplied evidence shows no runtime behavior change.

Verify Ctrl+K on a Windows/Linux setup or Cmd+K on a Mac triggers the link action; before this change, that key combination had no shortcut mapping.
Check that restoring a drawing or pasted item containing an element with a link URL retains that link on the element.
Confirm that a drawing containing an element with no link field still restores and renders as before.
Verify that with exactly one element selected, Ctrl/Cmd+K opens hyperlink editing and the link action indicates link creation when the element has no link.

Verify saving the input  two spaces, example.com, two spaces trims the spaces and saves the link as https://example.com.

report.summary: The release makes file-based loading more reliable across the editor, including for images, drawings, and reusable content.
keyChanges: File processing now uses a browser-compatible fallback when native file reading is unavailable, supporting image and PNG metadata operations in Safari.
Files with no declared type are identified from PNG, JPEG, or GIF content, while supported images with a mismatched declared type are corrected before import.
Scene and library files are handled as distinct import types, and dropped files can pass an available file handle into scene restoration.

Dropped files are now identified by their contents rather than being routed as Libraries solely because their MIME type or filename says “.excalidrawlib”; the shared loader is also used for files received at startup or through sharing.
Dropped images still try to load an embedded drawing before falling back to inserting the image; file-system handles are now obtained with the dropped file and passed into loading.

report.summary: The release improves how lines and arrows are selected and edited on the drawing canvas.
keyChanges: A single selected, unlocked line or arrow can show handles at its points instead of the usual selection box; linear elements no longer show resize or rotation handles.
Hovering over a line or arrow point now highlights it, and point handles are larger while editing; the selected-point color also changes.
New editor state initializes the linear-element selection as empty, and canvas export continues to omit selection controls.
Selecting a line or arrow now activates its editing handles without first entering point-editing mode, so its points can be hovered and dragged directly.
When a line or arrow is selected, pointer hit testing uses its actual geometry instead of treating its entire bounding box as a hit; context-menu selection also activates its handles.
When a selected line or arrow is no longer selected, its editing state is cleared; releasing an edited endpoint can update its connection to a shape.
Finishing a multi-point line or arrow, or selecting all when the only selectable element is a line or arrow, now also selects it for point editing.

A selected line or arrow can now have its vertices selected and dragged without first entering point-edit mode; point handles are reduced from 20 to 10, while the point-pick distance remains 11 screen pixels.
Locking a selected element now clears its linear-point editing selection.

report.summary: The release improves line and arrow editing with segment-level midpoint controls across multi-point and curved drawings.
keyChanges: While editing a multi-segment line or arrow, midpoint handles are calculated per segment, including along rounded curves; clicking one inserts a point into that segment rather than always adding it near the start.
Midpoint handles are omitted when a segment’s on-screen length is less than four point-handle sizes; rounded segments use curve length for this cutoff.
During collaboration, editing handles are rendered from the matching visible line, avoiding reliance on a potentially out-of-date editor copy.

Rounded lines and arrows with more than 2 points now use sampled curve length and curve position to locate segment midpoints, so midpoint handles and segment selection may differ from straight-line endpoint-based placement.

report.summary: The release standardizes how drawing tools identify selected objects, with no confirmed change to normal user-visible behavior.
keyChanges: Canvas gestures and selection-dependent actions now retrieve selected elements through a shared scene-level lookup, including selection used for dragging, resizing, text editing, color picking, and context menus.
Frame and group selection updates use the shared lookup while supplying their working element lists, so verify that selected objects remain correctly associated during those operations.
Horizontal and vertical flips now provide the editor scene when recalculating frame membership, so verify that flipping selected objects completes and produces the expected mirrored result.
Both zoom-to-fit behaviors and the context-sensitive editing hints now obtain selected objects through the editor’s scene, so verify they reflect the current selection.
Keyboard handling and rendering now retrieve selected elements through the editor’s scene manager while retaining the selection options shown in the prior code.
Connector line-edit actions and their context-menu labels also use the scene manager; bound text remains included where it was included before.

The alignment controls now determine whether multiple non-frame objects are selected using the current drawing; verify their availability and alignment when that selection differs from the action’s supplied element list.
Lock and unlock selection, context-menu wording, and shortcut eligibility also use the current drawing’s selection; the existing treatment of attached text and frame contents is unchanged.
All six alignment commands now use the current drawing selection and update frame membership with the editor’s current state, so alignment should apply to live selected objects only.

Copy, cut, copy-text, and PNG/SVG clipboard exports now resolve selections from the current drawing; PNG/SVG export still falls back to the full drawing when no live selected objects are found, and bound text and frame contents remain included where previously specified.
Grouping and ungrouping use the scene’s current selection, including attached text when grouping; verify selected objects and their group state remain consistent.
Horizontal and vertical spacing also use the scene’s current selection and update frame membership through the scene; verify spacing and frame contents after distributing objects.
Binding, unbinding, and wrapping text in a container now use the scene’s current selection, so verify these actions still target the intended text and shape or connector.
Selecting all elements in a frame and removing all elements from a frame now use the scene’s current selection to identify the frame; verify both actions still operate on the selected frame.
qaChecks: Verify selecting and dragging a grouped pair keeps the intended group selected and moves its elements together.
Check moving a selected object into or out of a frame updates which objects belong to that frame.
Confirm selecting a text object and entering text editing edits that selected text, and that selecting a line or arrow permits its points to be edited.
Test opening the canvas context menu and applying a picked color with an object selected; confirm the selected object receives the color.
Verify that flipping the selected element horizontally mirrors it and completes without an error.
Verify that flipping the selected element vertically mirrors it and completes without an error.
Verify each zoom-to-fit-selection behavior frames the selected object, rather than the other unselected object.
Check that with no object selected, each zoom-to-fit behavior fits the drawing.
Confirm the editing hint reflects the selected text object, then reflects the new selection after selecting a different object.

Verify no regression-specific input: the supplied evidence shows the old and new selection paths using the same selection options, so it does not identify an input that takes a different user-facing path.

Verify that with exactly two selected non-frame objects in the current drawing and a supplied element list that omits them, alignment controls are available and applying an alignment lines up those selected objects.

Check that with a selected object in the current drawing omitted from the supplied element list, the lock action applies to that selected object and the context-menu label reflects its resulting locked or unlocked state.

Verify the stale-selection case by selecting two objects, then making one selected object absent from the current drawing while the action’s supplied object list still contains it; run each edge and center alignment and confirm only live selected objects move into alignment.

Verify PNG and SVG clipboard export with only the stale object selected; because the current drawing has no live selected objects, confirm the exported content is the full drawing rather than the stale selection.
Check copy and cut with the stale selected object alongside a live selected object; confirm the live selection is copied and cut while the stale object is not included.
Verify grouping two selected objects treats them as a group, and ungrouping that selection restores the objects as separate elements.
Check horizontal and vertical spacing with at least two selected non-frame objects; confirm the objects are spaced evenly along the chosen direction.
Confirm distributing selected objects associated with a frame leaves frame contents consistent with their resulting positions.
Verify selecting the text and empty rectangle together allows them to be bound, with the text attached to the rectangle.
Check that selecting the shape or connector with attached text and unbinding it leaves the text separate.
Confirm that selecting a text element and wrapping it in a container creates a rectangle around the text.
Verify selecting only the frame and choosing the frame-content selection action selects its contents.
Check that selecting only the frame and choosing the remove-contents action removes its contents while leaving the frame selected.
uncertainty: The supplied changes do not establish a concrete, ordinary user input that behaves differently before and after; most replace selection lookup while retaining the same element list and selection options, so the checks are regression coverage rather than confirmation of a known behavior change.

The evidence shows the selection source changed, but provides no concrete user-produced input where the old element list and current scene selection differ, so a specific regression-triggering case cannot be identified.

The changed behavior differs from the previous behavior only when the action’s element list and the current drawing’s selection disagree; the supplied context does not establish a manual workflow for producing or observing that state.

The changed behavior differs when the supplied object list and current drawing disagree, but the supplied context does not establish how a manual tester can reproduce that stale-selection state through the interface.
The supplied evidence does not identify a concrete user input that the old selection lookup handled differently from the new scene-based lookup, so the precise regression-triggering case is unknown.

The supplied evidence does not establish a user-reproducible input where the old selection lookup and the current-scene lookup return different results, so these checks cannot target a confirmed old-versus-new edge case.

report.summary: The release adds easier canvas navigation and makes editing tools more consistent when switching and restoring them.
keyChanges: The whiteboard now has a hand tool, available from the desktop and mobile toolbars and the H shortcut; selecting it changes the cursor to a grab hand and lets users pan by dragging the canvas.
While the hand tool is active, shape-editing actions are hidden unless drawing elements are selected, and toolbar shortcut labels use the letter when no numeric shortcut is available.
The remembered-tool state now uses a new field, and finalizing the eraser consults that field when choosing the tool to resume; restored drawings start with no remembered tool.
The desktop and mobile toolbars now include a hand-tool control, and the shortcut guide adds the hand tool with the H shortcut.
Single-letter lowercase shortcuts are now displayed in uppercase; for example, v is displayed as V.

A hand-tool control is wired into the editor, and when the hand tool is active a single-pointer primary-button drag pans the canvas without requiring the space key; the same drag no longer starts creating an element.
The lock-control and shared tool-button changes only adjust component properties, and the new hand icon supplies the hand-tool symbol. No additional user-visible behavior is evidenced.
Pressing H now toggles the hand tool, clears the current selection, changes the cursor to a grab cursor, and returns to the previously active tool when toggled off.
Eraser switching now uses the shared previous-tool state; the eraser panel component was removed, so verify tool switching through the available editor interaction.
Imported drawing settings containing the hand tool were previously marked as using a disallowed tool; they are now accepted, so restoring such settings should preserve hand-tool mode.
qaChecks: Verify that selecting the hand tool or pressing H activates it, shows a grab cursor, and lets you pan the canvas by dragging without creating or moving a shape.
Check that shape-editing actions are hidden with the hand tool active and no selection, then reappear when a shape is selected.

Confirm that a drawing with a shape selected can switch to the eraser and finalize an erase, then resumes the previously active tool; reload a drawing while the eraser is active and confirm it restores without a stale remembered tool.
Verify that a toolbar tool with a letter shortcut but no numeric shortcut displays the letter as its shortcut label.
Verify the shortcut guide includes the hand tool with the H shortcut.
Check that a lowercase single-letter shortcut such as v is displayed as V.
Verify the hand-tool control is available on both device types, and selecting it makes its active state visible.
Confirm that while zen mode is active, toggling the lock control still updates its checked state to match whether the active tool is locked.
Verify that, with the hand tool active and without holding space, dragging with one primary pointer moves the canvas and creates no element.
Verify that pressing H activates hand mode, clears the selected element, and changes the canvas cursor to a grab cursor; pressing H again should return to the previously active tool.
Check that pressing E activates eraser mode and clears the selection, then pressing E again returns to the tool that was active before eraser mode.
Validate the combined sequence H, E, E, H: eraser mode should return to hand mode, and toggling hand mode off should leave selection active.
Verify restoring drawing data with the saved active tool set to hand leaves hand-tool mode active instead of treating the tool as disallowed.
uncertainty: The lock control no longer receives zen-mode state; the supplied evidence does not establish whether that state affected its presentation, so check whether its zen-mode appearance has changed.

When eraser mode is entered while hand mode is active, the shared previous-tool state may replace the tool saved before hand mode; confirm whether returning to selection after the combined sequence is intended.

report.summary: The release updates the editor and library experience, including navigation, controls, focus behavior, and on-screen guidance.
keyChanges: Older drawings that stored the Library as an open sidebar now restore with the default sidebar open regardless of the saved docked preference, while the older separate preference for an open Library is no longer restored.

Library updates still open the Library when requested, but keyboard focus returns to the editor only after a prompted update is accepted; unprompted updates and declined prompts no longer force focus.
The editor no longer takes keyboard focus automatically on startup unless automatic focus is enabled, while explicit sidebar controls are now available to embedded-editor integrations.
Library actions are regrouped, and an empty Library now includes the browse and management controls; the empty-state label and bottom border are also adjusted.
The Library’s Escape-close handler was removed, and resetting it no longer explicitly returns focus to the editor; removing selected items still removes them and clears the selection.
The welcome screen’s center content and menu, toolbar, and help guidance are wired to updated display points, while reusable editor buttons now support a selected visual state.
The library is now assembled inside the standard sidebar using shared editor state, so verify that adding and inserting drawing items and managing saved library items still work together.

Embedded-editor fallback coordination now clears host preference when the final wrapped component unmounts, so internal fallback content should be available again when the host-provided component is gone.

Pasting, dropping, or inserting Library items now keeps the sidebar open based on the default dock preference rather than whether it is currently docked, so those states can produce different results.

A new element-insertion capability places supplied elements at the canvas center, aligned to the grid; the sidebar toggle now accepts a sidebar name and optional tab instead of the previous library/custom-sidebar options.
After confirming or canceling a confirmation dialog, focus is returned to the editor container.

Sidebar controls can open or close a named sidebar, select its tabs, and show whether it is docked; outside clicks and Escape dismiss it only when it is not docked or the device cannot fit it, and an open dialog prevents dismissal.
A button’s supplied click handler now runs before its selection action, and if that handler prevents the default, the selection action does not run. The button can also display a selected state.

The editor now uses a default sidebar and its trigger in place of the former library-specific and custom-sidebar rendering; when a sidebar is open and docked on a desktop that fits it, the canvas area is narrowed.
On mobile, the scroll-back control now appears only when no sidebar is open; previously it could appear with a non-library sidebar open.
Editor update comparisons now detect different numbers of properties and compare selection maps by their contents, changing when editor updates are recognized.
Embedded editors now receive custom sidebars as children rather than through the former callback option, and the package exposes a default sidebar for integrations.
Sidebar state now identifies the open sidebar and optional tab, while the default sidebar’s docking preference is distinct from its actual docked state.
On devices that cannot fit a sidebar, editing hints are hidden whenever any sidebar is open; previously, only the Library sidebar hid them.
The Library toggle component was removed, including its prior open/close behavior and its special case when the Library sidebar was docked; verify Library access still works on desktop and mobile.
Sidebar closing now uses a close-request action, and the former conditional dock control was removed from the header; verify closing and any supported docking behavior.

The previous host-versus-fallback suppression mechanism was removed, while the sidebar contract identifies internal panels as lower priority than host panels; verify which panel appears when both are available.
qaChecks: Verify that restoring the drawing with the Library stored as the open sidebar opens the default sidebar even when its saved docked preference is turned off.
Check that restoring a drawing with only the separate older Library-open setting does not reopen the Library.
Verify that importing a library opens the Library sidebar.
Check that accepting a prompted library update returns keyboard focus to the editor, while declining the prompt does not force focus there.
Confirm that an unprompted library update does not take keyboard focus from another active control.
Verify that the editor does not take keyboard focus automatically on startup when automatic focus is disabled.
Check that requesting closure of the currently open sidebar closes it and reports that no sidebar remains open.
Verify that an empty Library shows its browse and management controls along with the empty-state message.
Verify that with the Library open and the sidebar undocked, pressing Escape closes it; repeat when the device cannot fit the sidebar.
Check that removing one selected saved item removes it from the Library and clears the selection.
Confirm that resetting a populated Library clears its items and returns keyboard focus to the editor.
Verify that the welcome screen displays its center content and the menu, toolbar, and help guidance.
Verify selecting one saved item, choosing the library removal action, and confirming removes only that item and clears its selection.
Check that choosing the library reset action with no items selected and confirming clears the library.
Confirm selected drawing elements can still be added to the library and a saved item can still be inserted into the drawing.
Verify that clicking outside an open, undocked library sidebar closes it.
Verify that after the host-provided component is removed and no wrapped instances remain, the internal fallback content appears without duplicate host and fallback content.
Verify inserting that element set places its bounds around the canvas center, aligned to the grid.
Check that pasting an element or inserting a Library item closes the open sidebar in this exact state; the previous behavior kept it open when it was docked.
Verify choosing either confirm or cancel closes the confirmation as appropriate and returns keyboard focus to the editor container.
Verify that opening a sidebar trigger displays its sidebar and selecting another tab makes that tab active.
Check that an outside click or Escape closes an undocked sidebar when no dialog is open, but leaves it open while a dialog is open.
Confirm that an outside click or Escape leaves a docked sidebar open on a device that can fit it, and that the dock control reflects its docked state.
Verify that clicking the button runs its click action first and, when that action prevents the default, does not run the selection action.
Verify that opening and docking the sidebar leaves the sidebar visible and reduces the drawing area's width.
Check that undocking the sidebar restores the drawing area rather than leaving it narrowed.
Verify that with a non-Library sidebar open, the scroll-back control is not shown; this is the case that showed it before but no longer meets the new condition.
Check that with no sidebar open and content scrolled away, the scroll-back control is shown.
Verify that changing properties from an object with one key, such as {a: 1}, to one with two keys, such as {a: 1, b: 2}, is recognized as a change and the editor reflects the updated input.
Verify that choosing a bar or line chart preview inserts that chart into the drawing and closes the chart dialog.
Verify the child-provided sidebar displays both tabs and its trigger opens the first tab.
Check that an integration using only the former callback option does not display its custom sidebar.
Verify that opening a custom sidebar hides editing hints on a device that cannot fit a sidebar, even though the previous behavior hid them only for the Library sidebar.
Verify that clicking the Library control while the Library is closed opens the Library, and clicking it again closes the Library, on both desktop and mobile.
Verify that selecting the sidebar close control closes the sidebar.
Check that a sidebar configured to be dockable still exposes a way to dock and undock it, and that its state changes accordingly.
Verify that when both sidebars are available, the host-provided sidebar takes precedence and the user does not see duplicate panels.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not identify which visible panel is the default sidebar, so confirm which panel should appear when restoring an older drawing with a string-valued sidebar setting.

The prior Escape handler is absent, and reset no longer explicitly returns focus to the editor; verify whether either behavior is supplied elsewhere, since loss of Escape-to-close or focus return is a likely Library regression.
The change removes the library’s own outside-click and keyboard-close handling, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether the replacement sidebar preserves those dismissal behaviors.

The sidebar toggle no longer rejects a custom sidebar when no custom sidebar renderer is configured; the supplied evidence does not establish whether this configuration should now open a visible sidebar or merely update sidebar state.

The chart change switches where the insertion callback is obtained, but the evidence does not show an input that behaved differently before and after; the paste check verifies the workflow, not a demonstrated regression case.

No affected application areas or navigation steps were supplied, and the graph does not identify replacements for the removed Library toggle or host-versus-fallback wrapper, so their new locations and whether their former behaviors are retained are unconfirmed.
