report.summary: The release updates how scene and drawing changes are tracked, synchronized, and integrated across editor workflows.
keyChanges: Canvas and observed editor-state snapshots are reused when their tracked content has not changed, while changed content is captured for history or snapshot updates.
Observed editor state now carries an internal marker so it can be recognized when snapshot updates receive it; verify that line editing and history continue to reflect the correct editor state.

Drawing updates now distinguish changes recorded as undoable edits from updates that refresh the history snapshot; this affects canvas gestures, color sampling, and updates sent through an embedded editor.
When a touchscreen stroke has fewer than 10 points and a second touch interrupts it, the short stroke is removed while the history snapshot is updated.
Importing an Excalidraw drawing now refreshes the existing drawing’s history snapshot after element ordering is reconciled, to avoid duplicate ordering indices on undo.

Loading a scene after a shareable-link hash change is now marked for capture, while local changes, browser-tab synchronization, and image-status updates are marked as updates; verify their undo-history treatment alongside the visible scene.
Scene loading no longer supplies the previous explicit “do not commit” setting, so confirm that loading still restores the intended drawing and local settings.

Incoming shared-scene changes, initial scene preparation for a new collaboration, the scene update after confirming collaboration shutdown, and image-upload completion now explicitly use the UPDATE action; the supplied evidence does not establish how that changes user-visible behavior.
Clearing the drawing store now also clears pending actions, and when capture and snapshot update are both scheduled, capture takes precedence.
Action results now select a store action instead of using a commit flag, and the exposed action values change from uppercase to lowercase; embedded integrations may need updating.
qaChecks: Verify that selecting the line or arrow and editing one point visibly updates the drawing.
Check that undo restores the previous line or arrow geometry and redo restores the edited geometry.
Verify that submitting a one-shape drawing update without specifying a history-recording option changes the drawing and that one undo restores the prior drawing, as the documented default indicates.

Check that a touchscreen stroke with fewer than 10 recorded points is discarded when a second finger touches the canvas before the stroke ends, and that undo does not bring back the discarded stroke or remove the prior drawing.
Verify that sampling a different color for a selected shape applies the sampled color and that undo restores the shape’s previous color.
Confirm that importing the Excalidraw file into the existing drawing preserves the elements’ ordering and that undo does not create duplicate ordering positions.
Verify loading the different drawing from its shareable link shows that drawing and preserves applicable local settings.
Check undo and redo after loading the linked drawing and making a new edit; confirm the loaded scene and subsequent edit behave consistently in the history.
Confirm a locally saved image reaches its saved state without disrupting the drawing or its user edits.
Verify drawing changes and image availability remain synchronized between participants after an image loads.
Check the failed-image case and confirm the shared drawing remains usable and subsequent edits still synchronize.
Verify that returning focus to the other tab applies the newer local drawing state and that the drawing remains editable.
Verify that when one participant changes a drawing element, the other participant sees the remote change in the shared scene.
Check that starting a new collaboration with an existing drawing preserves its visible elements for participants.
Confirm that after an image upload completes, the image remains visible in the shared drawing.
Test stopping collaboration and accepting the confirmation with an image in the drawing; confirm the drawing remains visible.
Verify that after replacing the drawing, the pending change from the previous drawing does not reappear in the replacement.

Check an action result using the former uppercase value CAPTURE and then the lowercase value capture; confirm the lowercase value records the drawing change and do not assume the former value remains compatible.
Confirm an action result uses the new action-selection field with value update or none, and that drawing changes are respectively updated without capture or left unrecorded.
uncertainty: The supplied before-and-after code does not establish a concrete user input that the old behavior handled differently from the new behavior, so the precise regression-triggering input cannot be confirmed.

The drawing-update API documents that omitting the history option defaults to recording an undoable change, but the new update logic does not apply a history action when the option is omitted; verify the expected default.

The supplied changes do not identify a specific input value or branch that behaves differently before and after; they change store-action settings, but the expected undo-history effects and the default behavior after removing the old loading option are not established here.

No input or branch distinction beyond adding the UPDATE action is shown, and its effect on history or other visible behavior is not defined in the supplied context; confirm the intended user-visible outcome before testing that specific effect.
It is unknown whether existing embedded integrations still use the former commit flag or uppercase action values, so compatibility with those integrations remains unverified.

report.summary: The release makes editor tools easier to find and use with searchable commands, keyboard shortcuts, and clearer context-aware controls.
keyChanges: Shortcut lookup can now select a requested shortcut, falling back to the first when that position is unavailable; the command-palette hint can therefore show its alternate shortcut instead of repeating the first.
The command palette supports keyboard navigation, command availability based on editor state, and running a selected command; running one closes the palette and clears its search.
Dialog focus is applied after the dialog renders, and the close icon is shown only in fullscreen mobile dialogs, not desktop dialogs.

Ctrl/Cmd+P now shows a temporary hint with the command-palette shortcuts and prevents the browser’s default action; a new command-palette menu item opens the searchable command list, and the Help dialog lists its shortcuts.
Ctrl/Cmd-double-clicking a selected line or arrow that is already being edited now continues through normal double-click handling instead of returning early.
Dialogs now account for animations being disabled when they are created, while clicking a drawing link continues to open its destination with reduced access to the originating page.
Canvas context-menu captions are now read from the standard item label, rather than the previous context-menu-specific caption.

The command palette opens with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P or Ctrl/Cmd+/, and organizes commands by App, Export, Editor, Tools, Elements, then Links; search also ignores accents and selected punctuation or spacing.

Color-editing commands are available in the palette only when elements are selected and their types support the relevant color; the selection properties area uses the same eligibility rules on desktop and mobile.
The main application menu now provides access to a command palette with sharing, live-collaboration, Excalidraw+, social, and theme commands; Excalidraw+ options vary for signed-in users.
Element-lock controls now reflect the selection, and “Unlock all elements” is available only when nothing is selected.
Opening another editor dialog now closes the share dialog.
The command palette now includes a theme-toggle command and routes image-command keyboard activation into direct insertion, while mouse activation selects the image tool without that option.
Canvas and alignment actions gain descriptive labels or palette names and icons; the alignment eligibility and alignment behavior are unchanged.
The link action derives its label safely when no element is selected; previously, resolving it in that state could fail.
Frame, group and ungroup, undo and redo, and line-edit actions now have standard action labels; several also receive icons, and line editing is categorized under Elements for command discovery.
The line-edit label still distinguishes entering and leaving edit mode, and now safely handles a missing selected line when choosing its label.
The shortcut catalog adds command-palette shortcuts CtrlOrCmd+Shift+P and CtrlOrCmd+/, plus mappings for zoom, tool switching, saving, and shortcut help.
Copy/paste styles, canvas modes, layer ordering, statistics, and the embed tool gain action labels or icons; statistics, view mode, and zen mode also gain command-palette names.
Object snapping changes from being marked as available in view-only mode to not being marked that way; the actual presentation or availability effect is unclear from the supplied evidence.

Labels are added or standardized across library, text, clipboard, selection, arrangement, export, menu, collaboration, and appearance actions; several actions also gain icons, and clipboard actions gain the keywords “svg”, “png”, “text”, “clipboard”, and “copy”.
The supplied diffs change action registration metadata rather than drawing behavior; no old-versus-new input that changes an operation was identified.
qaChecks: Verify the command-palette shortcut hint shows the second shortcut when available, rather than repeating the first; press the displayed alternate shortcut and confirm the palette opens.

Check that pressing Arrow Up or Arrow Down moves the selection through available commands and that pressing Enter runs the selected command, closes the palette, and clears the search when it is reopened.
Confirm that commands whose labels or icons depend on the current drawing reflect the drawing's current elements when the palette is shown.
Verify Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P and Ctrl/Cmd+/ each open the palette, and pressing either shortcut again closes it.
Check that Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+/ does not open the palette.
Test searching for “change-background” with a rectangle selected; confirm the background-color command appears, and choosing it opens the background-color editing popup.
Confirm the default command categories appear in this order: App, Export, Editor, Tools, Elements, Links.
Verify that on desktop the dialog has no visible close icon, while in fullscreen mobile view it has a close icon that closes the dialog.
Check that after opening a dialog with autofocus enabled, focus moves to a dialog control after the dialog renders; confirm dialogs with autofocus disabled do not receive this automatic focus.
Verify a dialog opened while animations are disabled appears without its normal animation, and that dialogs still open normally when animations are enabled.
Verify Ctrl/Cmd+P shows a temporary command-palette shortcut hint and does not trigger the browser’s default print action.
Check that the command-palette menu item opens the searchable command list, and that the Help dialog lists the command-palette shortcuts.
Confirm Ctrl/Cmd-double-clicking the already-edited selected line or arrow continues through the normal double-click handling rather than being stopped immediately.
Verify the context menu displays readable captions and its actions remain selectable.
Check that clicking a drawing link opens the intended destination.
Verify selecting a rectangle makes stroke-color and background-color editing available in the selection properties.
Check that selecting only an image does not offer stroke-color or background-color editing; then select the image together with a rectangle and confirm both color-editing options are available.

Verify the main application menu provides access to the searchable command palette, and that searching “stop” offers the session-ending command during an active collaboration but not when no session is active.
Check that the palette offers the share command and opens the sharing dialog, and that opening another editor dialog closes the sharing dialog.

Confirm that an unsigned user sees separate Excalidraw+ and sign-up choices, while a signed-in user sees “Sign in / Go to Excalidraw+”; selecting the applicable choice opens its Excalidraw+ destination.
Test the Excalidraw+ export command with the prepared drawing and confirm that it initiates export of the drawing to Excalidraw+.
Verify that with no elements selected, the selection-dependent lock action is unavailable; select an unlocked element and confirm the action becomes available.
Check that when an element is selected alongside a different locked element, the unlock-all action is unavailable; deselect everything and confirm it becomes available while a locked element remains.
Confirm that selecting one unlocked element presents a lock action, selecting one locked element presents an unlock action, and toggling either action changes that element’s lock state.
Verify searching for “dark” finds the theme-toggle command, and activating it switches between light and dark themes.
Confirm activating the image command with the keyboard starts direct insertion, while activating it with the mouse selects the image tool without direct insertion.
Check that resolving the link action with zero selected elements falls back to the create-link option without an error.
Verify that with one line selected, the line-edit action is categorized under Elements and its wording changes between editing and exiting line editing.
Check that frame, group and ungroup, undo, and redo actions display their appropriate labels and icons, and confirm undo and redo still reverse and reapply a recent drawing change.
Verify the shortcut catalog includes CtrlOrCmd+Shift+P and CtrlOrCmd+/ for the command palette.

Verify the catalog includes CtrlOrCmd+0, CtrlOrCmd+-, CtrlOrCmd++, Shift+1, Shift+2, and Shift+3 for the added zoom commands, and E, H, F, CtrlOrCmd+S, and ? for the added tool, save, and shortcut-help mappings.

Verify copy and paste styles, grid, object snapping, statistics, view mode, zen mode, layer ordering, and the embed tool are presented with their new action labels or icons where those actions are offered.
Verify the statistics, view-mode, and zen-mode actions are identifiable by their added command-palette names.

Verify whether object snapping is offered or usable in view-only mode, noting that its classification changed from allowed to not allowed; confirm the observed availability matches the product expectation.
Verify the editor presents the updated action names and supplied icons for applicable editing, clipboard, export, menu, and appearance actions wherever those actions are exposed.
uncertainty: Most command-palette handlers are additions-only in the supplied diff, so the prior behavior and a specific old-versus-new failure input cannot be established for those interactions.

The supplied evidence does not establish whether any context-menu users still provide captions through the previous mechanism; confirm actual editor context-menu captions remain visible. The precise intended result of the changed double-click path is also not specified, so confirm it matches the expected line-editing interaction.

The supplied changes add the command palette without a before-version implementation, so an input that the old palette handled differently cannot be established. Navigation details and affected surface IDs were not supplied.
The supplied context gives no navigation steps for the command palette or link action, so the empty-selection link-label check may not have an accessible manual entry point.
The supplied evidence does not identify which editor surfaces display the updated action labels and icons, or provide navigation steps to reach them.

The evidence shows object snapping is no longer classified as available in view-only mode, but does not establish whether this hides the action, prevents its use, or affects only another presentation of the action.

The supplied context identifies no affected pages or navigation, and the diffs establish no changed user-visible operation or edge-case input; confirm where these metadata changes appear in the interface.

report.summary: The release improves how the editor records and restores drawing changes, making undo and redo more consistent.
keyChanges: Connection and attachment cleanup now reconciles arrows and bound text as drawing elements change or are deleted, including restoring relationships during undo and redo.
When attached text is redrawn, its angle is now set to its container’s angle, so it should follow a rotated container after text or layout changes.
Editing actions now use the drawing store’s capture controls for history; verify that binding, text styling, and deletion remain undoable and redoable.

Undo and redo now apply recorded drawing and app-state changes to the current scene, including handling changes that no longer produce a visible difference; verify edits remain correctly reversible after other scene changes.
Grouping and ungrouping now capture their scene changes, and grouping uses the reordered element list returned by the ordering update; verify group membership, stacking order, and undo/redo.
When a non-library browser hash change restores a scene, the editor now captures that scene in its store instead of committing it to undo history.
Previously, undo and redo controls stayed enabled with empty history; now each is disabled when its history stack is empty and becomes available as edits are recorded.
Undo and redo now apply recorded drawing and app-state changes against the current scene and snapshot, including changes to element connections.
Undo and redo now reapply drawing and selection changes together, filtering selections and editing states that refer to elements or groups no longer present.
Applying drawing changes now recalculates affected connector bindings and attached text, and detects when element order changes.
The change-recording snapshot tracks observed drawing and editor-state changes; elements missing from a later scene snapshot are retained as deleted rather than dropped.
Selecting all elements inside a frame now records the selection change, so it can be reversed and reapplied with Undo and redo.
Scene-element updates made through an embedded editor without the history-commit option may no longer be undoable; updates that explicitly commit should still be checked for correct undo behavior.
Redo entries are intended to survive app-state-only changes, such as changing the selection, while element changes continue to clear redo history.

Collaboration updates no longer clear undo history, and starting or stopping a session no longer explicitly sets history behavior; verify local undo remains usable without losing synchronized drawing changes.

Canvas and selected-element actions now explicitly capture meaningful drawing changes or avoid storing view and export settings; loading a drawing captures the replacement scene, while saving does not add a drawing edit.
Zoom controls now disable at the minimum and maximum zoom limits, and fit-to-content uses the configured zoom limits.

Finalizing a drawing now captures a history state even for non-freehand tools; previously, the general finalization path captured history only for freehand, so test ordinary shape completion and undo/redo.
Entering or leaving line-point editing now captures history, and finalizing line editing clears its selected-line state; test that editing exits cleanly and the line remains intact.
Library, clipboard, style-copying, collaborator-following, and display or snapping actions now explicitly opt out of stored history, while selection and hyperlink actions continue to capture state.
Aligning, distributing, duplicating, locking, flipping, and changing the stacking order of elements now request scene capture; verify these edits still appear correctly and can be undone and redone.

When duplicating elements, index synchronization now uses the copies rather than the originals and copies together, which may affect their ordering; snapshot handling also filters uncommitted elements and uses the saved version when it is older than the previous local version.

Check that deleting the shape clears its attached relationships, and that undoing and redoing the deletion restores and reapplies the relationships consistently.

Verify that binding, unbinding, and wrapping text in a container can each be undone and redone, restoring the corresponding drawing state.

Verify that after placing only the first point of an arrow, then completing it with a second point, undo removes the completed arrow without leaving a stray partial arrow, and redo restores it.
Check that creating and deleting a shape, then undoing and redoing, restores the expected visible scene each time.
Verify that after deleting a selected shape, undo restores the shape and redo removes it again.
Check that undoing or redoing a change that removes the selected element or its group leaves no stale selection or group-editing state.
Verify that grouping the two separated shapes preserves their relative order and places the group at the highest selected shape's stacking position.
Check that undo restores the pre-group drawing and redo reapplies the group; then verify ungrouping can also be undone and redone.
Verify that changing to the scene hash displays the restored drawing and that a subsequent drawing edit can be undone and redone without treating scene restoration as a separate user edit.
Verify that with no drawing edits, both undo and redo controls are disabled.
Check that after creating one shape, undo becomes available; undo removes that shape, and redo restores it.
Confirm that after creating a shape with an attached arrow, undoing and redoing the relevant edits keeps the arrow connection consistent with the shape’s state.
Verify that undoing and redoing a shape change keeps its attached text positioned and sized with the shape.
Check that undoing and redoing a change to a bound shape keeps the connector attached and its endpoints aligned.
Verify that after changing which element is in front, undo restores the prior visible order and redo reapplies the new order.
Verify that selecting all elements inside a selected frame and then using Undo restores the previous selection; Redo selects the frame’s elements again.
Check that after undoing an element creation, clicking the empty canvas to change the selection does not remove the available Redo action.
Confirm that drawing a change after Undo clears the previous Redo action.
Test an element update that omits the history-commit option; verify the updated drawing appears and that Undo does not reverse this update.
Verify that an element update explicitly marked for history commit appears in the drawing and can be reversed with Undo.
Verify that after the other participant changes the scene, undoing the prior local edit still works and does not remove the other participant’s synchronized change.
Check that starting and then stopping collaboration leaves the drawing’s visible elements intact.
Verify that changing the selected shape’s fill, opacity, stroke, roundness, sloppiness, or arrowhead can be undone to restore its prior appearance.
Check that clearing the canvas can be undone to restore the drawing.
Verify that zoom-in is disabled at 30× and zoom-out is disabled at 10%, and that fit-to-content keeps the drawing within the configured zoom limits.
Verify that loading a drawing replaces the scene and that undo restores the scene that was present before loading.
Check that saving the drawing and changing its name or export settings do not undo the last drawing edit; confirm the saved or exported result reflects the chosen settings.
Verify drawing and finalizing a rectangle with a non-freehand tool, then using Undo and Redo, reverses and reapplies the drawing change without losing or duplicating the rectangle.
Check a multi-point line whose points are close enough together that it is invisible: finalize it, then use Undo and Redo, and confirm no invisible element reappears as a visible artifact.
Confirm that selecting a line or arrow, entering and leaving point editing, and finalizing exits point editing and keeps the line geometry intact through Undo and Redo.

Verify with three or more selected elements that aligning them by an edge or center and distributing them horizontally or vertically produces the requested arrangement, and that undo and redo reverse and restore each edit.
Verify that duplicating one selected element between unselected elements creates one copy while preserving the originals' relative order, and that undo and redo reverse and restore the duplication.

Check that locking selected elements, unlocking all elements, flipping selected elements horizontally and vertically, and moving them forward or backward in the stacking order each produce the requested result and can be undone and redone.

Verify during live collaboration that a new element not yet committed locally is not included in the captured update, and that an already-committed element is not replaced by a snapshot older than its previous local version.
uncertainty: The evidence does not establish whether the new history-capture controls behave identically to the previous history flags, so undo and redo consistency needs confirmation.

The previous history logic excluded an in-progress line or arrow with fewer than two points and omitted an uncommitted last point; the supplied new history code does not show an equivalent filter, so confirm the intended undo behavior for an arrow after only its first point.

The supplied changes contain no removed code, so the prior behavior and a concrete input handled differently before and after cannot be established; the checks above cover the behavior shown in the new implementation.
The supplied evidence does not establish how the new default history handling treats synchronized scene updates, so confirm whether undo retains local edits without reverting collaborators’ changes.
Finalization now captures state even when it removes an invisibly small multi-point element; it is unclear whether Undo or Redo can restore that discarded element.
The supplied evidence does not identify how to reproduce an uncommitted or older-snapshot state through the application, so the live-collaboration check may need a known in-progress update scenario.

report.summary: The release improves diagram editing with more capable bent connectors and more consistent behavior across common editing actions.
keyChanges: Elbow arrows now calculate routes around shapes and choose connection directions based on the target shape, including diamonds and rotated shapes.
Dragging an elbow-arrow endpoint toward a shape can snap it to a mid-edge connection; the default snap window scales with shape size and is clamped to 5–80 pixels.
Elbow arrows now draw rounded bends with a 16-pixel maximum radius, reduced to at most half the length of either segment beside a bend.

While dragging an elbow-arrow endpoint, binding can recognize points inside a shape’s axis-aligned bounds, not just near its outline; rectangular corner connections are also positioned 5 pixels clear of the corner.
Arrow binding and shape calculations were expanded to support these routing and connection updates; the supplied evidence does not establish other user-visible behavior changes.
New elbow arrows default to the round arrow type, and new routing logic calculates bent paths around drawing elements.
Undo and redo now redraw bound arrows using the current drawing, so connector routes can be recalculated as drawing changes are reversed or restored.

Arrow controls now appear when an arrow tool is active or an arrow is selected, and pressing A while the arrow tool is active cycles the new-arrow style from sharp to round to elbow and back; arrows no longer offer the roundness control.
Elbow arrows route with bends and connect to shapes; their routes update as connected shapes move, and their endpoints can be adjusted without grid snapping.
Elbow arrows are excluded from the line editor and box selection only selects their endpoints; a single bound elbow arrow does not move when dragged or resize when a resize handle is dragged.
A single arrow-tool hint now gives arrow-specific guidance, while multi-element drawing keeps the existing multi-element hint.
Bent connectors now keep fixed attachment points as connected shapes move, resize, or rotate, and preserve those points when copied or scaled; their routes also avoid rectangular corners.
Bent connectors no longer show transform handles or a bounding box, cannot be rotated, and show handles only at their endpoints rather than at interior bends.
The binding highlight now has a fixed 10-unit thickness instead of varying with the connected shape, and its rectangular outline follows the shape’s corner rounding.
Negative angles are now converted to positive degrees; for example, -90° becomes 270°, which affects rotation-related drawing interactions.
The Stats panel no longer offers angle editing for elbow arrows; position and size edits now also refresh connections to keep attached arrows aligned.
Restoring drawings now preserves elbow-arrow data and supplies a missing endpoint fixed point as [0,0]; converting arrow elements now constructs them as arrows.
Arrow-specific selection logic now recognizes only elements of type arrow, rather than treating other element types as arrows.

Arrows now have sharp, rounded, and elbow styles; changing an arrow to elbow style keeps its endpoints, removes intermediate points, and routes it as a bent connector, binding endpoints that overlap shapes.
Elbow arrows no longer offer linear-point editing, and dragging a segment midpoint does not add a point; changing edge roundness also excludes arrows from that control.
Arrow binding and updates during drawing edits now handle elbow-arrow connection points, including when connectors or their attached shapes are moved, resized, rotated, or flipped.
Elbow arrows now draw with only a start and end point, route as they are moved, and are not grid-snapped; a third placement click now finalizes the arrow instead of adding another point.
Deleting a shape connected to an elbow arrow now removes that endpoint’s connection and recalculates the arrow route; text edits and undo or redo also refresh connected arrow routing.
qaChecks: Verify the elbow arrow routes around the intervening shape and connects to the rotated diamond on the side indicated by the endpoint’s position.
Check dragging an arrow endpoint toward the middle of a shape edge snaps the connection to that edge, and dragging it away from the shape leaves the endpoint unattached.
Confirm moving or rotating a shape with a connected elbow arrow updates the arrow’s connection and route.
Verify dragging an elbow-arrow endpoint to the center of the rectangle connects the arrow to that shape and routes the endpoint to its outline.
Check that a bend beside a 20-pixel segment rounds by no more than 10 pixels, while bends beside segments of at least 32 pixels round by no more than 16 pixels.
Confirm a connection made at a rectangular corner is positioned 5 pixels clear of the corner.
Verify a newly created arrow with no explicitly selected arrow type uses the round type.
Check an elbow arrow connecting the two shapes with the third shape in its direct path; confirm the connector bends around the intervening shape.
Verify undo restores the shape and updates the bound arrow to match the restored drawing.
Verify redo restores the moved shape and recalculates the bound arrow route for that drawing.
Verify that dragging a connected shape updates the elbow arrow route and keeps its endpoint attached to the shape.
Check that dragging an endpoint or adding a point to an elbow arrow can place it between grid positions, and that the route updates to follow the edited endpoint.
Confirm that dragging a single elbow arrow with either endpoint bound does not move it, and that dragging a resize handle on that arrow does not resize it.
Verify that selecting an arrow exposes the arrow-style control and does not expose the roundness control; also confirm that the line editor is not offered for an elbow arrow.
Test pressing A while the arrow tool is already active: the new-arrow style should cycle sharp, round, elbow, then sharp.
Check that pressing an arrow key with a bound elbow arrow selected leaves it in place, including when Shift is held; previously the selected arrow moved.
Verify that the single-arrow hint gives arrow-specific guidance, while beginning a multi-element arrow keeps the multi-element guidance.
Verify that rotating the attached rectangle to 45° keeps the connector endpoint on the same relative point on the rotated shape.
Check that resizing the attached rectangle keeps the connector attached at the same relative point and updates its route.
Confirm that duplicating the connector and its attached rectangle preserves the connection and midpoint attachment on the duplicate.
Test routing an endpoint toward a rectangle corner and confirm the connector snaps to the outline without ending at the corner.
Verify that the selected connector has no bounding box or resize and rotation handles.
Check that editing the connector shows handles at its two endpoints but not at interior bends.
Confirm that dragging an endpoint of a bound bent connector does not rotate the connector.
Verify that clicking the visible outline of the -90° shape selects it and that its selection interaction remains aligned with the shape.
Check the binding highlight on both small and large shapes and confirm its thickness remains fixed at 10 drawing units rather than scaling with shape size.
Confirm that the binding highlight around a rounded rectangle follows its rounded corners.
Verify an elbow arrow has no angle control, while a regular arrow still allows rotation.
Check that entering a new position or width for a connected shape keeps its attached elbow arrow connected and routed; repeat with a multi-element or group selection.
Confirm that selecting an arrow versus a line produces the appropriate arrow-specific selection behavior.
Verify that loading the legacy elbow arrow keeps it bent and connected after restoration, including when the binding lacks a fixed point.
Check that loading or inserting arrow element data preserves its arrow identity and arrowhead.

Verify changing the multi-point arrow to elbow style preserves its endpoints, removes its intermediate points, and routes it with bends; endpoints overlapping shapes should snap to and connect with those shapes.
Check a single selected elbow arrow cannot enter linear-point editing, and dragging on its segment midpoint beyond the drag threshold does not insert a point.
Verify sharp, rounded, and elbow arrow styles can be selected for an arrow, and edge-roundness controls do not change an elbow arrow.
Verify moving, resizing, or rotating an attached shape keeps the elbow arrow connected and updates its route.
Check flipping a connected arrow or its attached shapes preserves the visible connections and elbow routing.
Verify that after starting an elbow arrow and placing its second endpoint, a third placement click finalizes it rather than adding a third point.
Check that dragging an elbow-arrow endpoint by a non-grid-aligned offset leaves it at that offset instead of snapping it to the grid.
Confirm that Ctrl or Command plus double-click on a selected elbow arrow does not enter linear-point editing.
Test dragging an endpoint of a selected elbow arrow onto a shape and confirm the connector updates its route and connection.
Verify that deleting one connected shape removes the arrow’s connection to that shape and recalculates the route, while the arrow and its other endpoint remain.
Check that undo restores the prior shape and connector route, and redo reapplies the change with the connector route updated accordingly.
uncertainty: The supplied changes contain no removed code, so the previous behavior is unavailable and no concrete input known to behave differently before and after this change can be identified.
For rotated shapes, the new drag hit test includes the axis-aligned bounding box, which can extend beyond the visible outline; confirm whether binding from those blank corner areas is intended.
The supplied changes add the routing implementation without showing its prior version, so there is no evidence to identify a specific input that followed a different old routing path.
A single bound elbow arrow is explicitly prevented from moving by dragging and from resizing, but the supplied context does not establish whether that restriction is intended product behavior.

The supplied before-and-after evidence does not establish which target wins when shapes overlap during endpoint binding, or which shape sizes would make the old variable-width highlight differ from 10 units.
The supplied context does not identify a navigation path or visible control for choosing elbow-arrow style, so the exact steps to access that option are unknown.

report.summary: The release improves canvas selection and drawing interactions, adding lasso tools and more accurate shape-aware behavior.
keyChanges: Lasso and frame-intersection checks now use geometry based on each object’s shape, including sampled curves and a closed 90-segment ellipse outline instead of the previous straight-line approximations; curved and rotated objects may therefore be selected or associated with frames differently.
Lasso selection now normalizes attached text to its container and removes frame children when the frame itself is selected, while line intersections allow a tolerance of 1 scene unit.
Lasso previews now use an animated, dashed violet outline with a translucent fill, and lasso trails are cleared when the gesture ends; very short paths may not produce a visible preview.
Starting a new trail update now clears previously completed trails, so verify temporary laser-pointer marks disappear as expected after a stroke ends.
New shapes no longer resize from their center, even when the pointer event previously triggered center-based resizing. Lasso-tool activation can also preserve the current selection when requested.
Tracing a lasso around or across visible elements updates the selection; a regular lasso clears the previous selection, while holding Shift keeps it.
Holding Alt while dragging a selection marquee now changes that gesture into a lasso, and releasing the pointer clears the temporary trail while retaining the resulting selection.
Restored editor state now recognizes lasso as a valid active tool, so a saved drawing configured with lasso should restore without treating that tool as invalid.

Line-segment intersection now accepts an optional tolerance: points must be less than the supplied threshold from a segment to count; existing in-app callers omit it and continue using the default tolerance.
The editor now offers lasso selection through the tool controls and command palette; when the selection tool is active, clicking its control switches to lasso, and clicking again switches back.
With lasso active, releasing Space now follows the selection-tool cursor path instead of clearing the current selection; selection actions are hidden when nothing is selected.
Canvas-panning and deep-selection hints now use list formatting that removes a terminal period from each hint; the embed icon’s stroke width also increases from 1.25 to 1.5.
A new lasso selection tool can select drawing elements that its path encloses or intersects; activating it clears the current selection, and activating it again returns to the regular selection tool.
qaChecks: Verify that a closed lasso around only the upper-right curved rim of an ellipse, excluding its center, selects the ellipse.
Check that a lasso edge passing within 1 scene unit of an object boundary still selects that object.
Confirm that lassoing attached text selects its container, and that selecting a frame does not leave its frame contents separately selected.

Test frame membership with a rotated rounded rectangle partly crossing the frame boundary; verify that its visible outline, rather than a straight bounding-box approximation, determines the intersection.
Verify a brief lasso gesture around an element, producing fewer than 12 outline points, still selects the enclosed element even if its animated preview is not visible.
Check that a completed lasso gesture clears its trail and leaves the resulting selection visible.
Confirm a completed temporary laser-pointer stroke disappears rather than remaining as a completed trail; repeat with a collaborator’s pointer if available.
Test dragging a new shape while holding the input that previously caused center-based resizing; confirm the shape starts at the pointer-down position and does not expand symmetrically around it.

Verify that, starting a selection drag on blank canvas and holding Alt before moving around two visible elements, the gesture changes from a rectangular marquee to a freehand lasso and selects elements enclosed or crossed by the path.
Check that an Alt-drag lasso without Shift clears the earlier selection, while the same gesture started with Shift held preserves the earlier selection as the traced elements are selected.
Confirm that releasing the pointer removes the temporary lasso trail but leaves the resulting selection in place.
Verify that restoring the saved state recognizes lasso as the active tool.
Verify that with the selection tool active, clicking its toolbar control switches to lasso, and clicking it again returns to selection.
Check that the lasso tool can also be found and activated from the command palette.
Confirm that with lasso active and an element selected, holding and releasing Space restores the cursor without clearing the selection.
Ensure that with lasso active and no elements selected, selection actions are not shown.
Verify that the canvas-panning hint appears without its terminal period and remains readable.
Verify that activating lasso selection while an element is selected clears the selection and changes the pointer to a crosshair; activate it again and confirm the regular selection tool returns.
Check a lasso path that fully encloses the rectangle and crosses the separate line without enclosing it; confirm both elements are selected.
uncertainty: The supplied evidence has no previous implementation for the new lasso-selection routines, so their exact before-and-after behavior cannot be established; the lasso checks focus on the geometry differences shown in the previous outline calculation.
The supplied context does not identify the exact center-resize key or modifier, and does not establish whether a lasso preview shorter than 12 outline points is intended to be invisible.

The supplied context gives no navigation path or visible control label for activating the dedicated lasso tool; the Alt-drag route is the only lasso entry point that can be described from the evidence.

No supplied in-app caller passes the new intersection tolerance, so no manual UI input is established that exercises its changed boundary; with a supplied threshold, a point exactly that far from the segment remains excluded.
The supplied changes show how to activate lasso but do not establish what canvas gesture should select elements; verify the expected gesture against product requirements.
Lasso selection is new, so the supplied evidence establishes no concrete input that had prior lasso behavior to compare with, and does not establish how users navigate to the tool.

report.summary: Selection and canvas interactions now adapt to device type and consistently follow the chosen tool.
keyChanges: On mobile or tablet, lasso selection now selects an unselected object immediately when touched and can allow dragging it in the same gesture; frame and frame-content selection remain mutually exclusive.

Desktop lasso gestures now avoid starting a selection trail on already-selected objects and block dragging while drawing a lasso, but allow dragging selected objects on a later pointer gesture; Ctrl+Alt selection now starts lasso selection and closes the element-link dialog if it is open.

After pasting or inserting drawing items, finishing text or drawing, and relevant pointer interactions, the editor returns to its device-specific default tool; touch context menus and double-clicks are also accepted when that default is lasso.
When lasso is the configured default selection tool, it takes the primary toolbar selection slot, its separate menu entry is hidden, and its shortcuts follow that configuration.
Exiting the laser tool, unlocking a tool, and finishing a paste now return to the configured selection tool; the empty-drawing welcome screen also recognizes that default.
On mobile and tablet, pasted drawing content is placed in the center rather than at the pointer, and lasso mode no longer shows a move cursor over an unselected object.

When a saved drawing opens, an active selection, lasso, or image tool is replaced with the device’s default selection tool; for example, a mobile drawing saved with standard selection now opens in lasso mode.
If image insertion is cancelled, the editor returns to the device’s default selection tool rather than always returning to standard selection.

When the configured default selection tool is lasso, clearing the canvas from the image tool, leaving the eraser without a remembered prior tool, deleting or cutting a selection, and finishing an editing action now return to lasso instead of standard selection.
The lasso selection action is unavailable when lasso is already the configured default selection tool.
Snapping, previously disabled whenever lasso was active, is now enabled while selected elements are being dragged with lasso; it remains disabled during lasso selection itself.
iPad and iPhone platform detection now ignores letter case, and mobile-device classification covers additional user-agent and platform names.

report.summary: The release overhauls text-to-diagram creation, combining improved chat management and generation with updated diagram previews and error handling.
keyChanges: Shared filled actions now honor an explicit disabled state as well as loading and success states, so actions marked unavailable cannot be activated.

Text-to-diagram chat accepts prompts, submits trimmed text with Enter, uses Shift+Enter for a newline, and clears the prompt after submission; the send control is enabled only when the trimmed prompt is longer than 3 characters and quota remains.

Chat history, message errors, and generated previews have controls for restoring or deleting chats, retrying eligible network failures after 5 seconds, viewing a response as Mermaid, and inserting a preview.
Mermaid errors now appear in a dedicated error state with the preview hidden instead of dimmed; when error details are hidden, the message is replaced with a translated syntax-error message.
Workflow panels now support multiple button, link, and informational actions; actions are disabled while text submission is in progress.
Chat history is saved locally, ordered by update time and limited to 10 conversations; saved titles are trimmed and titles longer than 50 characters become the first 47 characters plus three periods.
Text-to-diagram chats can be started, restored, and deleted; deleting the active chat loads the first remaining saved chat, or resets to an empty chat when none remain.
Restoring a chat converts its message timestamps to dates and restores its last assistant message’s error state.
Mermaid previews are scheduled during generation, pending content is flushed when generation ends, and preview visibility follows whether the chat has assistant messages.
Chats are saved when generation is not active; the saved list is sorted by recency and limited to 10 chats.

Text-to-diagram generation now sends chat messages to a streaming response instead of submitting one prompt for a single JSON result, so follow-up prompts can use chat history and generated content is assembled from streamed chunks.
Mermaid preview now rejects text with mismatched brackets, braces, or parentheses, or an unfinished operator at the end of the last line, until the syntax is completed.
Text-to-diagram conversion now returns parsing and rendering failures for the interface to display, and no longer rejects a preview solely because converting its canvas to a blob fails.
Generated diagram previews now choose dark-mode export using the editor’s current theme rather than checking a page theme class.
The command palette’s history symbol and the code-font symbol have updated designs.
Prompts from 3 through 10,000 characters can proceed to generation; shorter or longer prompts are rejected, and generation is also blocked when no requests remain.

Generated replies stream into the chat and are parsed as Mermaid diagrams; network, rate-limit, and parse failures are reported in the chat, with structured error messages shown in a readable form when possible.
Generation can be cancelled, and a retry after a network error clears that error while retrying the existing assistant reply.
The chat logic represented here selects the latest assistant reply for conversation and preview handling, and prepares only non-empty user and assistant messages for generation.
Text-to-diagram now brings chat generation, retry, repair, message deletion, Mermaid viewing, and diagram insertion into the dialog’s chat workflow.
Mermaid conversion now updates its preview only while the Mermaid tab is active and renders using the current theme; the dialog width changes from 1200 to 1520.
Chat responses are converted before insertion, and a diagram is added to the drawing only when conversion succeeds.

report.summary: The release updates flowchart editing, including keyboard navigation and connected-node placement, though some behavior changes remain unconfirmed.
keyChanges: Ctrl/Cmd+arrow previews flowchart nodes, releasing Ctrl/Cmd commits them and selects the first node, Escape cancels creation, and Alt+arrow navigates linked nodes; hidden nodes are brought into view when needed.

When creating flowchart nodes, placement now accounts for obstacles among elbow-arrow-connected elements and keeps at least one gap of clearance; existing drawings may place new nodes in a different, unoccupied position than before.
Directional keyboard navigation now finds linked nodes using the direction of their elbow-arrow attachment point, so verify that moving through connected nodes follows the expected direction.

New flowchart nodes are placed as a cluster using obstacles from the whole connected flowchart, rather than positioning each new node from only its immediate neighbors; placements keep a 100-unit gap along the creation direction and seek the nearest clear cross-axis space.

When a pending cluster grows, its existing nodes are intended to keep their positions when the larger cluster still fits; the previous direction fallback of “right” for unrecognized keys is removed, and the initial direction is now unset.

Flowchart creation status and pending nodes are now managed through a dedicated editor component; rendering and the undo/redo guard read the same underlying flowchart-creation state, so no behavior change is evident.
qaChecks: Verify Ctrl/Cmd+ArrowUp on a selected flowchart node previews a node above it, then release Ctrl/Cmd and confirm the node is added and selected.
Check Alt+ArrowRight from a node with a linked node to its right; confirm the linked node becomes selected, then release Alt and confirm navigation ends.
Test Ctrl/Cmd+ArrowRight to start node creation, then press Escape; confirm the pending creation is canceled and no pending node is committed.
Confirm a generated or navigated-to node outside the visible canvas is brought into view.
Verify that pressing Ctrl or Cmd with the right arrow to create a node places it clear of the connected node, with at least one gap of clearance, rather than overlapping the occupied area.
Check that creating nodes in a different direction after starting a flowchart uses that direction's placement and does not carry over the previous direction's alignment.
Confirm that pressing Alt with an arrow key navigates to a linked node whose elbow-arrow attachment point is in that direction; repeat with up, down, left, and right.

Verify adding a node beside a flowchart when a non-immediate connected node already occupies its placement band puts the new node in a clear cross-axis slot, without overlap, while retaining the 100-unit creation-direction gap from its parent.
Check expanding a visible pending cluster by one node; when the enlarged cluster fits in its anchored space, confirm the previously visible nodes stay in place.
Test directional keyboard navigation on a flowchart with linked nodes in different directions and confirm the corresponding linked node remains reachable.
Verify keyboard-driven flowchart creation and navigation still work, and pending flowchart nodes are shown in the editor.
Check Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl/Cmd+Y during flowchart creation; confirm history changes do not apply while creation is in progress and can apply after it ends.
uncertainty: The supplied diffs move existing shortcut logic into a shared handler but establish no concrete input handled differently before and after, so a regression-triggering input cannot be isolated.

The supplied evidence does not show the previous implementation of directional navigation, so it does not establish a specific input that behaved differently before; verify the directional checks against expected editor behavior.

The prior behavior used “right” for unrecognized keys, but the supplied evidence does not show what replaces that fallback or fully establish how directional navigation is handled now; confirm the expected result for a non-arrow key when no direction is set.
The supplied before-and-after code shows no input that behaves differently; it does not establish whether the reorganization changes any user-visible behavior.

report.summary: The release improves how drawings are created, organized, and displayed within frames.
keyChanges: Opaque fills now affect interior hit testing and overlapping-object searches only for element types that support background fills, changing which objects can be selected, erased, or targeted by arrows.
Frame highlighting now recognizes rectangle, diamond, ellipse, arrow, line, freehand, text, image, frame, and embeddable tools, and clears when selection is dismissed or an action is finalized.
Browsers that lack newer array capabilities now receive compatibility support so the editor can use them.
When a mixed selection is added to a frame, elements already in that frame now move together with newly added elements, just below the frame or after its highest child; attached text is included.
A single inserted element now goes to the end of the drawing order even when it is assigned to a frame, rather than being placed just before that frame.

When creating or dragging objects over overlapping content, frame membership now considers the top object under the pointer, selected objects, and existing frame membership rather than simply choosing the top overlapping frame.
New text placement skips frame outlines when finding a text container, prioritizes that container, and assigns frame membership only when the container belongs to the frame.
Library items duplicated with frame-order preservation retain their saved frame and child order; inserting new objects also updates frame highlighting, and switching tools clears it.
Added elements are now inserted alongside their frame’s children rather than simply at the end of the drawing, affecting pasted text, images, embedded content, and other new elements.
Pasted drawings and dropped Library items now preserve the order of children inside frames; verify their stacking order when adding a drawing that contains a frame.
Canvas rendering now accounts for element stacking, selection dragging, and frame highlighting; pointer movement updates frame highlights when appropriate.

The static and interactive canvases now use a canvas-specific change marker instead of the scene change marker to decide when to refresh; the supplied resize-call changes show no altered resizing rule.
When selected elements are dragged over a different highlighted frame, their temporary render order now places them with that frame’s children; verify the order during the drag and after it ends.
For an in-progress element assigned to a frame, changes to its version now invalidate the render cache, allowing its preview to refresh even when its identity stays the same.
Rendering and cleanup were reorganized without another evidenced user-visible behavior change.
New freehand marks, lines, embeds, flowchart nodes, and frames use the editor’s shared insertion path; check that creation still works and associated frames are highlighted where applicable.

When selected objects are dropped over a frame, destination handling now considers the selection’s shared frame and excludes the selected objects when finding a destination; objects already in that frame are no longer filtered out solely because they already belong to it.
Library items are duplicated with frame-child order preserved, so inserted items should retain the saved order of objects inside their frames.
qaChecks: Verify clicking the interior of the closed freehand drawing with its opaque red background does not select it as a filled area, while its outline remains selectable.
Check that an arrow endpoint placed over both overlapping objects can bind to the smaller underlying object instead of the top object’s opaque background stopping the search.
Verify moving the pointer over the frame highlights it with the rectangle and arrow tools active.
Confirm the frame highlight clears after dismissing the selection and after finalizing a canvas action.
Verify the editor opens and drawing and editing remain available in that browser environment.
Verify adding the existing frame child and the unframed element to the same frame keeps them together in the frame’s element order, with attached text still alongside its element.
Check inserting one element assigned to the frame while unrelated elements follow the frame places the new element at the end of the drawing order and leaves it visible in the drawing.
Verify that creating a new shape at the overlap point does not add it to the frame contents when the unframed foreground shape is the top object under the pointer.
Check that changing tools clears the current frame highlight, and that creating an object inside a frame highlights that object’s frame.
Verify that inserting the item retains the saved frame-before-children order and keeps the child objects associated with the frame.
Verify that double-clicking the overlap creates text bound to the underlying shape and does not make the text part of the frame.
Verify pasting a copied drawing containing a frame with multiple children preserves the children’s relative stacking order.
Check pasting two lines of text with the pointer inside a frame that already has two children places the text with the frame’s contents and leaves the existing children in order.
Confirm adding images and a supported embeddable link inside a frame keeps frame contents in order and leaves the new items visible.

Verify a shape drawn beneath a higher-stacked existing shape previews in the correct stacking position; with the rectangle tool active, move the pointer into a frame and then over a scrollbar to confirm the frame highlight appears and clears, and does not reset while drawing or dragging.
Verify that after changing the selected shape’s dimensions in the Stats panel, the canvas shows the updated shape rather than a stale drawing.
Check that selecting and editing a shape updates both its visible selection feedback and the drawing.

Verify that while dragging the separate selected element over the frame, it renders in order with the frame’s children, and that ending or cancelling the drag does not permanently reorder the drawing.

Check an in-progress element assigned to a frame: keep the same element and change its geometry so its version changes; confirm the visible preview updates to the new geometry rather than remaining stale.
Confirm that an in-progress element assigned to a frame renders in the frame context as it is created or adjusted.
Verify creating a freehand mark or line inside a frame highlights the associated frame and leaves the new object in that frame’s contents.
Check the boundary case by selecting objects already in a frame and dropping them over that same frame; confirm they remain associated with the frame and are not lost from its contents.
Confirm completing a flowchart with pending nodes inserts the nodes into the drawing.
Verify inserting that Library item preserves the saved order of the frame’s children.
uncertainty: The supplied evidence does not show whether removing arguments from frame wrapping and ungrouping changes how those actions update frame membership.

The new single-element insertion places frame-assigned elements at the end of drawing order, while frame additions use a position relative to the frame or its highest child; the supplied context does not establish the intended visible stacking in every case.

The intended product rule for placing a new object where an unframed foreground object overlaps a frame is not documented; the updated behavior leaves the new object outside that frame, so confirm that this membership is expected.
The evidence does not show what user action changes the new canvas marker independently of the old scene marker, so a specific regression-triggering input cannot be identified.

report.summary: The release updates application startup and server behavior, along with how JSON data, identifiers, and nested requests are handled.
keyChanges: When the requested .json database file is missing, startup now creates it with default data before loading it; verify startup with that exact missing-file condition.
Router setup errors are now printed in red and terminate startup with exit code 1 instead of escaping as an uncaught error.
Watch mode now monitors the source and routes directories with native filesystem events rather than the previous watcher, so verify reloads after files are replaced as well as edited.
Creating and updating resources no longer convert submitted fields to native values, so numeric-looking text such as "0" is passed through differently.
Resource lookup and deletion now use the path identifier as text instead of converting it first; compatibility with numeric stored IDs needs verification.
Collection filters now skip records when the filtered field is falsy, recognize operators such as _ne only at the end of a query key, and compare truthy stored values as text.
The command-line launcher now starts a packaged CLI entry point instead of the source CLI entry point.

Default server middleware no longer includes request-body parsing or method override; request parsing is now exposed separately, while the database router installs its own parsing and method-override middleware.
The database state is now validated when the router starts, before database routes are set up.

New records in a non-empty collection with a non-numeric highest ID now receive an ID from a short-ID generator instead of the previous UUID generator; empty collections still start at 1 and finite numeric IDs still increment.
Nested-resource GET and POST requests now keep parent IDs as text instead of converting values such as 0 to numbers or true to booleans, which may change downstream matching.
New data validation rejects non-plain top-level values and top-level property names containing /; the removed CLI .json detection helper leaves CLI classification behavior unclear.
Invoking the new entry point now calls the existing command-line interface; the remaining edits only change declaration syntax and do not alter runtime behavior.
qaChecks: Verify startup with the requested .json file absent: the CLI creates the file with default data and continues loading the database.
Check the router setup error case: startup prints the error and exits with status 1.
Verify that replacing the watched database file through an atomic rename reloads the server and that changing the watched routes file reloads it.
Check that changing an unrelated file in either watched directory does not report a reload for the configured source or routes file.
Verify the list query score=0 returns the record with score 0; this input matched before the new falsy-value check.
Confirm the list query code=2 matches the record whose code is stored as text "2".

Check status_ne_suffix=active against the record with status_ne_suffix set to "inactive"; the new suffix-only rule should treat this as equality and return no match, unlike the former substring-based inequality handling.
Verify creating and updating with count: "0" preserves the submitted text value rather than applying the former native-value conversion.
Check that the path identifier "1" still retrieves and deletes the resource stored with numeric ID 1.
Verify the existing command-line invocation starts without an error.
Verify a POST with content type application/json and body {"name":"case"} is not automatically parsed with defaults alone, but is available as a parsed body when the separate body parser is added.
Check that creating a record in that collection assigns a generated short-scheme ID rather than the previous UUID-style ID.
Verify nested GET and POST requests using parent ID 0 pass the parent ID as the string "0" and still process the requested nested collection.
Check that an object with the top-level property "team/member" is rejected with an error explaining that / in a property name is unsupported.
Confirm that an array value such as [] is rejected because the data must be an object.
Verify that invoking the new entry point with a valid source-file argument runs the command-line interface.
uncertainty: Native filesystem event delivery for atomic file replacement can vary by operating system, so confirm the watch-mode replacement check on each supported platform.
The evidence does not establish whether a text path ID still matches a numeric stored ID, and it supplies no CLI invocation or behavior contract, so compatibility for those cases remains unconfirmed.
The validation rules for initial database contents are not supplied, so a specific invalid dataset and its expected rejection cannot be identified.

The removed CLI JSON-detection helper previously accepted non-URL names ending in .json and excluded URLs ending in .json, but no caller or application surface is supplied to establish the new CLI behavior or a reliable check outcome.
Application context and prior entry-point behavior were not supplied, so the expected visible result after the CLI starts and any further navigation are unknown.
